datetimeconverter.name: datetimeconverter
datetimeconverter.core_method: Data wrangling, not statistics: lubridate parsing of date-time text, Excel serials (1900/1904) and Unix epochs with format auto-detection and two-digit-year rules, timezone handling, then component extraction (year, month, weekday, week, quarter, day of year) written back as Output columns, plus parse-quality tables
needs: zoneinfo + tzdata (absent from the trimmed bundled stdlib; the free-text timezone option needs it)
datetimeconverter.oracle: lubridate::ymd_hms / dmy_hms / mdy_hms and date-only variants, lubridate::with_tz, lubridate::force_tz, lubridate::week, lubridate::quarter, lubridate::yday
datetimeconverter.gain: none; ClinicoPathPj also has no Output (computed-column) option type yet

lassocox.name: lassocox
lassocox.core_method: Cross-validated LASSO Cox (glmnet::cv.glmnet family='cox', lambda.min or lambda.1se, seeded folds), selected-coefficient/HR table, Harrell C (survival::concordance), cox.zph on the refit, linear-predictor risk groups with KM; CV/path/coefficient/survival plots
needs: scikit-survival (CoxnetSurvivalAnalysis), or an own coordinate-descent Cox-lasso path
lassocox.gain: none; glmnet is the reference, and fold assignment from R's RNG cannot be reproduced (parity needs an explicit foldid)

multisurvival.name: multisurvival
multisurvival.core_method: Multivariable Cox PH (coxph, Efron ties, interactions, strata, landmark), finalfit HR tables, cox.zph, KM and adjusted curves, risk-score groups, bootstrap optimism-corrected C, riskRegression::Score time-dependent AUC/Brier, rms::cph nomogram, Fine-Gray via survival::finegray, person-time rates, AIC/LR/drop1 model comparison
multisurvival.oracle: survival::coxph, survival::cox.zph, survival::finegray, finalfit::finalfit, rms::cph, rms::nomogram, riskRegression::Score, survminer::ggadjustedcurves
multisurvival.gain: none; survival, rms and riskRegression are the reference implementations

oddsratio.name: oddsratio
oddsratio.core_method: Binary logistic regression OR table via finalfit (univariable + multivariable glm, profile-likelihood CIs, AIC/C-statistic/H&L metrics), optional Firth penalized logistic (logistf), 2x2 diagnostic metrics for one predictor (sens/spec with Clopper-Pearson, LR+/LR- by the Simel log method, as epiR::epi.tests), forest plot and rms::lrm nomogram
oddsratio.oracle: stats::glm(family = binomial) with stats::confint (profile), finalfit::finalfit(metrics = TRUE), logistf::logistf, epiR::epi.tests, rms::lrm
oddsratio.gain: drops finalfit/logistf/epiR from the table path; the forest plot and nomogram still need R drawing

outcomeorganizer.name: outcomeorganizer
outcomeorganizer.core_method: Data recoding: derives event indicators for overall, cause-specific, competing-risk, progression-free and multistate analyses from outcome/recurrence levels, with an event-priority hierarchy and interval/administrative censoring; writes Output columns and frequency/diagnostic tables
outcomeorganizer.oracle: no statistical oracle; the recoding rules in R/outcomeorganizer.b.R
outcomeorganizer.gain: none; ClinicoPathPj has no Output option type yet

singlearm.name: singlearm
singlearm.core_method: Single-cohort Kaplan-Meier: median survival with CI, survival at user cut points (Greenwood, survfit 'log' CI), reverse-KM follow-up, person-time incidence rates with exact Poisson CIs, competing-risk cumulative incidence (cmprsk::cuminc), Nelson-Aalen baseline hazard, landmark and date-derived follow-up; KM/cumulative-event/cumulative-hazard/KMunicate plots
singlearm.oracle: survival::survfit + summary.survfit(times =) and its median/0.95LCL/0.95UCL table, cmprsk::cuminc, survival::basehaz, exact Poisson limits via stats::qchisq
singlearm.gain: none, since R survival is the reference. Porting note: scipy.stats.ecdf offers only 'linear'/'log-log' CIs, so survfit's default 'log' CI and its median-CI rule need own code

survival.name: survival
survival.core_method: Univariable time-to-event comparison: KM by group, log-rank and Fleming-Harrington weighted log-rank (survdiff rho), pairwise tests with p-adjust, Cox HR (coxph Efron) with cox.zph, stratified and age-adjusted Cox (including age as time scale), RMST (survfit rmean), person-time rates, adjusted curves, flexsurv parametric fits, calibration, restricted cubic splines; many plots
survival.oracle: survival::survfit, survival::survdiff(rho =), survminer::pairwise_survdiff, survival::coxph, survival::cox.zph, summary(survfit, rmean =), flexsurv::flexsurvreg
survival.gain: none. A core of KM + k-group log-rank + univariable Efron Cox is an implementable (M) subset, but scipy.stats.logrank is two-sample only, with no weights or strata

survivalcont.name: survivalcont
survivalcont.core_method: Continuous-predictor survival: Cox HR per unit, optimal cut-off by maximally selected log-rank statistic (survminer::surv_cutpoint / maxstat), multiple cut-offs (quantile, recursive maxstat, rpart survival tree, min-p), KM/log-rank of the derived groups, RMST, stratified Cox, cox.zph, residual diagnostics
survivalcont.oracle: survival::coxph, survminer::surv_cutpoint, maxstat::maxstat.test(smethod = 'LogRank'), rpart::rpart(method = 'exp'), survival::survdiff, survival::cox.zph
survivalcont.gain: a numpy-vectorised permutation p-value for the selected cut-off, which the R version explicitly does not report (R could also add it via maxstat pmethod = 'condMC'); otherwise none

timeinterval.name: timeinterval
timeinterval.core_method: Date arithmetic: parses start/end dates (lubridate formats), computes intervals in days/weeks/months/years on a calendar or average-length basis, landmark subsetting, negative/extreme flags, summary (mean with t CI, median, IQR) and person-time totals; writes an Output column
timeinterval.gain: none; it needs an Output option type that the bridge lacks

aalenhazard.name: aalenhazard
aalenhazard.core_method: Aalen additive hazards regression (timereg::aalen, robust SEs) with cumulative regression functions B(t); semiparametric McKeague-Sasieni constant effects via const(). The constant-effect tests are never computed: n.sim = 0, and timereg::const() (a formula marker) is applied to the fitted model as if it were a test
aalenhazard.oracle: timereg::aalen (robust = 1; n.sim > 0 for the tests), survival::aareg
aalenhazard.gain: real Gaussian-multiplier resampling tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov / Cramer-von Mises) of time-varying effects, vectorised in numpy; the R version currently reports none

adaptivelasso.name: adaptivelasso
adaptivelasso.core_method: Adaptive LASSO Cox: initial ridge/Cox/univariate weights, then a glmnet Cox path with penalty.factor (optional strata via stratifySurv), CV lambda, bootstrap stability selection, cox.zph, baseline survival, risk groups; optional parallel CV
adaptivelasso.oracle: glmnet::cv.glmnet(family = 'cox', penalty.factor =), glmnet::glmnet, glmnet::stratifySurv, survival::coxph, survival::cox.zph, survival::basehaz

advancedSurvivalPower.name: advancedSurvivalPower
advancedSurvivalPower.core_method: Two-group survival power and sample size by Freedman's formula (powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default). The 'complex' design turns median survival, accrual, follow-up and loss into an event probability under exponential assumptions. Both arms get the same event probability (pE = pC) even though HR != 1
advancedSurvivalPower.gain: drops powerSurvEpi; adds a fast numpy Monte-Carlo check of the approximation (simulated exponential arms + scipy.stats.logrank) and instant power-curve data. The generator needs List option support first

advancedtrials.name: advancedtrials
advancedtrials.core_method: Group-sequential boundaries from gsDesign::gsDesign (test.type 1 or 4; Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming/Pocock, Hwang-Shih-DeCani, power spending) with a Schoenfeld event count. Calendar time (fixed 0.1/month event rate), conditional power, operating characteristics and all adaptive/platform/biomarker outputs are placeholders
advancedtrials.oracle: gsDesign::gsDesign, gsDesign::gsProbability, gsDesign::sfLDOF, gsDesign::sfLDPocock, gsDesign::sfHSD, gsDesign::sfPower, gsDesign::gsCP
advancedtrials.gain: real conditional/predictive power and numpy-simulated operating characteristics in place of the placeholders; drops gsDesign (boundaries need Jennison-Turnbull grid recursion)

alluvialSurvival.name: alluvialSurvival
alluvialSurvival.core_method: plot only: ggalluvial treatment-pathway alluvial diagram plus survminer KM curves
alluvialSurvival.gain: none until plots exist (a D3 alluvial would be the only route)

causespecifichazards.name: causespecifichazards
causespecifichazards.core_method: Cause-specific hazards: one coxph per cause with the other causes censored (or Weibull/exponential/lognormal survreg AFT), cmprsk::cuminc CIF at event-time quartiles with Wald CIs (nearest-time lookup), cox.zph. Model comparison and all plots are placeholders

classicalSurvivalPower.name: classicalSurvivalPower
classicalSurvivalPower.core_method: Lachin-Foulkes sample size and power with uniform or exponential entry and dropout (gsDesign::nSurvival), Schoenfeld event count (gsDesign::nEvents), detectable HR (gsDesign::zn2hr)
classicalSurvivalPower.gain: drops gsDesign; instant power-curve and timeline data. The generator needs List/String option support first

comparingSurvival.name: comparingSurvival
comparingSurvival.core_method: KM medians by group, k-sample log-rank (survdiff), pairwise log-rank with p-value correction, a trend test as the Wald test of coxph on integer group scores, landmark re-origin; ggfortify KM plot
comparingSurvival.gain: none; it duplicates the shipped survival analysis

competingRisksPower.name: competingRisksPower
competingRisksPower.core_method: stub/placeholder: power and sample size come from an invented heuristic (0.80 x sqrt(n/200) x |log HR|/log 1.5 x event and 'competing penalty' factors, clamped to 0.05-0.99). No Gray-test or Fine-Gray formula is used, and the power 'CI' is a fixed +/- z x 0.02
competingRisksPower.oracle: no R function in this code. Validate against the closed forms of Latouche, Porcher & Chevret (2004) and Pintilie (2002) using their worked examples, with a Monte-Carlo cross-check by cmprsk::cuminc (Gray test) / cmprsk::crr
competingRisksPower.gain: replaces a fabricated formula with the published Fine-Gray/Gray-test sample-size formulas plus fast numpy Monte-Carlo power (this is equally fixable in R)

competingsurvival.name: competingsurvival
competingsurvival.core_method: Overall (KM), cause-specific (KM with competing events censored) and competing-risk cumulative incidence (cmprsk::cuminc) with Gray's test, Fine-Gray subdistribution regression (cmprsk::crr via finalfit::crrmulti), CIF at time points; stacked and KM-vs-CIF plots
competingsurvival.gain: none. The CIF + Gray-test part alone is implementable (M); the hard part is crr with its censoring-adjusted sandwich variance

comprehensiveSurvivalPower.name: comprehensiveSurvivalPower
comprehensiveSurvivalPower.core_method: Partial stub. Real: Schoenfeld log-rank events and Lachin-Foulkes (gsDesign::nSurvival/nEvents), group-sequential via gsDesign::gsDesign/gsProbability, and a Gray-test sample size from a 'simplified' binomial-variance approximation. Cox, weighted log-rank, subdistribution, cause-specific, RMST, non-inferiority, SNP and Bayesian methods return notes only
comprehensiveSurvivalPower.oracle: gsDesign::nSurvival, gsDesign::nEvents, gsDesign::gsDesign, gsDesign::gsProbability; for the placeholder methods, Monte-Carlo with survival::survdiff / survRM2::rmst2
comprehensiveSurvivalPower.gain: real closed-form or numpy Monte-Carlo power for the eight placeholder methods; drops gsDesign

conditionalgee.name: conditionalgee
conditionalgee.core_method: GEE (geepack::geeglm) on recurrent-event gap times with previous-gap / cumulative-history / event-order conditioning terms. The 'exponential', 'Weibull' and 'lognormal' choices all fit a gaussian family (gamma uses Gamma). Censored final gaps are modelled as if observed. Diagnostics, predictions and residual/prediction plots are placeholders (rnorm)
conditionalgee.gain: none; fix the family mislabelling and the ignored censoring in R first

conditionalinference.name: conditionalinference
conditionalinference.core_method: Conditional inference survival tree (party::ctree with log-rank scores; quadratic/max test statistics, Bonferroni/univariate/Monte-Carlo test types; mincriterion/minsplit/minbucket/maxdepth), terminal-node KM curves, variable importance

conditionalsurvival.name: conditionalsurvival
conditionalsurvival.core_method: Conditional survival S(t | s) = S(t)/S(s) from Kaplan-Meier with delta-method CIs (Greenwood over (s, t]), landmark KM re-origin, and a 'simplified' IPW variant; presmoothed KM falls back to plain KM
conditionalsurvival.oracle: survival::survfit + summary.survfit(times =) for the ratio and Greenwood terms; condSURV::survCOND for the KMW/presmoothed estimators
conditionalsurvival.gain: instant conditional-survival grids over many (s, t) pairs; otherwise minor

continuousmarkov.name: continuousmarkov
continuousmarkov.core_method: Continuous-time Markov multistate model for panel data (msm::msm, BFGS) with covariates on log intensities, and P(t) via msm::pmatrix.msm. Three tables are wrong or fabricated: the sojourn table divides by the Q row sum, which is 0 for a generator (correct is -1/q_ii); the covariate-effects row is hard-coded (coef 0, HR 1, p 1); prevalence is an invented formula (0.2 + 0.1*state + 0.05*t)
continuousmarkov.gain: none specific to Python; the fabricated tables are cheaper to fix in R with sojourn.msm / hazard.msm / prevalence.msm

coxdiagnostics.name: coxdiagnostics
coxdiagnostics.core_method: plot-first: survminer::ggcoxdiagnostics martingale/deviance/score/Schoenfeld/dfbeta residual plots and ggcoxzph for a coxph fit, plus a cox.zph PH-test table, model summary and car::vif

datevalidator.name: datevalidator
datevalidator.core_method: Data cleaning: validates and repairs messy date strings (datefixR::fix_date_char with day/month imputation, anytime::anytime, lubridate::parse_date_time), Excel serial handling, format-pattern and quality tables
needs: zoneinfo + tzdata (absent from the trimmed bundled stdlib) for the output-timezone option

directbinomial.name: directbinomial
directbinomial.core_method: Direct binomial regression for the cumulative incidence with an additive link (timereg::comp.risk, model = 'additive', time-varying coefficients). The covariate-effects table is always empty, the goodness-of-fit row is hard-coded (statistic 1.25, p 0.284), and the residual plot is rnorm noise
directbinomial.gain: none; the hard-coded GOF row should be removed or replaced in R

emfrailty.name: emfrailty
emfrailty.core_method: Partial stub: every frailty distribution and EM variant fits the same shared gamma-frailty Cox by penalized partial likelihood (survival::coxph + frailty(id)). Empirical-Bayes frailty predictions and shrinkage are random draws (rnorm/runif)
emfrailty.gain: a genuine gamma-frailty EM with real empirical-Bayes frailties is implementable (M) and would deliver what the title promises; lognormal, inverse-Gaussian and stable frailties are what make the full scope hard

epidemiosurvival.name: epidemiosurvival
epidemiosurvival.core_method: Mostly stub. Real parts: KM by exposure, weighted coxph HR, exact Poisson rate CIs (epitools::pois.exact), a rate ratio (epitools::rateratio fed events and person-time minus events), and Levin PAR with a bootstrap CI. Case-cohort variances return constants (1.0/1.2). Life tables, age standardisation, APC, competing mortality, trends, excess mortality and four plots are not implemented
epidemiosurvival.oracle: epitools::pois.exact, epitools::rateratio, epitools::ageadjust.direct, epitools::ageadjust.indirect, survival::survfit, survival::coxph(weights =); survival::cch for case-cohort
epidemiosurvival.gain: real exact rate ratios, SMR, direct/indirect standardisation and life tables in place of the placeholders; case-cohort Cox (survival::cch) stays hard

extratrees.name: extratrees
extratrees.core_method: Extremely randomized survival forest (ranger::ranger, splitrule = 'extratrees') with permutation importance. The importance, OOB-error, survival and partial-dependence plots are placeholders (runif/rnorm/sin)
extratrees.gain: none; forests are seed-specific, so there can be no numeric parity with ranger

finegray.name: finegray
finegray.core_method: Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard regression (cmprsk::crr) with an sHR table, Gray's test and CIFs by group (cmprsk::cuminc), and predicted CIF for a covariate pattern

firthregression.name: firthregression
firthregression.core_method: Firth penalized likelihood for logistic regression (logistf: profile penalized-likelihood CIs, penalized LR tests) and Cox regression (coxphf: Breslow ties, profile CIs), compared with glm/coxph; separation check
firthregression.gain: drops logistf/coxphf; the logistic half alone is M effort

flexcomprisk.name: flexcomprisk
flexcomprisk.core_method: stub/placeholder: every modelType (splines, forest, time-varying, cause-specific, Fine-Gray, ensemble) fits the same survival::coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ covs), and eventOfInterest is never used. 'splines' wraps only the first covariate in ns(); 'time-varying' adds covariate x follow-up time as a Cox covariate (invalid). The validation plot is rnorm noise
flexcomprisk.oracle: none valid in this code; the real targets would be cmprsk::crr or riskRegression::FGR (Fine-Gray), flexsurv::flexsurvspline per cause, riskRegression::Score
flexcomprisk.gain: none until the advertised methods exist, in either language

flexmultistate.name: flexmultistate
flexmultistate.core_method: Clock-forward multistate model with one flexsurv fit per transition (flexsurvspline Royston-Parmar, or flexsurvreg Weibull/lognormal/exponential), transition probabilities (flexsurv::pmatrix.fs), restricted time in state (totlos.fs), microsimulation (sim.fmsm), AIC/BIC

flexparametric.name: flexparametric
flexparametric.core_method: Parametric survival regression (flexsurv::flexsurvreg: exponential, Weibull, lognormal, loglogistic, gamma, generalized gamma, Gompertz, etc.) and Royston-Parmar splines on hazard/odds/normal scales (flexsurvspline) with time-varying spline interactions; AIC/BIC; survival, hazard and density predictions
flexparametric.gain: none. No-covariate fits are direct via scipy.stats.<dist>.fit(CensoredData), but flexsurv's parameterisations, covariates on ancillary parameters and spline models are the bulk of the work

flexrstpm2.name: flexrstpm2
flexrstpm2.core_method: Royston-Parmar generalized survival models (rstpm2::gsm with PH/PO/probit links, called from R/flexrstpm2-estimation.R) with spline time-varying effects, cure fraction and background hazard for relative survival; predictions with optional bootstrap

gradientboosting.name: gradientboosting
gradientboosting.core_method: Cox boosting: mboost::glmboost(family = CoxPH()) with k-fold cvrisk to choose mstop (the default), gbm::gbm(distribution = 'coxph'), or xgboost (AFT approximation). The predictions table (risk_score = runif) and the convergence/importance/partial plots are placeholders
gradientboosting.gain: none. The default component-wise linear Cox boosting is deterministic for a fixed mstop and would be implementable (M) on its own

groomecompare.name: groomecompare
groomecompare.core_method: Compares two staging systems: a Cox model on stage per system (coxph), log-HR 'consistency' (max adjacent difference), 'discrimination' (log-HR range), 'balance' (max/min stage size), and an ad hoc 'prediction' = consistency + 1/discrimination + balance, which is not Groome's explained-variation measure; C-index comparison (survival::concordance), optional bootstrap of the ranks; radar/bar/KM plots
groomecompare.oracle: survival::coxph, survival::concordance; the metric definitions of Groome et al. (2001)
groomecompare.gain: a numpy-vectorised bootstrap of the ranking, and a chance to replace the ad hoc 'prediction' metric with Groome's; otherwise none

groupedforest.name: groupedforest
groupedforest.core_method: Treatment hazard ratio within each subgroup (a separate coxph per level, optional covariates, Wald CIs via broom::tidy), optional overall HR, treatment x subgroup interaction LR test; the value is mainly the forest plot
groupedforest.oracle: survival::coxph, broom::tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE), stats::anova (LR test)
groupedforest.gain: none over R; the forest plot would still have to be drawn by R or D3

grouplasso.name: grouplasso
grouplasso.core_method: Group-LASSO / group-MCP / group-SCAD Cox (grpreg::grpsurv, cv.grpsurv) with user or factor groupings, CV lambda, concordance, bootstrap stability selection, permutation test

hiddenmarkov.name: hiddenmarkov
hiddenmarkov.core_method: Hidden Markov multistate model (msm::msm with an ematrix of misclassification, panel/exact obstypes, covariates on intensities and hidden covariates): transition intensities, pmatrix, prevalence, Pearson GOF (pearson.msm), Viterbi decoding
hiddenmarkov.oracle: msm::msm(ematrix =), msm::qmatrix.msm, msm::pmatrix.msm, msm::viterbi.msm, msm::pearson.msm, msm::prevalence.msm

highdimcox.name: highdimcox
highdimcox.core_method: Penalized Cox (glmnet LASSO, ridge, elastic net, adaptive LASSO) with CV lambda, subsampling stability selection, concordance, variable-importance and path plots

illnessdeath.name: illnessdeath
illnessdeath.core_method: Illness-death multistate model from complete histories: unadjusted Aalen-Johansen state occupation (multi-state survfit with id/istate, IJ-variance CIs), a separate counting-process cause-specific Cox per transition with cluster(id) robust SEs, basehaz, cox.zph, martingale-residual summaries, restricted mean time in state with a whole-subject bootstrap
illnessdeath.oracle: survival::survfit(Surv(start, stop, state) ~ 1, id =, istate =), survival::coxph(cluster = id, ties =), survival::basehaz, survival::cox.zph
illnessdeath.gain: the whole-subject bootstrap of restricted time in state would be faster vectorised; otherwise none

jiwillsurvive.name: jiwillsurvive
jiwillsurvive.core_method: plot-first: KM curves (survminer/ggplot2), follow-up plots, a survival table at time points and a log-rank test (survfit/survdiff). The iwillsurvive package named in the title is not used
jiwillsurvive.gain: none; it duplicates the survival analysis

joinpoint.name: joinpoint
joinpoint.core_method: Joinpoint (segmented log-linear) regression of rates on time: segmented::selgmented chooses 0..Kmax joinpoints by BIC; per-segment APC = 100(exp(slope) - 1) with t-based CIs (segmented::slope), plus AAPC
joinpoint.oracle: segmented::selgmented(type = 'bic'), segmented::slope, segmented::aapc; the NCI Joinpoint program
joinpoint.gain: an exhaustive grid search (the global optimum; segmented can stop at a local one) and the NCI permutation test for the number of joinpoints (Kim et al. 2000), both cheap in numpy

jointfrailty.name: jointfrailty
jointfrailty.core_method: Joint frailty model for recurrent and terminal events via frailtypack. The default 'shared_frailty' path calls frailtypack::jointfrailty(), which the installed frailtypack 3.8.1 does not export (it has frailtyPenal/longiPenal/multivPenal), so the default cannot run. The frailty, association, prediction and residual tables and all plots are placeholders

jointmodeling.name: jointmodeling
jointmodeling.core_method: Joint longitudinal-survival model: Bayesian JMbayes2::jm (the default) on nlme::lme + coxph submodels, a two-stage approach (lme, then Cox/survreg), or joineR::joint (ML); dynamic prediction and validation
needs: pymc or another MCMC engine (for the default Bayesian JMbayes2 path)

jvisr.name: jvisr
jvisr.core_method: plot-first: visR::estimate_KM + visR::visr KM and cumulative-incidence plots with risk tables and quantile/p-value annotations; CDISC ADTTE input

landmarkanalysis.name: landmarkanalysis
landmarkanalysis.core_method: Landmark Cox models: at each landmark the subjects still at risk are re-origined with a prediction-window horizon and a coxph is fitted; HR table (Wald, fixed 1.96), C-index with SE (survival::concordance), and an 'AUC' column that is just the C-index. The super model, bootstrap validation, dynamic-risk, calibration and discrimination plots are placeholders
landmarkanalysis.oracle: survival::coxph, survival::concordance; dynpred::cutLM + coxph(cluster =) for the super model
landmarkanalysis.gain: a real stacked super-model and numpy-vectorised bootstrap optimism correction in place of the placeholders (also doable in R)

lassointro.name: lassointro
lassointro.core_method: Static educational HTML guide (overview, decision guide, scenarios, pitfalls, glossary). It computes nothing.

marginalrecurrent.name: marginalrecurrent
marginalrecurrent.core_method: reReg::reReg recurrent-event rate models: Cox-type 'cox', accelerated rate 'ar', and joint 'cox|cox'/'ar|ar' with a terminal event, with sandwich or bootstrap SE and cumulative-rate/survival functions. 'gamma_frailty' is mapped to reReg 'cox.HW', whose frailty is unspecified rather than gamma. The goodness-of-fit table is a placeholder (all NA).
marginalrecurrent.gain: none for a faithful port: reReg's non-smooth estimating equations would have to be re-derived. An LWYY/Andersen-Gill rate model with robust SE plus a Nelson-Aalen mean cumulative function would be implementable, but it is a different method.

markovmultistate.name: markovmultistate
markovmultistate.core_method: stub/placeholder: transition intensities, sojourn times, covariate effects and predictions are hard-coded mock values (rnorm/runif/sample). No msm/mstate model is ever fitted, and the code itself says so.
markovmultistate.gain: A real fit of the promised time-homogeneous CTMC on panel data (P(t) = expm(Qt) likelihood, log-linear covariates, Hessian SEs) replacing fabricated output. msm is not even called. Parametric-bootstrap CIs for P(t) and state occupancy would be cheap.

mixedcox.name: mixedcox
mixedcox.core_method: Mixed-effects Cox via coxme::coxme: Gaussian random intercept or slope, nested clusters, Laplace-approximated integrated partial likelihood, with a coxph comparison and LR test.
mixedcox.gain: none: there is no Python coxme, and the R version works

mixedeffectscox.name: mixedeffectscox
mixedeffectscox.core_method: Shared gamma-frailty Cox via survival::coxph(... + frailty(cluster)), a penalized partial likelihood. Partial stub: the random-effects table shows a hard-coded variance of 1, not the fitted theta.
mixedeffectscox.gain: none for a port. The fake variance is a small R fix (read the fitted theta).

multistatesurvival.name: multistatesurvival
multistatesurvival.core_method: mstate pipeline: msprep, then Breslow Cox stratified by transition, then msfit/probtrans (Aalen-Johansen). Covariates enter un-expanded, so one effect is shared across all transitions. The 'clock_forward' and semi-Markov branches look swapped (Surv(time) vs Surv(Tstart,Tstop)). Partial stub: the transition-probability, state-probability, sojourn and HR display helpers are called but never defined.
multistatesurvival.oracle: mstate::msprep, survival::coxph(Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status) ~ strata(trans), method = 'breslow'), mstate::msfit, mstate::probtrans
multistatesurvival.gain: The no-covariate Aalen-Johansen transition matrix (product integral of Nelson-Aalen increments) is implementable in numpy (about M) and would fill the empty tables. The hard part is matching msfit/probtrans with covariates and their variances.

ncvregcox.name: ncvregcox
ncvregcox.core_method: SCAD/MCP-penalized Cox via ncvreg::cv.ncvsurv (coordinate-descent path plus k-fold CV for lambda), then a coxph refit and concordance.
ncvregcox.gain: none: the path algorithm and random CV folds cannot be matched draw for draw, and the R version works

oneSurvival.name: oneSurvival
oneSurvival.core_method: Kaplan-Meier for a single outcome: n, events, median survival with its CI (survfit, Greenwood with log CI). The ggfortify KM plot is the main output.
oneSurvival.gain: none. The table is tiny, the plot has to stay in R, and the survfit log-CI and median-CI rule need about 20 lines of own code (scipy.ecdf offers only linear and log-log CIs). An RMST row could be added.

parametricfrailty.name: parametricfrailty
parametricfrailty.core_method: Mislabelled: no parametric shared-frailty likelihood is fitted. It calls frailtySurv::frailtySurv, which is semiparametric with a nonparametric baseline; its argument names (data, distribution, frailty_dist, method) appear not to match frailtySurv's (dat, frailty, control) - unverified. The survreg fallback has no frailty term.
parametricfrailty.oracle: frailtypack::frailtyPenal(hazard = 'Weibull', RandDist = 'Gamma'), parfm::parfm(dist = 'weibull', frailty = 'gamma'); survival::survreg for the no-frailty limit
parametricfrailty.gain: Would deliver what the title promises: a closed-form Weibull/exponential/Gompertz x gamma-frailty marginal likelihood (lognormal frailty by Gauss-Hermite), with frailty variance, Kendall's tau and empirical-Bayes frailties, and no frailtySurv dependency.

pcacox.name: pcacox
pcacox.core_method: Dimension reduction, then Cox on the component scores. Reduction is standard PCA (prcomp), sparse PCA (sparsepca::spca), kernel PCA (kernlab::kpca) or supervised PC (superpc train/cv), with components chosen by CV. Also C-index and permutation/bootstrap validation.
pcacox.oracle: stats::prcomp, sparsepca::spca, kernlab::kpca, superpc::superpc.train, superpc::superpc.cv, survival::coxph, survival::concordance
pcacox.gain: Plain PCA plus Cox is implementable once a numpy Cox engine exists. Matching the spca, kernlab and superpc variants and their random CV is not worth it.

plscox.name: plscox
plscox.core_method: Partial least squares Cox regression (plsRcox::plsRcox, Bastien 2005) with cv.plsRcox choosing the number of components, then coxph on the components.

progressionsurvival.name: progressionsurvival
progressionsurvival.core_method: Progression-free survival: KM by treatment with survival at time points, univariable Cox treatment HR (Fine-Gray via cmprsk::crr as an option), landmark KM/Cox, and subgroup Cox with a treatment x subgroup interaction. The survival_method and comparison_test options (FH, MaxCombo, RMST) are never read. CIF, biomarker, sensitivity, interim and progression-pattern parts are placeholders.
progressionsurvival.oracle: survival::survfit, survival::survdiff, survival::coxph (Efron ties), cmprsk::cuminc, cmprsk::crr
progressionsurvival.gain: Could fill the placeholders: Aalen-Johansen CIF, RMST at rmst_tau and FH/MaxCombo weights are short numpy code. Needs a shared numpy Cox (Efron) engine; Fine-Gray would also need IPCW weights.

relativesurvival.name: relativesurvival
relativesurvival.core_method: Relative and net survival against population life tables: relsurv::rs.surv (Pohar-Perme, Ederer I/II), rsadd (additive excess hazard), rsmul, cmp.rel (crude mortality), and rstpm2::stpm2 flexible parametric, with survexp and the survexp.us/slopop ratetables.
relativesurvival.oracle: relsurv::rs.surv, relsurv::rsadd, relsurv::rsmul, relsurv::cmp.rel, rstpm2::stpm2, survival::survexp
relativesurvival.gain: none. Pohar-Perme alone is implementable, but it depends on R-only population ratetables (the data would have to be exported) and on the age/year/sex lookup machinery.

rpasurvival.name: rpasurvival
rpasurvival.core_method: Survival tree: rpart(method = 'exp') with cost-complexity pruning by xval CV. Terminal nodes become risk groups, compared by KM, log-rank and Cox. A new risk-group column is written (Output option), and the tree plot is a main figure.
rpasurvival.gain: none: rpart's exponential-scaling splits and random xval folds cannot be matched, there is no Python rpart, and ClinicoPathPj has no Output columns or plots

semimarkov.name: semimarkov
semimarkov.core_method: stub/placeholder: the whole semi-Markov engine returns mock results via rnorm/runif/sample, even when SemiMarkov is installed. The code marks it as a RELEASE BLOCKER.
semimarkov.oracle: SemiMarkov::semiMarkov (not installed locally); flexsurv::flexsurvreg per transition on clock-reset times
semimarkov.gain: Real estimates of the promised parametric semi-Markov model (Weibull or exponentiated-Weibull sojourns with proportional covariate effects, by MLE) instead of fabricated ones, with no R package needed

simonmakuch.name: simonmakuch
simonmakuch.core_method: Simon-Makuch time-dependent KM (counting-process survfit by current exposure), Mantel-Byar test, time-dependent Cox (tmerge, then coxph with time-varying exposure plus baseline covariates), landmark analysis, naive vs time-dependent comparison, and cox.zph.
simonmakuch.oracle: survival::tmerge, survival::survfit(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ exposure), survival::coxph (counting process), survival::cox.zph, survival::survdiff
simonmakuch.gain: The Simon-Makuch curves plus the Mantel-Byar score test alone are implementable (M). The size comes from the counting-process Cox with covariates and cox.zph. Little added value over R.

simpleSurvivalPower.name: simpleSurvivalPower
simpleSurvivalPower.core_method: Closed-form survival power and sample size: Schoenfeld events for log-rank, Hsieh-Lavori for Cox with a continuous covariate (powerSurvEpi), RMST under exponential survival, non-inferiority, SNP, multi-arm, O'Brien-Fleming/Pocock approximations, and root-finding for effect size or duration. Defect: the 'Monte Carlo simulation' always shows 0.0% empirical power. It ignores the simulated times (o1 + o2 = n_total, so the variance is 0 and every p is 1).
simpleSurvivalPower.oracle: powerSurvEpi::ssizeEpiCont.default, powerSurvEpi::powerEpiCont.default, gsDesign::nEvents (Schoenfeld), plus the closed-form formulas in the .b.R
simpleSurvivalPower.gain: A genuine vectorized numpy simulation (accrual, dropout, administrative censoring, a log-rank test per replicate) would replace the broken 0% figure and check the analytic numbers. Removes powerSurvEpi.

smoothhazard.name: smoothhazard
smoothhazard.core_method: Smoothed hazard, but home-grown. 'kernel' divides the events within +/- b of t by (at risk x 2b), which is not the Ramlau-Hansen estimator. 'bspline' fits smooth.spline to a histogram of rates. The muhaz/bshazard methods named in the UI are not used, and covariates only filter complete cases. The value is the hazard curve.
smoothhazard.oracle: muhaz::muhaz (fixed global bandwidth, boundary correction), bshazard::bshazard
smoothhazard.gain: A correct boundary-corrected kernel-smoothed Nelson-Aalen hazard with bootstrap pointwise bands. The curve itself would still have to be drawn by R.

sparsegrouplasso.name: sparsegrouplasso
sparsegrouplasso.core_method: Not a true sparse group lasso: glmnet elastic-net Cox (Breslow ties) with group-derived adaptive penalty factors, cv.glmnet choosing lambda, ridge/lasso comparisons, and concordance.
needs: scikit-survival (CoxnetSurvivalAnalysis, a port of glmnet's algorithm; not bundled)
sparsegrouplasso.oracle: glmnet::glmnet(family = 'cox'), glmnet::cv.glmnet, survival::concordance; SGL::cvSGL for a real sparse-group penalty

spatialbayesiansurvival.name: spatialbayesiansurvival
spatialbayesiansurvival.core_method: stub/placeholder: a non-spatial survreg is fitted as a 'surrogate for the Bayesian mean', and its Wald CIs are labelled Bayesian. Spatial effects are hard-coded (0, RR 1) for the first five regions. spBayesSurv is never called.
needs: pymc or another MCMC engine (not bundled)
spatialbayesiansurvival.gain: none realistic: spatial MCMC survival in bare numpy is a large project, and MCMC can only be matched in distribution

standardizedratio.name: standardizedratio
standardizedratio.core_method: Indirect standardization: SIR/SMR = O/E, with E from rate x person-time or supplied directly. Exact Poisson CI and p-value via poisson.test, overall and per stratum.
standardizedratio.gain: small: mid-P and Byar intervals and a heterogeneity chi-square across strata are a few lines each. The R version already uses base R only.

subgroupforest.name: subgroupforest
subgroupforest.core_method: Treatment effect within each subgroup: Cox HR, logistic OR, modified-Poisson RR with HC0 sandwich, or mean difference by lm. Interaction tested by LR or F test (anova). The forest plot is the main output.
subgroupforest.oracle: survival::coxph, stats::glm (binomial, poisson), sandwich::vcovHC(type = 'HC0'), stats::lm, stats::anova
subgroupforest.gain: little: the forest plot stays in R and the sandwich dependency goes. Needs a shared numpy Cox (Efron) engine and an IRLS GLM.

superpc.name: superpc
superpc.core_method: Supervised principal components, own code: univariable Cox Wald screening of each feature, PCA (prcomp) on the selected features, Cox on the top components, k-fold CV C-index with unseeded folds.
superpc.oracle: survival::coxph (per feature and on the PCs), stats::prcomp, survival::concordance; superpc::superpc.train for the canonical method
superpc.gain: Speed: vectorized Newton score/Wald screening of thousands of features (R loops one coxph per feature), and seeded, reproducible CV

surveysurvival.name: surveysurvival
surveysurvival.core_method: Design-based survival: survey::svydesign (weights, strata, clusters), svykm weighted KM with design SEs, svycoxph with linearization variance, svytotal.
surveysurvival.gain: none. Weighted KM point estimates are easy, but the design-based SEs (strata, PSU, FPC) are exactly what the survey package provides.

survivalbart.name: survivalbart
survivalbart.core_method: stub/placeholder: BART::wbart is fitted on log(time), ignoring censoring. Variable importance, MCMC diagnostics, CV log-likelihoods and predictions are runif/rnorm placeholders.
survivalbart.gain: none realistic: MCMC sum-of-trees is not a numpy/scipy job and cannot be matched draw for draw

survivalcalibration.name: survivalcalibration
survivalcalibration.core_method: Calibration of supplied predicted survival probabilities at a horizon: observed KM vs mean predicted in quantile groups, calibration slope/intercept from lm on the group means, E:O ratio, Harrell C (concordance). Brier is complete-case: subjects censored before the horizon are dropped, with no IPCW. 'Bootstrap validation' resamples the fixed predictions with no refit and is capped at 100 resamples.
survivalcalibration.oracle: survival::survfit, survival::concordance, stats::lm; riskRegression::Score or pec::pec for IPCW Brier
survivalcalibration.gain: IPCW Brier, a Greenwood-Nam-D'Agostino test, and thousands of vectorized bootstrap resamples instead of the 100-resample cap

survivalfeaturerank.name: survivalfeaturerank
survivalfeaturerank.core_method: Univariable Cox for each feature (HR, CI, Wald p, C with se(C)), ranked by p, HR or C, with p.adjust and KM plots of the top features. For factors with more than 2 levels only the first contrast is used. Mostly plots (11 images); a ranking export uses an Output option.
survivalfeaturerank.oracle: survival::coxph (summary: coefficients, conf.int, concordance incl. se(C)), stats::p.adjust
survivalfeaturerank.gain: Fast vectorized screening of many features and a global Wald/LR p for multi-level factors. Matching se(C) needs survival's concordance variance algorithm. Plots and the Output export have no ClinicoPathPj equivalent yet.

survivalmodelvalidation.name: survivalmodelvalidation
survivalmodelvalidation.core_method: Validation of a supplied risk score: Harrell C with boot CIs, CV and temporal splits of the same fixed score (no refit, so 'optimism' is about 0 by construction), Cox calibration slope, timeROC AUC(t), pec calibration and prediction error, dcurves DCA. Defect: concordance() is called in formula form without reverse = TRUE, so for a higher-is-riskier score it reports 1 - C, while the text gives the risk interpretation.
survivalmodelvalidation.oracle: survival::concordance(..., reverse = TRUE), boot::boot.ci, timeROC::timeROC, pec::pec, dcurves::dca
survivalmodelvalidation.gain: Fast vectorized bootstrap, and boot, pec, timeROC and dcurves are no longer needed. A port would also fix the C direction and the no-refit optimism. It overlaps survivalvalidation, so one engine could serve both.

survivalvalidation.name: survivalvalidation
survivalvalidation.core_method: Validation of a supplied risk, or of a coxph fitted from a free-text formula: pec CV prediction error (AppErr used as a stand-in), IBS/CRPS, survcomp/survConcordance C-index, timeROC AUC, calibration, dcurves DCA. Bootstrap and external validation are stubs.
survivalvalidation.oracle: survival::coxph + survival::survfit (Breslow baseline), pec::pec, pec::ibs, pec::crps, survcomp::concordance.index, timeROC::timeROC, dcurves::dca
survivalvalidation.gain: Real bootstrap and external validation (refitting per resample is cheap with a numpy Cox engine), and survcomp (Bioconductor) and pec are no longer needed. pec's random CV folds cannot be matched, so validate on fixed folds.

timedependent.name: timedependent
timedependent.core_method: Time-dependent covariate Cox (counting process, tt() transforms, timereg::timecox time-varying coefficients), landmark models, timeROC AUC(t), pROC cut-points, CV/bootstrap, riskRegression::Score, cox.zph.
timedependent.oracle: survival::coxph (counting process, tt), timereg::timecox, survival::cox.zph, timeROC::timeROC, riskRegression::Score, pROC::roc

timeroc.name: timeroc
timeroc.core_method: Two modes. Binary ROC with pROC: AUC with DeLong CI, Youden cut-point, roc.test by DeLong, bootstrap or Venkatraman. Time-dependent cumulative/dynamic AUC(t) with timeROC: KM, Cox or Aalen IPCW, with iid SEs.
timeroc.oracle: timeROC::timeROC (weighting = 'marginal', iid = TRUE), pROC::roc, pROC::ci.auc, pROC::roc.test
timeroc.gain: Fast permutation and bootstrap comparisons (Venkatraman, bootstrap roc.test at 1000+ reps). Start with KM weighting: the Cox/Aalen censoring weights need extra models.

timeupdatedsurvival.name: timeupdatedsurvival
timeupdatedsurvival.core_method: Dynamic, time-updated survival with timereg (aalen additive hazards, dynreg, cox.aalen), plus coxph/cox.zph and a Weibull survreg comparison.

timevarycox.name: timevarycox
timevarycox.core_method: Counting-process Cox with time-varying covariates (start-stop data, optional tt() terms, robust/cluster SE) and cox.zph. Defect: the backend reads 17 options its .a.yaml never declares (start_time, stop_time, ties_method, time_interaction, use_start_stop, ...). jmvcore raises on those, so the analysis cannot run as written. All plots are placeholders.
timevarycox.oracle: survival::coxph(Surv(start, stop, event) ~ ..., cluster = id), survival::cox.zph
timevarycox.gain: none: the R draft first needs its options declared

weightedlogrank.name: weightedlogrank
weightedlogrank.core_method: Weighted log-rank family via survival::survdiff, but mislabelled. rho = 1 (Peto-Peto, Fleming-Harrington G1) is reported three times, as 'Gehan-Wilcoxon', 'Peto-Peto' and 'Modified Peto', so the three are identical. rho = 0.5 is reported as 'Tarone-Ware', which actually weights by sqrt(n at risk).
weightedlogrank.gain: A correctness gain in about 100 lines: genuinely distinct K-group weights (Gehan-Breslow n, Tarone-Ware sqrt(n), Peto-Peto, Andersen's modified Peto, FH(rho, gamma)) plus a MaxCombo test

winratio.name: winratio
winratio.core_method: Unmatched Pocock win ratio on a hierarchical composite (up to two time-to-event endpoints and one continuous endpoint with a tolerance), with win odds, net benefit, and either the Dong et al. 2016 U-statistic variance or a subject bootstrap. Pairs are compared in a double interpreted R loop.
winratio.oracle: WINS::win.stat (Dong 2016 variance), BuyseTest::BuyseTest (Gehan scoring), and the R analysis itself
winratio.gain: Speed: the n1 x n0 comparison matrix is a numpy broadcast, so bootstrap CIs with 2000+ resamples become practical for hundreds of patients (R does B x n1 x n0 interpreted comparisons)

agreement.name: agreement
agreement.core_method: Interrater reliability suite: Cohen's kappa (weighted, exact), Fleiss/Conger kappa, Krippendorff alpha (bootstrap CI), Gwet AC1/AC2, PABAK, ICC (irr::icc forms with F CIs), Lin's CCC, Bland-Altman/TDI, Kendall W, Light/Finn/Robinson/iota, Stuart-Maxwell/Bhapkar/rater bias, pairwise kappas, specific agreement, rater/case clustering, kappaSize sample size. Also lme4/ordinal mixed-effects and latent-model branches.
agreement.oracle: irr::kappa2, irr::kappam.fleiss, irr::icc, irr::kripp.alpha, irr::kendall, irrCAC::gwet.ac1.raw, irrCAC::conger.kappa.raw, DescTools::CCC, DescTools::StuartMaxwellTest, vcd::Kappa
agreement.gain: small. The core coefficients port cleanly, and vectorized bootstrap CIs (alpha, AC1, kappa) would be fast. But the analysis is shipped and heavily audited, the lme4/ordinal branches stay hard, and its 44 Html panels, 9 plots and 3 Output options have no ClinicoPathPj equivalent.

cotest.name: cotest
cotest.core_method: Calculator, no data: post-test probabilities for two tests used in parallel, from sensitivity, specificity, prevalence and conditional dependence (phi covariance among diseased and non-diseased). Fagan nomogram.
cotest.oracle: the R analysis itself (closed-form Bayes, Gardner et al. 2000 covariance model)
cotest.gain: No uncertainty is propagated today. A Monte Carlo over beta-distributed sens/spec/prevalence would add CIs to every post-test probability.

decision.name: decision
decision.core_method: 2x2 diagnostic accuracy against a gold standard: sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, LR+/-, accuracy, DOR with epiR::epi.tests Clopper-Pearson CIs, Bayes recalculation at a prior prevalence, Fagan nomogram, and a misclassified-case listing and export (Output option).
decision.gain: none beyond dropping epiR. A prevalence sweep or beta-binomial uncertainty for PPV/NPV could be added. The Output export and Html report have no ClinicoPathPj equivalent yet.

decisioncalculator.name: decisioncalculator
decisioncalculator.core_method: The same diagnostic-accuracy metrics as decision, from entered TP/FP/FN/TN counts (up to three cut-offs): epiR::epi.tests CIs, prevalence scenarios, workload.
decisioncalculator.gain: none: a pure calculator that could share one Python engine with decision

decisioncombine.name: decisioncombine
decisioncombine.core_method: Combination rules for 2-3 binary tests (all, any, majority, patterns): epi.tests metrics per pattern, paired comparisons (Newcombe, Agresti-Caffo CIs), stratified association tests (Fisher, exact conditional Mantel-Haenszel), and rmultinom bootstrap optimism correction.
decisioncombine.gain: small: an exact CMH by convolution avoids the uniroot underflow fallback noted in the R code. The bootstrap is already vectorized in R.

decisioncompare.name: decisioncompare
decisioncompare.core_method: Compares 2-3 tests on the same cases: per-test epi.tests metrics, paired McNemar (exact, mid-p or asymptotic) with Holm adjustment, Newcombe method-10 CIs for paired differences, Cochran's Q, OPA with a non-inferiority margin, and stratified tables.

decisioncurve.name: decisioncurve
decisioncurve.core_method: Decision curve analysis for a binary outcome: net benefit of model probability columns vs treat-all and treat-none over a threshold grid, bootstrap CIs and pairwise model comparisons, interventions avoided, clinical impact, standardized net benefit, relative utility, cost-benefit.
decisioncurve.gain: little: the R bootstrap is already O(n log n + T log n), and the DCA plot is the main output

enhancedROC.name: enhancedROC
enhancedROC.core_method: Clinical ROC: pROC AUC with DeLong or bootstrap CIs, Youden and constrained cut-points, partial AUC, smoothing, CROC, convex hull, DeLong comparisons, multiclass (Hand-Till), calibration (logistic recalibration, Hosmer-Lemeshow, Brier, ns() spline calibration, E:O), NNT/decision impact, internal validation.
enhancedROC.oracle: pROC::roc, pROC::ci.auc (DeLong), pROC::coords, pROC::roc.test, pROC::smooth, pROC::multiclass.roc, boot::boot.ci, stats::glm
enhancedROC.gain: Fast stratified bootstrap (AUC, partial AUC, cut-point) at 2000+ reps. Density smoothing and ns() calibration match R only approximately. A large surface for an analysis that is shipped and works.

kappaSizeCI.name: kappaSizeCI
kappaSizeCI.core_method: Number of subjects needed so the kappa CI excludes a lower bound, via kappaSize::CIBinary/CI3Cats/CI4Cats/CI5Cats. Goodness-of-fit model: Donner-Eliasziw for 2 raters; Altaye-Donner-Klar/Eliasziw cells for multiple raters and 2-5 categories.
kappaSizeCI.gain: Could simulate the achieved CI coverage at the planned n on every run (today it is quoted from offline validation) and drop kappaSize. One engine serves all three kappaSize analyses.

kappaSizeFixedN.name: kappaSizeFixedN
kappaSizeFixedN.core_method: Lowest expected kappa (lower CI bound) for a fixed N, via kappaSize::FixedNBinary/FixedN3Cats/FixedN4Cats/FixedN5Cats, same goodness-of-fit model.
kappaSizeFixedN.gain: Same as kappaSizeCI: on-the-fly coverage simulation, and it shares that engine (S once the engine exists)

kappaSizePower.name: kappaSizePower
kappaSizePower.core_method: Power-based sample size for testing kappa0 against kappa1 (kappaSize::PowerBinary/Power3Cats/Power4Cats/Power5Cats, noncentral chi-square), plus an in-R Monte Carlo of the pooled-cell goodness-of-fit test for binary outcomes (seeded rmultinom, vectorized bisection ML).
kappaSizePower.oracle: kappaSize::PowerBinary, kappaSize::Power3Cats, kappaSize::Power4Cats, kappaSize::Power5Cats, and the analysis's own .simPowerBinary
kappaSizePower.gain: small: the simulation is already vectorized in R. numpy would allow larger R and a simulation for 3-5 categories too.

lassologistic.name: lassologistic
lassologistic.core_method: Penalized logistic regression with glmnet (lasso, ridge or elastic net; cv.glmnet lambda.min/1se), bootstrap validation, pROC AUC, a coefficient-based points score with cut-offs, and a predictions export (Output option).
needs: scikit-learn (L1 logistic; would not reproduce glmnet's lambda path and standardization exactly; not bundled)

nogoldstandard.name: nogoldstandard
nogoldstandard.core_method: Diagnostic accuracy without a gold standard for 2-5 binary tests: 2-class latent class model (poLCA EM, conditional independence), own penalized EM (Beta(2,1) priors, MAP point estimate), composite reference, all/any-positive rules, kappa between tests, case-bootstrap CIs.
nogoldstandard.gain: Vectorized EM makes many random starts and 1000+ bootstrap refits cheap (poLCA per resample is slow). Conditional-dependence latent class models could be added later.

psychopdaROC.name: psychopdaROC
psychopdaROC.core_method: Optimal cut-point ROC with cutpointr: maximize/minimize a metric, Youden, cost/utility, loess-smoothed, bootstrapped, or normal/kernel Youden. Also pROC AUC/DeLong, partial AUC, IDI/NRI, power for AUC, Bayesian AUC, fixed-sens/spec interpolation, and meta-analysis of AUCs.
psychopdaROC.oracle: cutpointr::cutpointr (method/metric), pROC::roc, pROC::ci.auc, pROC::roc.test, pROC::coords, pROC::var, pROC::cov
psychopdaROC.gain: Much faster vectorized bootstrap of cut-points (boot_runs) and of IDI/NRI. The loess-smoothed metric cannot be matched, since scipy has no R loess.

sequentialtests.name: sequentialtests
sequentialtests.core_method: Closed-form combined Se/Sp/PPV/NPV/LR+/LR-/NNT for two tests (serial-positive, serial-negative, parallel) under conditional independence, per-population flow counts and cost per strategy; five ggplot figures (flow diagram, population flow, sensitivity analysis).
sequentialtests.oracle: sequentialtests() itself / hand-computed identities (serial+: Se1*Se2, Sp1+(1-Sp1)*Sp2; serial-/parallel: Se1+(1-Se1)*Se2, Sp1*Sp2) for each preset
sequentialtests.gain: none: a no-data calculator that is instant in R; the flow-diagram plots, much of its value, would have to stay in R. Useful only as a no-data template for ClinicoPathPj.

adaptivetrialdesign.name: adaptivetrialdesign
adaptivetrialdesign.core_method: stub/placeholder: one interim look; the prop.test or Welch t-test p-value is turned into 1 - p/2 and labelled a 'posterior probability of efficacy'; about 25 options (spending functions, priors, MCMC, simulations) are ignored.
adaptivetrialdesign.oracle: gsDesign::gsDesign (sfu = sfLDOF / sfLDPocock) and rpact::getDesignGroupSequential for real boundaries and conditional power; stats::prop.test / stats::t.test for the current single look
adaptivetrialdesign.gain: Replaces a mislabelled p-value with real group-sequential boundaries (Lan-DeMets spending through recursive integration or MVN crossing probabilities). Simulated operating characteristics vectorise well in numpy. This is new work, not a port; the Bayesian/MCMC options would be hard and need PyMC.

agreementintro.name: agreementintro
agreementintro.core_method: No statistics: a rule-based guide that maps questionnaire answers (data type, raters, design) to the recommended agreement analysis.

aivalidation.name: aivalidation
aivalidation.core_method: Per-score ROC AUC with DeLong (or stratified bootstrap) CI, Youden-optimal cutoff with Se/Sp, Youden J and MCC at that cutoff, pairwise DeLong tests of correlated AUCs, and k-fold CV of the Youden threshold (AUC of fixed scores per fold).
aivalidation.oracle: pROC::roc (direction = 'auto' via medians), pROC::auc, pROC::ci.auc (delong; method = 'bootstrap' is stratified), pROC::roc.test(method = 'delong'), pROC::coords(x = 'all') whose thresholds are midpoints between unique values
aivalidation.gain: No new capability over pROC. One verified AUC/DeLong helper would serve about 8 analyses in this batch (modelval, predmodel, leaveonecenterout, multiclassroc, door, clinicalscore...) and makes bootstrap CIs fast.

bayesdca.name: bayesdca
bayesdca.core_method: Decision curve analysis: net benefit over a threshold grid for each predictor versus treat-all/none. The Bayesian version draws Se/Sp from conjugate Beta posteriors (prevalence held fixed) for credible bands, then EVPI = E[max NB] - max E[NB]; optional bootstrap CIs.
bayesdca.oracle: dcurves::dca for frequentist net benefit (exact). Bayesian E[NB] is linear in Se and Sp, so posterior means can be checked exactly with Beta means; credible limits and EVPI only within Monte Carlo error.
bayesdca.gain: Speed: the R EVPI step runs sapply per draw (draws x thresholds). numpy computes draws x thresholds x strategies in one array, so 1e4-1e5 draws and dense threshold grids become instant. It could also draw prevalence from its posterior, which the R code holds fixed.

bayesiandiagnostic.name: bayesiandiagnostic
bayesiandiagnostic.core_method: stub/placeholder: frequentist 2x2 Se/Sp/PPV/NPV/LR/DOR. The 'posterior mean/median/mode' columns repeat one point estimate, the 'credible intervals' are Wald intervals, and the PPV/NPV interval is a literal +/-0.1. Prior, MCMC and hierarchical options are unused.
bayesiandiagnostic.oracle: stats::qbeta / stats::pbeta for conjugate Beta-binomial posteriors (exact); Monte Carlo PPV/NPV/LR summaries within MC error; mada::reitsma as frequentist reference for the multi-study bivariate option
bayesiandiagnostic.gain: Replaces fabricated intervals with real conjugate posteriors and fast vectorised posterior draws (equally possible in R). The hierarchical/bivariate multi-study model would be hard (needs MCMC such as PyMC).

bayesiannetworkma.name: bayesiannetworkma
bayesiannetworkma.core_method: stub/placeholder: counts studies and treatments; every treatment effect (0.5, SD 0.1, CrI 0.3-0.7), SUCRA and rank is hardcoded. No network meta-analysis is fitted.
bayesiannetworkma.oracle: gemtc::mtc.run / multinma::nma (Bayesian); netmeta::netmeta for a frequentist alternative
bayesiannetworkma.gain: None until a real model exists. A numpy weighted-least-squares (netmeta-style) frequentist NMA would be implementable and avoids JAGS/Stan, which jamovi cannot install.

brierscore.name: brierscore
brierscore.core_method: Time-dependent Brier score at t with IPCW (reverse-KM censoring weights), scaled Brier versus a KM null model, integrated Brier score over [t1,t2], bootstrap CIs, multi-model comparison and a calibration-by-group table.
brierscore.oracle: riskRegression::Score(metrics = 'brier', cens.model = 'km', times =), pec::pec (IBS), survival::survfit for the reverse KM
brierscore.gain: Speed: the R IPCW weight loop is O(n^2) (which() per subject) and is repeated per bootstrap replicate; searchsorted makes it O(n log n). Validate against riskRegression, not this code: events get G(T_i) not G(T_i-), and the analytic SE sqrt(B(1-B)/n) treats Brier as a proportion.

causalmediation.name: causalmediation
causalmediation.core_method: Basic tier: mediation::mediate (nonparametric bootstrap) with lm/glm mediator and outcome models, giving ACME, ADE, total effect and proportion mediated, plus medsens rho sensitivity. HD tier: hdmax2. The comprehensive (CMAverse) tier is a 'coming soon' placeholder.
causalmediation.oracle: mediation::mediate(boot = TRUE, sims =) and mediation::medsens; for lm-lm models the ACME equals a*b from stats::lm coefficients, which is an exact check
causalmediation.gain: Drops mediation for the common lm/glm case, with a vectorised bootstrap (CIs match only within MC error). The HD tier (hdmax2) and survival outcome models are hard and would stay in R.

clinicalscore.name: clinicalscore
clinicalscore.core_method: Fits a logistic (default), linear, proportional-odds (MASS::polr) or Cox model and converts coefficients to integer points (Schneeweiss or beta x10 scaling). Outputs a score lookup with predicted risk, AUC (pROC), bootstrap validation, calibration and decision-curve tables; the nomogram is drawn with rms.
clinicalscore.oracle: stats::glm(binomial), stats::lm, MASS::polr(Hess = TRUE), survival::coxph, pROC::auc / pROC::ci.auc; points computed by hand from the coefficients
clinicalscore.gain: Little. R fits these instantly; the rms nomogram and plots stay in R; the Cox option is the hard part (Efron ties). Needs model.matrix-style dummy coding of factors.

clinicalvalidation.name: clinicalvalidation
clinicalvalidation.core_method: Fits logistic, Cox, random forest, LDA or SVM, then validates by bootstrap, k-fold, repeated CV or holdout: AUC, Brier, calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow, slope), PR curve and multi-model comparison.
clinicalvalidation.oracle: stats::glm, survival::coxph, MASS::lda, randomForest::randomForest, e1071::svm, ResourceSelection::hoslem.test, PRROC::pr.curve, pROC::ci.auc
clinicalvalidation.gain: none: scikit-learn forests and SVMs would not reproduce randomForest/e1071 anyway. Only the logistic/LDA path is portable with numpy/scipy.

clinicalvalidationinteractive.name: clinicalvalidationinteractive
clinicalvalidationinteractive.core_method: stub/placeholder: no model is fitted. AUC, sensitivity, specificity, a calibration statistic and its p-value are drawn with runif().
clinicalvalidationinteractive.oracle: stats::glm, pROC::ci.auc, pROC::coords (threshold under min Se/Sp/PPV/NPV constraints), rms::validate for optimism
clinicalvalidationinteractive.gain: Nothing specific to Python. The output is fabricated today and the analysis duplicates clinicalvalidation/predmodel: merge rather than port. An honest logistic-only version would be IRLS, bootstrap/CV AUC and constrained threshold search.

cohenskappa.name: cohenskappa
cohenskappa.core_method: Cohen's unweighted and linear/quadratic weighted kappa with Fleiss-Cohen-Everitt asymptotic SE, CI and z-test (psych::cohen.kappa), bootstrap CI, Stuart-Maxwell and McNemar tests, per-category agreement; Fleiss' and Light's kappa for 3-5 raters.
cohenskappa.oracle: psych::cohen.kappa (kappa, var.kappa, weighted.kappa, var.weighted), irr::kappa2, irr::kappam.fleiss, irr::kappam.light, DescTools::StuartMaxwellTest, stats::mcnemar.test
cohenskappa.gain: Removes psych, irr and the heavy DescTools from this analysis, and vectorises the bootstrap (R calls psych::cohen.kappa once per replicate). A verified kappa helper is reusable by modalitycomparison and multiclassdiagnostics.

concordanceindex.name: concordanceindex
concordanceindex.core_method: Harrell's C via survival::concordance(reverse = TRUE) with infinitesimal-jackknife SE, Wald or bootstrap CI, Somers' D = 2C-1, truncated C at evaluation horizons and KM by risk group. Pairwise model comparisons use z-tests that assume independent C-indices (flagged as anticonservative).
concordanceindex.oracle: survival::concordance (concordance, var, count: concordant/discordant/tied.x/tied.y); Hmisc::rcorr.cens for Somers' Dxy
concordanceindex.gain: Modest, since survival::concordance is already fast C code. Python could add a correct paired comparison using the joint IJ covariance of two C-indices (as concordance(y ~ x1 + x2) gives) in place of the independence z-test. Matching the IJ variance exactly needs care.

costeffectiveness.name: costeffectiveness
costeffectiveness.core_method: Patient-level CEA by strategy: mean cost/effect, incremental values, ICER, strong/extended dominance, NMB at one or many WTP thresholds, bootstrap ICER/NMB CIs and P(cost-effective). Deterministic SA uses hardcoded ranges, and the PSA/EVPPI paths are partly placeholders.
costeffectiveness.oracle: dampack::calculate_icers (ICER, strong/extended dominance), BCEA::bcea (CEAC, EVPI from bootstrap/PSA draws); bootstrap results within MC error
costeffectiveness.gain: Speed: one array covers strategies x replicates x WTP grid, so dense CEACs and EVPI are cheap where the R code loops per replicate. The CE-plane, CEAC and tornado plots still need R.

decisiongraph.name: decisiongraph
decisiongraph.core_method: Decision-tree roll-back of expected cost/utility, ICER/NMB/dominance, one-way sensitivity (tornado), Markov cohort trace with discounting and half-cycle correction, PSA with beta/gamma/lognormal/Dirichlet draws, CEAC, EVPI and budget impact. The tree diagram is the main figure.
decisiongraph.oracle: no package in the R code: hand-computed trees; heemod::run_model for Markov cohort traces, dampack::calculate_icers; PSA within MC error
decisiongraph.gain: Speed for PSA: the cohort traces for all draws are one batched matrix product (draws x cycles x states), allowing 1e4+ simulations where the R code chunks and parallelises. The tree graph and tornado/CEAC plots must stay in R.

decisionpanel.name: decisionpanel
decisionpanel.core_method: Combines up to 5 binary tests: Se/Sp/PPV/NPV/accuracy/Youden/cost for single tests and for parallel (any/all/majority), sequential and exhaustive combinations; forward/backward panel building, redundancy, NRI, bootstrap and CV of the chosen panel; optional CART tree (rpart/partykit).
needs: scikit-learn, only for the tree option (would not reproduce rpart/partykit)
decisionpanel.oracle: hand-computed 2x2 tables (base table()) for every combination; rpart::rpart / partykit::ctree for the tree option
decisionpanel.gain: Speed: all 2^k-1 combinations x rules x bootstrap replicates are boolean array reductions in numpy; the R code needs caching to stay responsive. Trees and plots stay in R.

diagnosticsamplesize.name: diagnosticsamplesize
diagnosticsamplesize.core_method: Calculator: n such that the Clopper-Pearson CI for Se/Sp has a target width (search over n using qbeta), inflated by prevalence and non-response; zero-miss planning n = ceil(log(alpha/2)/log(lower bound)); comparison across prevalences.
diagnosticsamplesize.oracle: stats::binom.test()$conf.int (Clopper-Pearson) inside the same n search; presize::prec_sens / presize::prec_spec (method = 'exact')
diagnosticsamplesize.gain: none: an instant closed-form calculator. A good small first port.

differentialdiagnosis.name: differentialdiagnosis
differentialdiagnosis.core_method: stub/placeholder: diagnoses come from a hardcoded 6-diagnosis list with literal probabilities; the user's data never affect the output.
differentialdiagnosis.gain: Nothing specific to Python; it needs a real implementation first, in either language. An honest version would be a naive-Bayes posterior over confirmed diagnoses with Laplace smoothing and LR ranking. The Bayesian-network and random-forest options would be hard.

door.name: door
door.core_method: DOOR probability = P(index more desirable) + 0.5 P(tie), the Mann-Whitney/AUC form, with placement (DeLong) variance and a clipped Wald CI, plus a rank-distribution table per group.
door.oracle: pROC::auc and pROC::var(method = 'delong') on the oriented rank (same estimand and variance); stats::wilcox.test W / (n1*n0)
door.gain: Only speed for large n: R uses O(n1*n0) loops, rankdata is O(n log n). A good small validation target.

entropyanalysis.name: entropyanalysis
entropyanalysis.core_method: Shannon entropy (optionally normalised) of each case's predicted class-probability vector, uncertainty flags, conditional entropy H(Y|X), mutual information with a binned predictor (equal width/frequency/Sturges) and KL divergence.
entropyanalysis.oracle: entropy::entropy.empirical (unit = 'log2'), entropy::mi.plugin, entropy::KL.plugin, infotheo::mutinformation; bins must reproduce R cut() (right-closed, use digitize(right=True))
entropyanalysis.gain: none: already base-R arithmetic; scipy.stats.entropy is a one-line equivalent.

evalue.name: evalue
evalue.core_method: E-value for an estimate and a CI limit (VanderWeele & Ding 2017): RR + sqrt(RR(RR-1)). Converts OR (sqrt if common), HR ((1-0.5^sqrt(HR))/(1-0.5^sqrt(1/HR)) if common) and SMD (sqrt(exp(1.81 d))); supports a non-null true value.
evalue.oracle: EValue::evalues.RR, evalues.OR, evalues.HR, evalues.MD. evalues.MD uses exp(0.91 d), while this analysis uses sqrt(exp(1.81 d)) = exp(0.905 d), so SMD rows differ slightly by design.
evalue.gain: none: closed form, instant in R.

fragilityindex.name: fragilityindex
fragilityindex.core_method: Walsh fragility index: changes outcomes one patient at a time and recomputes Fisher's exact (or uncorrected chi-square) p until it crosses alpha; reverse FI for non-significant results, fragility quotient and trajectory table; accepts raw data or 2x2 counts.
fragilityindex.oracle: stats::fisher.test, stats::chisq.test(correct = FALSE); fragility::frag.study for the index
fragilityindex.gain: none: a short loop of exact tests that is instant in R.

gcomputation.name: gcomputation
gcomputation.core_method: Parametric g-formula: outcome glm (gaussian or logistic) on treatment + covariates (+ optional interactions), standardised counterfactual means E[Y(1)] and E[Y(0)], their difference and (binary) ratio, percentile bootstrap CIs.
gcomputation.oracle: stats::glm + stats::predict(type = 'response') averaged over the data (exact point estimates); stdReg::stdGlm or marginaleffects::avg_comparisons; bootstrap CI within MC error
gcomputation.gain: Little: a numpy IRLS bootstrap is faster than B glm refits, but R handles typical sizes. Needs model.matrix-style dummy coding of factors and interactions.

generalizedroc.name: generalizedroc
generalizedroc.core_method: Binormal ROC allowing unequal variances (AUC = Phi(a/sqrt(1+b^2))) after optional log/sqrt/'Box-Cox' transform (lambda picked from a 6-value grid by Shapiro p, not MLE). Also empirical and kernel ROC, Shapiro normality tests, median-Levene/Fligner/Bartlett variance tests and bootstrap/asymptotic CIs. The tram covariate-specific ROC paths return 0.75 placeholders.
generalizedroc.oracle: closed-form binormal AUC with stats::pnorm; stats::shapiro.test, stats::fligner.test, stats::bartlett.test, car::leveneTest(center = median); kernel ROC must pass R's bw.nrd0 to gaussian_kde (bw_method = h/sd); tram::Colr / tram::BoxCox for the covariate part
generalizedroc.gain: Removes tram for the non-covariate part, and scipy.stats.boxcox would give a proper MLE lambda (a deliberate behaviour change). The tram/covariate ROC has no Python equivalent (hard) and its placeholder outputs need fixing first.

greyzoneroc.name: greyzoneroc
greyzoneroc.core_method: stub/placeholder: the summary and boundary tables are filled with NA/placeholder rows; no grey-zone boundaries are computed.
greyzoneroc.oracle: pROC::coords(roc, 'all', ret = c('threshold','sensitivity','specificity')) for the threshold-wise operating points the boundary search uses (no standard CRAN grey-zone function)
greyzoneroc.gain: Nothing specific to Python; a real implementation is needed first. Grey zones are clinically relevant (HER2 2+, ASCUS, AI 40-60%). A two-threshold version (Se/Sp or LR targets) with a vectorised bootstrap of both boundaries would be a genuine addition.

icccoeff.name: icccoeff
icccoeff.core_method: ICC from one-way or two-way ANOVA mean squares (single/average, consistency/agreement; McGraw & Wong forms) with F-test and exact F-based CIs via irr::icc.
icccoeff.oracle: irr::icc(model =, type =, unit =) (value, Fvalue, df1, df2, p.value, lbound, ubound); psych::ICC as cross-check
icccoeff.gain: Removes irr from this analysis; no speed or capability gain. Listwise deletion must match irr.

idi.name: idi
idi.core_method: IDI = change in discrimination slope (mean risk in events minus non-events) between baseline and new risk, relative IDI, trimmed-mean variant, event/non-event decomposition, bootstrap (percentile/BCa) CIs and tests; subgroup analysis is a placeholder.
idi.oracle: Hmisc::improveProb (IDI with Pencina SE and z-test), PredictABEL::reclassification; boot::boot.ci(type = 'bca') within MC error (BCa acceleration estimates differ between boot and scipy)
idi.gain: Removes boot and vectorises the bootstrap; no new capability.

jpps.name: jpps
jpps.core_method: Predictive Power Score (ppsr): a cross-validated CART tree (rpart via parsnip) predicts the target from each predictor, and MAE/F1 is normalised against a naive baseline; PPS matrix and comparison with correlation.
needs: pandas (the original Python ppscore depends on both)
jpps.gain: none: PPS originated in Python (ppscore), but it needs scikit-learn and pandas, which jamovi's Python lacks, and a hand-written CART would not reproduce rpart.

latentbiomarker.name: latentbiomarker
latentbiomarker.core_method: CFA (lavaan::cfa, ML or ordinal/WLSMV indicators) for a latent biomarker, fit and modification indices, regression/Bartlett factor scores, Cox regression of the score with adjusters, PH test (cox.zph), KM by score strata.
latentbiomarker.gain: none: lavaan's estimators (WLSMV, robust fit indices) are the R ecosystem's strength.

leaveonecenterout.name: leaveonecenterout
leaveonecenterout.core_method: Leave-one-center-out CV: refits a logistic (default), linear or Cox model, optionally with LASSO via cv.glmnet, on all centres but one. Reports per-centre AUC with DeLong CI (or C-index / R2), calibration, pooled mean with t CI and between-centre SD.
leaveonecenterout.oracle: stats::glm, stats::lm, pROC::roc / pROC::ci.auc (DeLong), survival::coxph + survival::concordance, glmnet::cv.glmnet
leaveonecenterout.gain: Little: R refits are fast and there is no new capability. Only the default logistic/linear paths are portable; the LASSO (glmnet path) and Cox options are hard.

likelihoodratio.name: likelihoodratio
likelihoodratio.core_method: Dichotomises a continuous test at a Youden/cost/ROC01/concordance/manual cutpoint, then reports 2x2 Se/Sp, LR+/LR- with log-method (Simel) CIs, DOR, post-test probabilities over prevalence ranges and a stratified homogeneity chi-square. All five plots are 'Implementation needed' placeholders.
likelihoodratio.oracle: epiR::epi.tests (LR+/LR- with CIs), pROC::coords(best.method = 'youden'), closed-form log-LR SE (Simel 1991)

mageeequation.name: mageeequation
mageeequation.core_method: Magee equations 1-3 (linear combinations of Nottingham score/grade, mitoses, ER/PR H-score, HER2, tumour size, Ki-67) estimating the Oncotype DX recurrence score, risk categories by cut-offs, and agreement with the actual RS (correlation, category concordance).
mageeequation.oracle: published coefficients (Klein et al., Mod Pathol 2013) computed by hand; stats::cor / stats::cor.test
mageeequation.gain: none: plain arithmetic. A small, clinically useful pathology calculator and a good first port.

mendelianrandomization.name: mendelianrandomization
mendelianrandomization.core_method: Summary-data MR (MendelianRandomization): IVW fixed/random/multiplicative, MR-Egger with intercept pleiotropy test, weighted median (bootstrap SE), Cochran's Q heterogeneity, leave-one-out and single-SNP estimates. The four plot renderers are placeholders.
mendelianrandomization.oracle: MendelianRandomization::mr_ivw (model = 'fixed'/'random'), mr_egger, mr_median(weighting = 'weighted'); match package defaults (normal distribution, residual-SE floor of 1)
mendelianrandomization.gain: Drops MendelianRandomization, which has a large dependency tree (plotly, robustbase, quantreg, glmnet). IVW and Egger are weighted regressions; the weighted median is a vectorised parametric bootstrap.

methodcomparison.name: methodcomparison
methodcomparison.core_method: Bland-Altman bias and limits of agreement (parametric or nonparametric) with CIs and proportional-bias regression, Passing-Bablok and Deming regression (mcr::mcreg), Lin's CCC (DescTools::CCC), Pearson/Spearman correlation and clinical-limit agreement.
methodcomparison.oracle: mcr::mcreg(method.reg = 'PaBa' / 'Deming', method.ci =), DescTools::CCC (rho.c with Fisher-z CI), BlandAltmanLeh::bland.altman.stats
methodcomparison.gain: Removes mcr and DescTools; Passing-Bablok's O(n^2) pairwise slopes are fine in numpy. Must match mcr's CI methods. scipy.odr is deprecated in 1.17, so Deming should use the closed form.

methodvalidation.name: methodvalidation
methodvalidation.core_method: Partial stub: computes only mean/SD/CV% precision and bias% versus a reference per concentration level, with pass/fail limits. The EP05/EP15 nested-ANOVA precision, linearity, LoD/LoQ, uncertainty and reference-interval options are declared but not computed.
methodvalidation.oracle: base mean/sd for the current output; VCA::anovaVCA for the promised EP05 repeatability/within-lab variance components
methodvalidation.gain: None for the current code. What is missing, in either language, is EP05-A3/EP15-A3 variance components (balanced nested ANOVA with Satterthwaite df).

misclassificationbias.name: misclassificationbias
misclassificationbias.core_method: Simple bias analysis: back-corrects 2x2 exposure counts for nondifferential or differential Se/Sp, compares corrected with observed OR/RR/RD, runs an Se/Sp grid (range) analysis and gives multinomial-resampling simulation intervals for the corrected effect.
misclassificationbias.oracle: episensr::misclassification(type = 'exposure', bias_parms =) for corrected counts and OR/RR; simulation intervals within MC error
misclassificationbias.gain: Small: vectorised simulation and Se/Sp grids. Proper probabilistic bias analysis (Se/Sp drawn from beta priors) would be cheap to add.

modalitycomparison.name: modalitycomparison
modalitycomparison.core_method: Agreement between two scoring modalities (e.g. HER2-low IHC Null/Ultralow/1+): concordance %, unweighted/weighted Cohen's kappa (irr::kappa2), contingency table, direction of discordance with an exact binomial (sign) test, and a low-end category focus.
modalitycomparison.gain: Removes irr and can share a kappa helper with cohenskappa; no capability gain.

modelbuilder.name: modelbuilder
modelbuilder.core_method: Builds up to four nested logistic models with interactions, stepwise AIC/BIC, log/polynomial/rcs transforms, mean or multiple imputation (mice), LASSO/ridge/elastic-net (glmnet), train/test split, CV/bootstrap validation, AUC comparison, NRI/IDI and DCA export.
modelbuilder.oracle: stats::glm, stats::step, glmnet::cv.glmnet, mice::mice + mice::pool, rms::rcs, pROC::roc.test
modelbuilder.gain: none: its value is R's modelling ecosystem (mice, glmnet, rms).

modelval.name: modelval
modelval.core_method: External validation of existing predicted probabilities: calibration-in-the-large and calibration slope (logistic recalibration glm), Brier, AUC with DeLong CI, net benefit over a threshold range and subgroup calibration; a loess flexible calibration curve is drawn (plot only).
modelval.oracle: stats::glm(y ~ logit_p) and glm(y ~ offset(logit_p)) for slope and CITL, rms::val.prob, pROC::ci.auc (DeLong), dcurves::dca; R loess() is not reproducible exactly (plot only)
modelval.gain: Little: it shares IRLS, DeLong and net-benefit helpers with predmodel and bayesdca. The loess calibration curve must stay in R.

multiclassdiagnostics.name: multiclassdiagnostics
multiclassdiagnostics.core_method: Multi-class confusion matrix from predicted class labels: per-class Se/Sp/PPV/NPV/F1, accuracy with Wald CI, macro/weighted averages, Cohen's kappa (psych), per-class one-vs-rest 'AUC' from labels (which equals balanced accuracy), McNemar between two models. The DeLong path uses an alphabet-derived encoding (flagged).
multiclassdiagnostics.oracle: caret::confusionMatrix (byClass metrics, exact accuracy CI), psych::cohen.kappa, stats::mcnemar.test, pROC::auc
multiclassdiagnostics.gain: Removes psych/tidyr from this analysis; confusion-matrix arithmetic is trivial in numpy. No capability gain.

multiclassroc.name: multiclassroc
multiclassroc.core_method: Multi-class ROC from per-class score columns: one-vs-rest and one-vs-one AUCs, macro/weighted averages, bootstrap or 'simplified' DeLong CIs, pairwise comparisons and a confusion matrix. The 'multinomial' method is OvR relabelled, and micro-AUC is set equal to macro-AUC.
multiclassroc.oracle: pROC::multiclass.roc (Hand-Till OvO), pROC::roc + pROC::ci.auc (DeLong) per class; micro-average by pooling all class-score pairs, computed by hand
multiclassroc.gain: An honest micro-average and Hand-Till M come almost free from vectorised ranks; otherwise none.

netreclassification.name: netreclassification
netreclassification.core_method: Categorical NRI at user risk thresholds and category-free (continuous) NRI, event/non-event components, reclassification tables, BCa/percentile bootstrap CIs (boot) and AUC change. The subgroup analysis is a placeholder returning 0.1.
netreclassification.oracle: PredictABEL::reclassification (categorical NRI), Hmisc::improveProb (category-free NRI with SE), nricens::nribin; categories via digitize(right=True) to match cut(); boot::boot.ci within MC error
netreclassification.gain: Removes boot and vectorises the bootstrap; no new capability (fix the 0.1 placeholder first).

nonparametricregression.name: nonparametricregression
nonparametricregression.core_method: Partial stub: reports LOESS fit statistics (stats::loess R2, residual SE, effective df) or a univariate smoothing spline's lambda and GCV. Kernel, quantile, GAM and robust methods return 'not yet implemented', and the fitted-curve plots are stubs.
needs: statsmodels (lowess, KernelReg, QuantReg); even these do not reproduce stats::loess
nonparametricregression.gain: None: a curve-first analysis whose value is the fitted plot, which ClinicoPathPj cannot draw. Matching loess's kd-tree interpolation and smooth.spline's spar/df parametrisation means reimplementing them; quantile regression via linprog and kernel regression would be implementable.

ordinalroc.name: ordinalroc
ordinalroc.core_method: Ordinal AUC = concordance probability between the predictor and an ordered outcome (pairs in different categories), with bootstrap or naive Wald SE sqrt(A(1-A)/n) and a z-test. Category-specific cumulative AUCs, the proportional-odds test, polr coefficients and optimal thresholds are unimplemented stubs.
