ordinalroc.oracle: survival::concordance(ordinal_outcome ~ predictor) (C and IJ variance), pROC::auc per cumulative split, MASS::polr(Hess = TRUE)
ordinalroc.gain: Nothing specific to Python; the real work is finishing the stubbed helpers (cumulative-split AUCs take a few lines with rank statistics) and replacing the naive SE.

ppv.name: ppv
ppv.core_method: Calculator: Ioannidis (2005) positive predictive value and false discovery rate of a claimed finding, from the prior share of true hypotheses, alpha, power and bias u (p-hacking); percentages table plus a 500-study dot plot.
ppv.oracle: closed form PPV = ((1-beta)R + u*beta*R) / (R + alpha - beta*R + u - u*alpha + u*beta*R) (Ioannidis 2005); existing ppv() output
ppv.gain: none: plain arithmetic, and the dot plot (the main visual) would stay in R.

prauc.name: prauc
prauc.core_method: Precision-recall curve and PR-AUC by trapezoidal integration, F-beta scores and the F-optimal threshold, bootstrap SE/CI, prevalence-baseline comparison and ROC-AUC comparison.
prauc.oracle: PRROC::pr.curve (auc.integral, auc.davis.goadrich), precrec::evalmod; average precision by hand. Linear trapezoids between PR points are optimistic versus Davis-Goadrich interpolation.
prauc.gain: A vectorised bootstrap; otherwise none. It overlaps precisionrecall, so consolidate the two into one analysis before porting.

precisionrecall.name: precisionrecall
precisionrecall.core_method: Precision-recall curve with trapezoid or average-precision area, prevalence baseline, bootstrap percentile CI, a paired permutation test comparing two scores (random within-row swaps), plus F-score and ROC panels.
precisionrecall.oracle: PRROC::pr.curve, precrec::evalmod; average precision = sum(diff(recall) * precision) by hand; permutation p within MC error
precisionrecall.gain: Vectorised permutation and bootstrap. Same estimand as prauc: merge the two.

predmodel.name: predmodel
predmodel.core_method: Logistic prediction model (optional stepwise selection): coefficient table, Hosmer-Lemeshow test, AUC with DeLong CI, Brier, calibration (loess plot), risk groups at cut-offs, and bootstrap optimism correction (hard-capped at 50 replicates whatever nBootstrap says) or k-fold CV.
predmodel.oracle: stats::glm, stats::step (AIC), pROC::ci.auc, ResourceSelection::hoslem.test (g = 10), rms::validate (bootstrap optimism)
predmodel.gain: Speed: numpy IRLS makes the full requested bootstrap affordable; the R code caps it at 50 'for performance'. Stepwise selection and HL decile grouping must reproduce R's step/quantile tie rules.

roc2d.name: roc2d
roc2d.core_method: Per-marker empirical AUC with DeLong CI and Youden cut-off (pROC); AUCs of min/max/mean/product scores on min-max-scaled markers (the 'OR (Max)' and 'Maximum' rows are the same pmax rule); 21-point grid search for the convex weight w*M1+(1-w)*M2 maximising AUC. The 2D ROC surface and threshold-region plots are TODO stubs
roc2d.oracle: pROC::roc (direction = 'auto' flips the direction so AUC >= 0.5, and the port must do the same), pROC::auc, pROC::ci.auc (method = 'delong'), pROC::coords(x = 'best', best.method = 'youden')
roc2d.gain: A real two-threshold AND/OR search over all (t1, t2) pairs, vectorised in numpy, plus bootstrap optimism correction for the data-optimised combination AUC (R reports it uncorrected)

rocreg.name: rocreg
rocreg.core_method: Not ROC regression: stratified AUC per covariate level (pROC DeLong CI, SE back-derived from the CI width, Hanley-McNeil fallback), inverse-variance pooled AUC and a Cochran Q heterogeneity chi-square. Adjusted AUC, covariate effects, bootstrap and all plots are unimplemented (partial stub)
rocreg.oracle: pROC::roc, pROC::ci.auc (DeLong), stats::pchisq for Q; for a genuine covariate-adjusted ROC, ROCnReg::AROC.sp
rocreg.gain: Could deliver the covariate-adjusted ROC that R only advertises: Janes-Pepe AROC (linear model of the marker in non-diseased cases, placement values for diseased cases) with bootstrap CIs, in a few dozen numpy lines (about M effort with that addition)

screeningcalculator.name: screeningcalculator
screeningcalculator.core_method: Bayes-theorem calculator from entered Se/Sp/prevalence (no data): PPV, NPV, LR+/LR-, post-test probabilities for 2-3 sequential tests, a Fagan nomogram plot, and Buderer-type sample size n = z^2 p(1-p)/(w/2)^2 inflated by prevalence
screeningcalculator.oracle: Closed-form Bayes and Buderer formulas, cross-checked against the current R screeningcalculator output
screeningcalculator.gain: none (closed-form calculator; the only extra is the Fagan plot, which still needs R)

segmentationmetrics.name: segmentationmetrics
segmentationmetrics.core_method: Per-image confusion counts from per-pixel label columns: Dice, IoU, volumetric similarity, Se/Sp. 'Hausdorff', HD95, ASSD and surface Dice use 1-D boundary positions in row order, not true 2D/3D geometry. Also multiclass macro/weighted averages, instance IoU matching, normal or percentile-bootstrap CI of the mean, paired t-test/Wilcoxon method comparison, IQR/z outliers
segmentationmetrics.oracle: Closed-form Dice/IoU on counts; stats::t.test(paired = TRUE), stats::wilcox.test(paired = TRUE), stats::quantile(type = 7); for true 2D Hausdorff, a brute-force base-R minimum distance over pixel coordinates
segmentationmetrics.gain: True 2D/3D Hausdorff, HD95 and surface distances via distance_transform_edt/directed_hausdorff when x/y pixel coordinates are supplied, replacing the 1-D row-order proxy; also much faster on million-pixel masks

spikeslabpriors.name: spikeslabpriors
spikeslabpriors.core_method: Bayesian spike-and-slab variable selection by MCMC (BoomSpikeSlab lm.spike / logit.spike / probit.spike / poisson.spike): posterior inclusion probabilities, posterior coefficient summaries, inclusion Bayes factor versus prior odds
spikeslabpriors.oracle: BoomSpikeSlab::lm.spike, logit.spike, probit.spike, poisson.spike; agreement is possible only within Monte Carlo error because the RNG differs. For the Gaussian model, exact PIPs by enumerating all models under the same conjugate prior
spikeslabpriors.gain: For the linear model with up to about 15-20 predictors, exact (enumerated) posterior inclusion probabilities with no MCMC noise; otherwise none (the samplers would be own Gibbs/data-augmentation code)

survivalPower.name: survivalPower
survivalPower.core_method: Log-rank/Cox survival power, sample size, detectable HR and study duration: Schoenfeld events with Lachin-Foulkes event probabilities (uniform accrual, exponential dropout, uniroot solves), non-inferiority, multi-arm disjunctive power (1-D integral over equicorrelated normals), group-sequential designs via gsDesign (gsSurv, gsSurvPower, gsProbability; Lan-DeMets OBF/Pocock), and Monte Carlo trial simulation with survdiff plus a Clopper-Pearson CI
survivalPower.oracle: Closed-form Schoenfeld/Lachin-Foulkes for the fixed design; gsDesign::gsSurv, gsDesign::gsSurvPower, gsDesign::gsProbability, gsDesign::gsDesign (sfLDOF/sfLDPocock), survival::survdiff, stats::binom.test
survivalPower.gain: A vectorised numpy log-rank over all simulated trials would run 10^4-10^5 Monte Carlo trials in seconds; the R loop of one survdiff per trial takes about 6 s at the default 2000 runs and 10-60 s at higher counts. The fixed-design parts are easy, but the group-sequential boundaries need a port of gsDesign's recursive numerical integration

timedependentdca.name: timedependentdca
timedependentdca.core_method: Survival decision curve at chosen time points. Risk comes from a direct probability column, from KM within predictor quantile strata, or from a one-covariate Cox model (survfit.coxph). Net benefit uses KM in the high-risk group (Vickers 2008), with treat-all/none, interventions avoided, optional loess smoothing and bootstrap CIs; no IPCW
timedependentdca.oracle: survival::survfit, survival::coxph(ties = 'efron') with the survfit.coxph baseline, dcurves::dca(Surv(time, event) ~ x, time = t) for the net-benefit formula, stats::loess
timedependentdca.gain: Vectorised bootstrap (R refits survfit/coxph in every replicate) and a proper IPCW net-benefit option, which the R notice says is missing. Caveat: R's loess (interpolated surface) has no scipy equivalent, so smoothing must be re-implemented or dropped

treeadvanced.name: treeadvanced
treeadvanced.core_method: CART (rpart) with cp tuning and pruning (1-SE rule, minimum xerror), Boruta / caret RFE / random-forest feature selection, holdout/CV/bootstrap validation, confusion-matrix metrics with CIs, pROC AUC, variable importance, and rpart.plot/parttree plots
treeadvanced.oracle: rpart::rpart, rpart::prune, randomForest::randomForest, Boruta::Boruta, caret::rfe, pROC::roc
treeadvanced.gain: none (sklearn's CART differs from rpart, with no surrogate splits and no cp/xerror table; RF, Boruta and xerror CV are RNG-bound, so R results cannot be matched; the tree plots stay in R)

treecompare.name: treecompare
treecompare.core_method: Benchmark of CART (rpart), conditional inference tree (party::ctree), random forest, gbm and xgboost under CV/holdout/bootstrap: accuracy, balanced accuracy, AUC, Se/Sp, F1 and timing; pairwise paired t-tests/McNemar with p.adjust; ranking table
treecompare.oracle: rpart::rpart, party::ctree, randomForest::randomForest, gbm::gbm, xgboost::xgboost, pROC::auc, stats::mcnemar.test, stats::p.adjust
treecompare.gain: none (five R learners have no bundled Python equivalent, and ctree has none in Python at all)

treeensemble.name: treeensemble
treeensemble.core_method: Random-forest classification (randomForest) with mtry options, holdout/CV, OOB error curve, confusion-matrix metrics with CIs, Gini/permutation importance
treeensemble.gain: none (forest results are RNG-bound and cannot be matched to R)

treemedical.name: treemedical
treemedical.core_method: Single CART decision tree (rpart, Gini, cp pruning) with holdout/CV validation, confusion-matrix metrics with CIs, AUC (pROC), variable importance; the tree diagram (rpart.plot/parttree) is a main output
treemedical.gain: none (a CART identical to rpart, with surrogates and xerror pruning, is a large rewrite, and the tree plot needs R)

trichotomousroc.name: trichotomousroc
trichotomousroc.core_method: Three-class ordinal ROC: two-threshold search maximising the mean class-correct rate (generalised Youden; grid capped at 100 quantile cut-offs), or tertile/fixed thresholds; 3x3 classification; empirical VUS = P(X_neg < X_ind < X_pos) with strict inequalities (ties not half-weighted). The VUS bootstrap CI and all four plots are stubs
trichotomousroc.oracle: Brute-force base-R VUS over expand.grid of all triples; the existing R grid search for the thresholds
trichotomousroc.gain: Exhaustive threshold search over all cut-offs using cumulative sums (R caps at 100 quantiles), a tie-consistent VUS shared with vusanalysis, and the missing bootstrap CI

vusanalysis.name: vusanalysis
vusanalysis.core_method: Empirical VUS for k ordered classes (dynamic program with ties half-weighted), pairwise Mann-Whitney AUCs with bootstrap CIs/tests, percentile-bootstrap CI and SE of VUS, a bootstrap z-test against chance 1/k!, stratified VUS. Plots are stubs; covariate adjustment is unimplemented
vusanalysis.oracle: Brute-force base-R VUS over all class tuples; pROC::auc or stats::wilcox.test statistic/(n1*n2) for the pairwise AUCs
vusanalysis.gain: A vectorised O(n log n) VUS makes 2000-replicate bootstraps fast (R runs an O(n^2) vapply in every replicate); a port could add the Nakas-Yiannoutsos analytic VUS variance

diagnosticmeta.name: diagnosticmeta
diagnosticmeta.core_method: DTA meta-analysis. Reitsma bivariate random-effects model (mada::reitsma REML/ML/fixed) gives summary Se/Sp, LRs, DOR and the SROC (mada::sroc); also PHM SROC (mada::phm), univariate logit Se/Sp heterogeneity (metafor::rma: tau^2, I^2, Q), moderator meta-regression, Deeks funnel test (weighted lm on 1/sqrt(ESS)), continuity corrections and Wilson study CIs
diagnosticmeta.oracle: mada::reitsma, mada::sroc, mada::phm, metafor::rma (REML; tau2, I2, QE), stats::lm(weights = ESS) for the Deeks test
diagnosticmeta.gain: none (shipped and checked against mada/metafor; a port would only re-derive the same REML fits)

ihcheterogeneity.name: ihcheterogeneity
ihcheterogeneity.core_method: Biopsy-vs-whole-section reproducibility: ICC from mean squares with F-based CIs, robust/RMS CV, Bland-Altman bias and limits of agreement (t CIs), Spearman with Fisher-z CI, one-way variance components, ICC-precision sample-size planning (integrate/uniroot), Kruskal-Wallis across spatial compartments
ihcheterogeneity.oracle: psych::ICC (ICC1/ICC2/ICC3 with F CIs), stats::cor.test(method = 'spearman'), stats::t.test, stats::kruskal.test, stats::aov

swimmerplot.name: swimmerplot
swimmerplot.core_method: plot only: ggswim swimmer lanes with event markers. Side tables give person-time, milestone/event counts and medians, reverse-KM follow-up, response rates with Clopper-Pearson CIs, and a Fisher group test
swimmerplot.gain: none (the value is the ggswim figure, which ClinicoPathPj cannot draw)

waterfall.name: waterfall
waterfall.core_method: plot first: waterfall and spider plots of best % change. Tables give RECIST category counts, ORR/DCR with Clopper-Pearson CIs, person-time, a Fisher exact OR between groups, KM duration of response and reverse-KM follow-up
waterfall.gain: none (shipped, and the plots are the product)

aeplot.name: aeplot
aeplot.core_method: plot only: butterfly bar chart of adverse-event frequencies by arm (all-grade vs high-grade); no inferential statistics
aeplot.oracle: none (a ggplot2 figure; counts via base::table)

biomarkerresponse.name: biomarkerresponse
biomarkerresponse.core_method: Biomarker vs response: ROC AUC with DeLong CI, Youden optimal threshold with bootstrap CI (pROC), threshold Se/Sp/PPV/NPV; Welch t-test, Wilcoxon with Hodges-Lehmann CI, Cliff's delta; ANOVA with Tukey HSD, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn (FSA); Pearson/Spearman for a continuous response; scatter/box plot
biomarkerresponse.oracle: pROC::roc, pROC::ci.auc, pROC::coords('best'), stats::t.test, stats::wilcox.test(conf.int = TRUE), stats::aov + stats::TukeyHSD, stats::kruskal.test, FSA::dunnTest, stats::cor.test
biomarkerresponse.gain: none beyond dropping FSA/pROC (DeLong, Dunn and the Hodges-Lehmann interval are short own code); the plot stays in R

circos.name: circos
circos.core_method: plot only: circlize chord diagram of from/to flows or a matrix

classification.name: classification
classification.core_method: mlr3 supervised classification (rpart, ranger random forest, kknn, naive Bayes, logistic regression, SVM) with train/holdout/CV, up/down-sampling or SMOTE, confusion matrix, Se/Sp/PPV/NPV, AUC (pROC) and bootstrap CIs (boot)
classification.oracle: mlr3 learners classif.rpart / classif.ranger / classif.kknn / classif.naive_bayes / classif.svm plus the logistic learner, pROC::roc, boot::boot.ci
classification.gain: none (scikit-learn is not bundled; learners and resampling are RNG-bound, so R results cannot be matched)

clinicalcalculators.name: clinicalcalculators
clinicalcalculators.core_method: Mostly a stub: a logistic regression (glm, optional stepwise AIC via step()) or Cox regression (coxph) coefficient/OR/HR table after mean/mode imputation. About 30 options (nomogram, calibration, DCA, validation, 6 of 8 model types) do nothing
clinicalcalculators.gain: none (finish the analysis in R first; porting a stub adds nothing)

clinicalheatmap.name: clinicalheatmap
clinicalheatmap.core_method: plot first: tidyheatmaps clinical heatmap with hierarchical/k-means clustering and silhouette. Extras: log-rank of clusters vs survival, and ANOVA/chi-square/Fisher associations of annotations with clusters
clinicalheatmap.oracle: stats::hclust, stats::cutree, stats::kmeans, cluster::silhouette, survival::survdiff, stats::chisq.test, stats::fisher.test

condsurvival.name: condsurvival
condsurvival.core_method: Conditional survival CS(t|s) = S(s+t)/S(s). It uses KM per group (the Fleming-Harrington choice still fits KM) or intercept-only parametric fits (flexsurvreg/survreg: Weibull, exponential, lognormal, log-logistic). The CI is the ratio of opposite pointwise bounds: labelled delta method, but not valid. Also landmark KM and log-rank
condsurvival.oracle: survival::survfit(conf.type = 'log'), flexsurv::flexsurvreg / survival::survreg(~ 1) for point estimates (flexsurv summary CIs are simulation-based), survival::survdiff
condsurvival.gain: A correct CS interval (Greenwood variance accumulated over (s, s+t] only, on the log or log-log scale) and real Fleming-Harrington estimates; censored MLE is built into scipy.stats fit()

consortdiagram.name: consortdiagram
consortdiagram.core_method: plot only: CONSORT flow diagram (consort::consort_plot) from per-participant exclusion columns; counting only

ctdnadynamics.name: ctdnadynamics
ctdnadynamics.core_method: Paired ctDNA VAF: log2 fold-change, per-time clearance rate, cleared/persistent (MRD) classification at a detection threshold, landmark log-rank and a single-covariate Cox HR (Wald CI) by MRD status

curemodels.name: curemodels
curemodels.core_method: Cure models: semiparametric mixture cure (smcure: EM with PH/AFT latency, bootstrap SEs), parametric mixture/non-mixture cure (flexsurvcure), nonparametric cure probability (npcure::probcure) and relative-survival cure with background hazard (cuRe::fit.cure.model); reverse-KM follow-up checks and sensitivity refits
curemodels.gain: none (four specialised R engines; only the parametric mixture cure is a short scipy likelihood)

dendrogram.name: dendrogram
dendrogram.core_method: plot first: hierarchical clustering (dist + hclust, cutree) drawn as base, dendextend, ggraph or ComplexHeatmap dendrograms

digitalvalidation.name: digitalvalidation
digitalvalidation.core_method: Digital vs reference method agreement: Pearson/Spearman correlation; ICC (psych::ICC row 6, which is ICC3k average-measures, although labelled ICC(3,1)); Lin's CCC with z-transform CI (epiR::epi.ccc); Bland-Altman bias (paired t-test) and proportional bias (lm of difference on mean); Cohen's kappa at decision thresholds. The bootstrap_ci option is not implemented
digitalvalidation.oracle: psych::ICC, epiR::epi.ccc(ci = 'z-transform'), psych::cohen.kappa, stats::cor.test, stats::t.test(paired = TRUE), stats::lm
digitalvalidation.gain: The advertised bootstrap CIs, removal of the psych/epiR dependencies, and a chance to fix the ICC single-vs-average mix-up; small effort

explainableai.name: explainableai
explainableai.core_method: Mostly placeholder: random-forest importance (randomForest) and GLM-based permutation importance are real, but SHAP, LIME, partial-dependence and fallback importance values are fabricated with runif()/rnorm(); real SHAP/LIME would need Python shap/lime via reticulate
explainableai.oracle: randomForest::randomForest / randomForest::importance, stats::glm with manual permutation; the SHAP/LIME rows have no oracle because R fabricates them
explainableai.gain: Exact Shapley values for linear/logistic models take a few numpy lines (phi_j = beta_j * (x_j - mean x_j)) and would replace fabricated numbers; tree/kernel SHAP and LIME need packages that jamovi's Python lacks

functionalsampling.name: functionalsampling
functionalsampling.core_method: Rare-event spatial analysis on cell coordinates: nearest-neighbour distance from each rare event to any other cell; Clark-Evans ratio using the rare-event density, a bounding-box area and no edge correction (z-test); and a rule-based 'catalyst function' verdict (frequency, randomness, NND CV < 30%)
functionalsampling.gain: cKDTree makes NND O(n log n) for whole-slide detections (R loops over all cells for each rare event). A Monte Carlo CSR test with edge correction would fix the current z-test, which mixes rare-to-any-cell distances with the rare-event density

geemodel.name: geemodel
geemodel.core_method: GEE (geepack::geeglm) for gaussian/binomial/poisson/Gamma with independence/exchangeable/AR1/unstructured working correlation, robust sandwich SEs, QIC, and emmeans post-hoc contrasts with p-adjustment
geemodel.gain: none (statsmodels GEE is not bundled, and matching geepack's correlation/scale estimators plus emmeans would be a large own implementation)

gsdesign.name: gsdesign
gsdesign.core_method: Group-sequential design: efficacy/futility boundaries with Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming/Pocock/Hwang-Shih-DeCani spending (gsDesign), survival sample size (gsSurv), binary endpoints (nBinomial), continuous endpoints, and non-proportional hazards via average hazard ratio (gsDesign2::gs_design_ahr)
gsdesign.gain: none (gsDesign's recursive-integration boundary engine and gsDesign2's AHR design would have to be rewritten, and trial statisticians expect the gsDesign numbers)

haralicktexture.name: haralicktexture
haralicktexture.core_method: Analysis of pre-computed texture-feature columns; no GLCM/Haralick features are computed from images. Covers descriptives with moments skewness/kurtosis, a correlation matrix and filter, Shapiro-Wilk, IQR/z outliers, CV, Welch t-test between groups, per-feature AUC (pROC), an ad-hoc 'Moran's I' (weights 1/(1+d), clipped to [-1, 1]) and local CV
haralicktexture.oracle: moments::skewness / moments::kurtosis (match scipy skew(bias=True) and kurtosis(fisher=False, bias=True)), stats::shapiro.test, stats::cor.test, stats::t.test, pROC::auc, ape::Moran.I with the same weight matrix
haralicktexture.gain: Vectorised pdist replaces the O(n^2) interpreted double loop, and a standard Moran's I with a permutation p-value replaces the clipped approximation

hematologicindices.name: hematologicindices
hematologicindices.core_method: Inflammation indices from blood counts (NLR, PLR, LMR, SII, PNI, CAR, GPS/mGPS) with a median/IQR table. One index is split at the median or at a log-rank-maximising cut (20-80% quantile grid; the p-value is not corrected for the search), then KM medians, log-rank and a Cox HR for the binary split
hematologicindices.oracle: survival::survfit (median), survival::survdiff, survival::coxph; maxstat::maxstat.test for a selection-corrected cut-point p-value
hematologicindices.gain: A permutation-corrected p-value for the data-driven cut point (permuting over the whole search); the R p-value is optimistic

hierarchicalpathology.name: hierarchicalpathology
hierarchicalpathology.core_method: Nested random-intercept models (e.g. patient/slide/region) via lme4::lmer, lme4::glmer (binomial, poisson) or glmmTMB negative binomial; variance components, level-specific ICCs, model comparison and diagnostics
hierarchicalpathology.gain: none (statsmodels MixedLM would cover only the Gaussian case; Laplace GLMMs and NB2 have no bundled equivalent)

ihcadvanced.name: ihcadvanced
ihcadvanced.core_method: IHC marker clustering: k-means with optimal k by elbow, silhouette or gap statistic (cluster::clusGap); PCA (prcomp); iterative marker selection; bootstrap consensus clustering (parallel::mclapply); silhouette validation
ihcadvanced.oracle: stats::kmeans (fixed centres, algorithm = 'Lloyd' to match kmeans2), cluster::silhouette, cluster::clusGap, stats::prcomp. Partitions match only up to label permutation; RNG-bound parts can be compared only distributionally
ihcadvanced.gain: Vectorised consensus and gap-statistic resampling without parallel::mclapply, which forks and does not parallelise on Windows

ihcbasic.name: ihcbasic
ihcbasic.core_method: IHC scoring (standard, binary or H-score) and case clustering: Gower or Jaccard distance (cluster::daisy), hierarchical clustering (ward.D2/complete/average), k-means or PAM, silhouette, per-cluster marker summaries and Kruskal-Wallis
ihcbasic.oracle: cluster::daisy(metric = 'gower'), stats::hclust (scipy 'ward' on distances = R 'ward.D2'), stats::cutree, cluster::pam, cluster::silhouette, stats::kruskal.test
ihcbasic.gain: none (Gower and PAM need own code, while R's cluster package is fast and already a dependency)

ihccluster.name: ihccluster
ihccluster.core_method: Large mixed-type IHC clustering workflow: Gower/Jaccard/Hamming distances; PAM, hierarchical, k-means or MCA (FactoMineR); automatic k by silhouette; bootstrap consensus; split-half reproducibility (kappa); marker importance (Kruskal epsilon^2, Cramer's V, chi-square/Fisher); marker clustering by mutual information; diagnostic panel metrics; compartment concordance; heatmap, PCA/MCA and KM plots
ihccluster.oracle: cluster::daisy, cluster::pam, stats::hclust, stats::kmeans, cluster::silhouette, FactoMineR::MCA, stats::chisq.test, stats::fisher.test, stats::kruskal.test
ihccluster.gain: none for clinicians: the numerics already run in R and the heatmaps would still need R. The only gain is dropping FactoMineR/ComplexHeatmap for the numerical part

ihcdiagnostic.name: ihcdiagnostic
ihcdiagnostic.core_method: Per-marker diagnostic performance (trapezoidal AUC; optimal, clinical or median cut-points; Se/Sp/PPV/NPV with CIs; optional CV). Differential diagnosis clusters cases (PAM or hierarchical on Gower), maps clusters to diagnoses and scores 'confidence' by centroid distance. A greedy antibody-panel search covers top-marker pairs/triples
ihcdiagnostic.oracle: pROC::auc (the trapezoidal AUC equals the Mann-Whitney AUC), cluster::daisy, cluster::pam, stats::hclust, stats::binom.test
ihcdiagnostic.gain: none (an exhaustive panel search over all marker subsets would be the only speed gain)

ihcimmune.name: ihcimmune
ihcimmune.core_method: Immune-infiltrate scoring: TIL, Sterlacci and granzyme rules, immune-contexture categories, PD-1/PD-L1/CD8 checkpoint scores. Moran's I uses row-standardised 1/(d+1) weights and a normal z-test; above 1000 cells it uses an unseeded random 500-cell subsample. Also clustering index, NND, quartile hot/cold spots, and Shannon/Simpson/Brillouin/Berger-Parker diversity
ihcimmune.oracle: ape::Moran.I (same weight matrix), vegan::diversity (shannon, simpson), spatstat.explore::clarkevans; the TIL/contexture rules can only be checked against the existing R output
ihcimmune.gain: Moran's I on all cells with sparse k-NN weights (cKDTree) and a permutation p-value, replacing the unseeded 500-cell subsample that makes the R result change between runs on whole-slide data

ihcpredict.name: ihcpredict
ihcpredict.core_method: Heuristic diagnosis prediction for new cases from a training CSV: rule-based panels, nearest-centroid distance, cluster or hybrid scoring. 'Confidence' is a normalised 1/(1+d), not a calibrated probability. Also alternatives, evidence and low-confidence flags
ihcpredict.oracle: Only the existing R ihcpredict output (no external reference method)
ihcpredict.gain: none (a port would copy the heuristic; a calibrated multinomial model would be a new analysis)

ihcscoring.name: ihcscoring
ihcscoring.core_method: IHC score standardisation: H-score, Allred and binary/percentage scores; agreement between methods (psych::ICC, kappa, Bland-Altman); distribution and QC metrics; optimal cut-points (cutpointr Youden, maxstat with log-rank for survival); multiple-cut-off and CPS analysis; rule-based molecular subtyping and checkpoint tests (chi-square/Fisher/Kruskal). The 'automated' StarDist/colour-deconvolution mode shows simulated values (runif/rnorm)
ihcscoring.oracle: psych::ICC, cutpointr::cutpointr (maximize_metric, metric = youden), maxstat::maxstat.test, survival::survdiff, stats::chisq.test, stats::fisher.test, stats::kruskal.test
ihcscoring.gain: none for the scoring statistics; real nucleus segmentation would suit Python but needs stardist/tensorflow, which jamovi's Python lacks

ihcsurvival.name: ihcsurvival
ihcsurvival.core_method: Prognostic IHC survival: univariable Cox per marker with FDR adjustment, Gower + Ward.D2 prognostic clustering, risk-group Cox and KM/log-rank, multivariable Cox, cox.zph PH test, central vs invasive-front comparison, landmark survival
ihcsurvival.oracle: survival::coxph, survival::cox.zph, survival::survfit, survival::survdiff, cluster::daisy, stats::hclust(method = 'ward.D2'), stats::p.adjust
ihcsurvival.gain: none (survival is the reference implementation, and several Cox fits plus cox.zph would have to be re-implemented)

ihcthreshold.name: ihcthreshold
ihcthreshold.core_method: Descriptive only: per-threshold mean, SD, CV and range of the positive-cell ratio across sample areas. The 'optimal' threshold is the minimum CV, minimum SD or maximum 1/(1+CV); the last always equals minimum CV
ihcthreshold.oracle: Base R mean/sd (n-1 denominator) per threshold

irecist.name: irecist
irecist.core_method: Rule-based iRECIST classification of longitudinal lesion sums (baseline/nadir, iUPD to iCPD confirmation windows, pseudoprogression), best overall response, and ORR/DCR/pseudoprogression rates with Clopper-Pearson CIs; waterfall/swimmer/spider plots
irecist.oracle: stats::binom.test; the response rules can only be checked against the existing R output
irecist.gain: none (a rule engine plus plots; the only statistic is an exact binomial CI)

jjoncoplot.name: jjoncoplot
jjoncoplot.core_method: plot first: oncoplot, mutation-frequency and co-occurrence displays of a genomic alteration matrix with a TMB panel; pairwise Fisher co-occurrence/mutual-exclusivity tests with p.adjust

lymphnoderatio.name: lymphnoderatio
lymphnoderatio.core_method: Lymph node ratio (positive/examined, minimum-yield filter) and summary table. Strata come from fixed cut-offs or a log-rank-maximising cut (15-85% quantile grid, uncorrected p); then KM, log-rank and Cox HR per stratum
lymphnoderatio.oracle: survival::survfit, survival::survdiff (k groups; scipy.stats.logrank is two-sample only), survival::coxph; maxstat::maxstat.test for a corrected optimal-cut p-value
lymphnoderatio.gain: A selection-corrected p-value for the data-driven cut; LODDS could be added in one line

metaanalysis.name: metaanalysis
metaanalysis.core_method: Generic meta-analysis with metafor::rma (FE plus REML/DL and other tau^2 estimators, Knapp-Hartung), prediction interval, Egger (regtest), Begg (ranktest), trim-and-fill, leave-one-out and influence diagnostics, subgroup analysis and meta-regression; DTA branch via mada::reitsma; forest/funnel plots
metaanalysis.oracle: metafor::rma, metafor::regtest, metafor::ranktest, metafor::trimfill, metafor::leave1out, metafor::influence, mada::reitsma
metaanalysis.gain: none (metafor is the reference implementation, and the plots stay in R)

mlpathology.name: mlpathology
mlpathology.core_method: Confusion-matrix metrics (accuracy with exact binomial CI, kappa, sens/spec/PPV/NPV, F1, MCC, macro-F1), ROC AUC with DeLong CI and Youden cut, Dice/Jaccard for binary masks, McNemar and DeLong tests comparing two models; the bootstrap_validation toggle is declared but never read
mlpathology.oracle: caret::confusionMatrix; pROC::roc, pROC::ci.auc (DeLong), pROC::coords('best', Youden), pROC::roc.test (DeLong); stats::mcnemar.test
mlpathology.gain: Removes caret, a very heavy dependency. Case-resampling in numpy makes the declared but unwired bootstrap CIs cheap for every metric. An HTML/D3 ROC with a threshold slider and a live confusion matrix would be a real usability gain.

modelperformance.name: modelperformance
modelperformance.core_method: Fits up to 5 covariate sets as Cox PH (the default), logistic or linear models and compares AIC/BIC, log-likelihood, Nagelkerke R2, Harrell C or ROC AUC, and MCC. The cross-validation table reports hard-coded placeholder fold scores (0.7/0.75/0.8) and the calibration plot does nothing.
needs: statsmodels (PHReg with efron ties, GLM), or an own Efron-ties Cox engine plus IRLS
modelperformance.oracle: survival::coxph (ties='efron') + summary()$concordance; stats::glm(family=binomial); stats::lm; stats::AIC/BIC/logLik; DescTools::PseudoR2(which='Nagelkerke'); pROC::auc
modelperformance.gain: Nothing beyond R itself. Any port must replace the fabricated CV scores with real fold refits; once a Cox/IRLS engine exists, numpy makes repeated k-fold refits cheap.

multifocalconcordance.name: multifocalconcordance
multifocalconcordance.core_method: Per marker: the proportion of cases whose foci all share one value, and Cohen's kappa computed by hand for two-focus designs. Also counts case-level patterns (fully/partially concordant, discordant) and the gain/loss direction for binary markers.
multifocalconcordance.oracle: irr::kappa2 (unweighted) for kappa; base R table()/split() counts reproduced from the module
multifocalconcordance.gain: Minor. Exact Clopper-Pearson CIs for the concordance rates, and a kappa SE/CI, are one call each and are missing in R.

multiplexanalysis.name: multiplexanalysis
multiplexanalysis.core_method: Marker descriptives, pairwise Pearson/Spearman with p-adjustment, k-means phenotyping (elbow-chosen k, hard-coded seed 42), scaled PCA, Shannon diversity, and fixed-radius cell-proximity counts from a full distance matrix. The immune-contexture, diversity, QC/batch, network and pathway tables are declared but never filled.
multiplexanalysis.oracle: stats::cor.test, stats::p.adjust, stats::prcomp(scale.=TRUE), vegan::diversity(index='shannon'); stats::kmeans matches only up to label permutation and local optimum (Hartigan-Wong vs Lloyd)
multiplexanalysis.gain: KD-tree neighbour counting replaces R's O(n^2) dist() matrix, which is infeasible at whole-slide cell counts. Removes vegan.

optimalcutpoint.name: optimalcutpoint
optimalcutpoint.core_method: Binary outcome: ROC cutpoint maximising Youden, closest-to-top-left or ROC01 (cutpointr, optional bootstrap). Survival outcome: maximally selected log-rank statistic (maxstat; HL or exactGauss p, optional permutation p), median/tertile/quartile splits with log-rank and Cox HR. Continuous outcome: maximum-correlation split.
optimalcutpoint.gain: The permutation null is vectorised (R refits maxstat nperm=2000 times), as is the cutpoint bootstrap, so both finish in seconds. Python can also return the whole statistic-vs-cutpoint curve for an interactive slider showing sens/spec/HR/log-rank at any cut, which makes the optimism of a data-driven cut visible.

pathagreement.name: pathagreement
pathagreement.core_method: Inter-rater reliability: Cohen (weighted) and Fleiss/Conger kappa, Krippendorff alpha, Gwet AC1, Brennan-Prediger, PABAK, ICC, bootstrap CIs, and kappaSize sample-size planning. Also rater-bias and per-category tests, hierarchical clustering of rater styles with silhouette, and a reader-accuracy workflow against a reference standard.
pathagreement.oracle: irr::kappa2, irr::kappam.fleiss(exact=), irr::kripp.alpha; irrCAC::gwet.ac1.raw, bp.coeff.raw, fleiss.kappa.raw, conger.kappa.raw; psych::ICC, psych::cohen.kappa; vcd::Kappa; kappaSize::CIBinary/CI3Cats-CI5Cats; cluster::silhouette
pathagreement.gain: Removes about 8 agreement and plotting dependencies (irr, irrCAC, psych, vcd, kappaSize, cluster, ggdendro, pheatmap). A case-resampling bootstrap for every coefficient becomes fast enough to switch on by default.

pathologyagreement.name: pathologyagreement
pathologyagreement.core_method: Agreement between two methods: ICC (psych::ICC forms), Lin's CCC (epiR, z-transform CI), Bland-Altman bias and limits of agreement with CIs plus a proportional-bias regression, Pearson/Spearman with percentile-bootstrap CI, and Shapiro-Wilk. Also a multi-method ICC and correlation matrix.
pathologyagreement.oracle: psych::ICC; epiR::epi.ccc(ci='z-transform'); stats::cor.test; stats::lm(diff ~ mean); stats::shapiro.test
pathologyagreement.gain: Drops psych and epiR. BCa bootstrap CIs come with scipy.stats.bootstrap at no extra code.

pathologycomposition.name: pathologycomposition
pathologycomposition.core_method: Partial stub. Outcome rate per component level with Clopper-Pearson CI, and composition-group risks. The 'Cochran-Armitage' trend is actually a Spearman test on scores ordered by first appearance. The optimal-composition matcher is a placeholder that returns TRUE for every case, so every composition gets the whole-sample risk.
pathologycomposition.oracle: stats::binom.test; stats::cor.test(method='spearman') for the current trend; stats::prop.trend.test for a true Cochran-Armitage test
pathologycomposition.gain: Nothing beyond R itself. Any port must fix the placeholder pattern matcher and the mislabelled trend test.

pathsampling.name: pathsampling
pathsampling.core_method: Per-sample detection probability q (geometric MLE 1/mean(first positive sample), or pooled empirical proportion), cumulative detection 1-(1-q)^n and the minimum number of samples for a target confidence. Also bootstrap detection curves, hypergeometric and beta-binomial (VGAM MLE) models, geometric goodness-of-fit, and lymph-node ratio / AJCC N tabulations.
pathsampling.oracle: VGAM::vglm(family=betabinomial) + VGAM::Coef; stats::dgeom, stats::phyper, stats::dhyper, stats::pbinom; stats::cor.test
pathsampling.gain: Drops VGAM (the beta-binomial MLE is scipy.stats.betabinom.logpmf plus minimize). The 10,000-iteration bootstrap vectorises. An interactive samples-vs-detection-probability curve with a target-confidence slider is cheap to recompute.

patientfollowupintro.name: patientfollowupintro
patientfollowupintro.core_method: Static HTML guide (overview, data structures, limitations, RECIST rules, glossary). It computes nothing.

patientsimilarity.name: patientsimilarity
patientsimilarity.core_method: Dimensionality reduction (t-SNE by default, UMAP, PCA, MDS), then k-means, hierarchical or DBSCAN clustering with silhouette, then Kaplan-Meier and log-rank by cluster. The value is mostly the projection plot.
patientsimilarity.oracle: Rtsne::Rtsne, umap::umap, stats::prcomp/cmdscale/kmeans/hclust, dbscan::dbscan, cluster::silhouette, survival::survdiff (embeddings are comparable only in distribution)
patientsimilarity.gain: None in the bundled interpreter. t-SNE and UMAP are stochastic and would not reproduce R's embedding anyway.

qtwist.name: qtwist
qtwist.core_method: Q-TWiST: restricted means of the TOX, TWiST and REL states from the areas between the Kaplan-Meier OS and PFS curves up to tau, a utility-weighted sum per arm, the treatment difference with bootstrap CI, and utility sensitivity and threshold grids.
qtwist.oracle: survival::survfit + print(fit, rmean=tau), or survRM2::rmst2, for each RMST; the module's own partition arithmetic
qtwist.gain: The bootstrap (1000 resamples x 2 endpoints x 2 arms of KM refits) vectorises. A (u_tox, u_rel) threshold surface is a natural interactive plot. The R RMST SE uses a non-standard formula that a port could replace with the Greenwood-based RMST variance.

qualitycontrol.name: qualitycontrol
qualitycontrol.core_method: Levey-Jennings/Shewhart limits, tabular CUSUM, EWMA, Westgard multirule counts, sigma metric, within/between-run precision, nonparametric or parametric reference intervals, proficiency z-scores, Mann-Kendall trend, and Cp/Cpk. When no batch variable is given, within-run variance is fabricated as 0.7 x the total variance.
qualitycontrol.oracle: Kendall::MannKendall (check tie and continuity conventions against scipy.stats.kendalltau); stats::quantile(type=7); stats::shapiro.test; CUSUM/EWMA recursions and CLSI EP5 formulas checked by hand
qualitycontrol.gain: Minor: drops Kendall. Any port should replace the fabricated precision split with a real nested ANOVA over days and runs.

recist.name: recist
recist.core_method: RECIST 1.1 rule engine: target-lesion selection (max 5, max 2 per organ), sum of diameters, change from baseline and nadir, CR/PR/SD/PD including the 5 mm absolute-increase rule, non-target and new-lesion overrides, confirmation window, best overall response. ORR/DCR with exact binomial CIs.
recist.oracle: stats::binom.test; RECIST 1.1 worked examples (Eisenhauer et al. 2009) and the module's own per-patient output
recist.gain: None statistically, since the rules are deterministic. One shared Python RECIST engine could serve both recist and waterfallrecist.

reclassmetrics.name: reclassmetrics
reclassmetrics.core_method: Categorical and continuous (category-free) NRI with event and non-event components, IDI with discrimination-slope components, asymptotic (Pencina) or percentile-bootstrap CIs, and a reclassification table. The survival outcome type is rejected as not implemented.
reclassmetrics.oracle: Hmisc::improveProb (continuous NRI, IDI and their SEs); PredictABEL::reclassification or nricens::nribin (categorical NRI)
reclassmetrics.gain: Faster bootstrap. The missing time-to-event NRI (KM-weighted, Pencina 2011) is a modest addition with scipy.stats.ecdf. Risk cut-offs could be edited interactively.

recurrentsurvival.name: recurrentsurvival
recurrentsurvival.core_method: Andersen-Gill counting-process Cox (survival::coxph with cluster-robust SE), and optional reReg models (Cox-LWYY etc.) with event and MCF plots. The PWP, frailty, multistate and counting-process branches only print a 'simplified implementation' note.
needs: statsmodels (PHReg with entry times, efron ties and fit(groups=) robust SE)
recurrentsurvival.oracle: survival::coxph(Surv(start, stop, event) ~ x + cluster(id)); reReg::reReg (no Python counterpart)

residualcancerburden.name: residualcancerburden
residualcancerburden.core_method: Symmans RCB index = 1.4(f_inv*d_prim)^0.17 + [4(1-0.75^LN)*d_met]^0.17, classed RCB-0/I/II/III at the 1.36 and 3.28 cut points, with a distribution summary, KM medians and a log-rank test across classes.
residualcancerburden.oracle: MD Anderson RCB calculator formula (Symmans et al., J Clin Oncol 2007); survival::survfit (median); survival::survdiff
residualcancerburden.gain: None; the formula is trivial in either language. The KM and k-sample log-rank helpers would be reusable elsewhere.

spatialanalysis.name: spatialanalysis
spatialanalysis.core_method: Point-pattern statistics in a rectangular bounding window: Ripley K/L (border and isotropic corrections) with a 99-simulation CSR envelope, nearest-neighbour distances and the Clark-Evans test, kernel-intensity hotspots, grid Getis-Ord Gi*, Morisita index, and cross-type pcf / nearest-neighbour interaction.
spatialanalysis.oracle: spatstat.explore::Kest/Lest(correction=c('border','isotropic')), envelope (comparable only in distribution), clarkevans.test, density.ppp, pcfcross(correction='translate'); spatstat.geom::nndist, nncross
spatialanalysis.gain: KD-tree pair counting scales K/L, NND and cross-type statistics to whole-slide cell counts (1e5 to 1e6 points), where spatstat slows down or drops corrections. CSR envelopes vectorise. Removes the spatstat package family.

stagemigration.name: stagemigration
stagemigration.core_method: Comparison of old vs new TNM staging: migration matrix and Will Rogers checks, Cox C-index/LR/AIC comparison, NRI/IDI, time-dependent ROC, decision curves, bootstrap optimism, RMST, and competing risks (cuminc / Fine-Gray). Cure, interval-censoring, frailty and random-forest branches are spread over about 33k lines in R/stagemigration-part*.R.
stagemigration.oracle: survival::coxph, concordance, survdiff, cox.zph; timeROC::timeROC; cmprsk::cuminc, crr; dcurves::dca; pROC::roc; randomForestSRC::rfsrc; flexsurv::flexsurvcure; icenReg::ic_par; coxme::coxme
stagemigration.gain: None. The scope is too large, and the R version is still under security and correctness remediation.

stereology.name: stereology
stereology.core_method: Point- and intersection-counting estimators per case: Aa = Vv = P_hit/P_total, B_A = 2I/L, S_V = 2*B_A = 4I/L, N_A = Q/A. Reports the mean with an unseeded percentile-bootstrap CI, then a Welch t-test (2 groups) or one-way ANOVA. Note that the standard formulas are S_V = 2*I_L and B_A = (pi/2)*I_L, so the module's S_V is doubled and its B_A is about 27% high.
stereology.oracle: stats::t.test (Welch); stats::aov; stereology formulas (Weibel 1979; Howard & Reed: S_V = 2 I_L, B_A = (pi/2) I_L)
stereology.gain: Seeded, reproducible bootstrap with a BCa option (R's bootstrap is unseeded). Any port must fix the B_A and S_V constants.

studydiagram.name: studydiagram
studydiagram.core_method: CONSORT/flow-diagram builder: participants and exclusions per step with percentages, rendered as HTML/graph. No statistics.

survivalendpoints.name: survivalendpoints
survivalendpoints.core_method: Derives PFS, OS, TTP, DOR and time on treatment from dates or times plus event flags, then reports KM medians (survfit), event and censoring rates, and milestone survival.
survivalendpoints.oracle: survival::survfit median with conf.type='log' CI (scipy offers only linear and log-log, so own Greenwood code is needed); summary(survfit, times=milestones)
survivalendpoints.gain: None; the work is mostly date arithmetic and rule logic.

synopticcompleteness.name: synopticcompleteness
synopticcompleteness.core_method: Completeness percentages per report and per item (non-missing, or equal to a 'present' value), by-group summaries, and a linear trend of completeness over time (lm slope and p).
synopticcompleteness.oracle: stats::lm(comp ~ t) slope and p-value; base R proportions

timeupdatesurvival.name: timeupdatesurvival
timeupdatesurvival.core_method: Aalen additive-hazards cumulative coefficients (timereg::aalen, n.sim=0), windowed and kernel-weighted Cox fits smoothed by splines or lowess, the cox.zph PH test, and dynamic predictions. The smoothing-diagnostics plot draws a fabricated CV curve with rnorm().
needs: lifelines (AalenAdditiveFitter, CoxPHFitter), or own Aalen and Cox engines
timeupdatesurvival.gain: None. A port must also drop the fabricated rnorm() diagnostics.

tumorbudding.name: tumorbudding
tumorbudding.core_method: ITBCC budding grade from hotspot counts normalised to 0.785 mm2 (Bd1 0-4, Bd2 5-9, Bd3 >=10), aggregated per case, then a log-rank test across grades and a one-covariate Cox trend HR with grade scored 1 to 3.
tumorbudding.oracle: survival::survdiff; survival::coxph(Surv ~ as.integer(grade)) with Efron ties; ITBCC 2016 cut-offs (Lugli et al. 2017)

tumorgrowth.name: tumorgrowth
tumorgrowth.core_method: Growth-curve fits (exponential, Gompertz, logistic, von Bertalanffy, power, linear) by nonlinear mixed effects (nlme, the default), nls, or brms, with doubling times, treatment effects and predictions. The residual plot uses rnorm() placeholder residuals.
needs: an NLME implementation (none exists in numpy/scipy/statsmodels)
tumorgrowth.gain: The nls path alone is direct with curve_fit and could ship as a small population-level fit with delta-method doubling-time CIs. The default NLME path gains nothing.

variablebiplot.name: variablebiplot
variablebiplot.core_method: PCA (prcomp), LDA (MASS::lda) or PLS-DA (mixOmics) projection with variable contributions, variance explained, a group-separation silhouette and confidence ellipses. The value is mostly the biplot.
variablebiplot.gain: Removes mixOmics (Bioconductor, which CRAN-only module builds cannot install) with about 100 lines of NIPALS PLS-DA. The biplot still needs R drawing or HTML/D3; an interactive biplot with hover labels would help.

waterfallrecist.name: waterfallrecist
waterfallrecist.core_method: Lesion-level RECIST v1.1: target selection (max 5, max 2 per organ), sum of diameters vs baseline and nadir, new-lesion and non-target overrides, per-visit response and confirmed best overall response, ORR/DCR with prop.test (Wilson, continuity-corrected) CIs.
waterfallrecist.oracle: stats::prop.test, which matches binomtest(...).proportion_ci(method='wilsoncc') except when |x - n/2| < 0.5, where R shrinks the correction; RECIST 1.1 worked examples
waterfallrecist.gain: None. It could share one RECIST engine with recist.

agepyramid.name: agepyramid
agepyramid.core_method: Plot only: counts and percentages by age band and sex, drawn as an age pyramid.

alluvial.name: alluvial
alluvial.core_method: Plot only: alluvial/Sankey flow diagrams (easyalluvial / ggalluvial) with an optional flow-count table.
alluvial.gain: None. An interactive HTML/D3 Sankey would be a plotting project, not a Python one.

benford.name: benford
benford.core_method: Benford first-digit or first-two-digit test: digit frequencies vs log10(1+1/d), chi-square goodness of fit, MAD with Nigrini conformity labels, mantissa arc test, and the largest-deviation suspects.
benford.gain: Drops benford.analysis. The R code itself documents that Nigrini's fixed cut-offs mislabel exactly-Benford data at small n; a Monte Carlo null for MAD at the actual sample size is a few vectorised lines.

categorize.name: categorize
categorize.core_method: Data transformation: bins a continuous variable (equal width, quantiles, manual, mean +/- SD, median, Fisher-Jenks via classInt) into a new column, with a frequency table.
categorize.gain: None. The bridge has no Output (add-to-data) support yet.

checkdata.name: checkdata
checkdata.core_method: Single-variable QC report: missingness, z/IQR/MAD outlier flags, distribution summary, duplicates and a missingness-run heuristic. No inferential test; the MCAR test is explicitly declared not applicable.

chisqposttest.name: chisqposttest
chisqposttest.core_method: Chi-square or Fisher test of an RxC table with expected counts, adjusted standardized residuals (Bonferroni criterion), pairwise 2x2 post-hoc tests with p-adjustment, Cramer's V with a bootstrap CI, and chi-square power.
chisqposttest.oracle: stats::chisq.test ($statistic, $expected, $stdres); stats::fisher.test (2x2 is exact in both; for RxC R uses the exact network algorithm while scipy defaults to Monte Carlo); stats::p.adjust; pwr::pwr.chisq.test; boot::boot.ci
chisqposttest.gain: Drops pwr and boot. The bootstrap for the Cramer's V CI vectorises.

crosstable.name: crosstable
crosstable.core_method: Table formatting: grouped descriptive cross-tables via gtsummary, arsenal, finalfit or tangram, with their embedded tests (chi-square/Fisher, t/ANOVA/Kruskal), q-values and an SMD table.

dataquality.name: dataquality
dataquality.core_method: Plot-first QC: visdat overview, missingness and type plots, plus duplicate and constant-variable flags. The only inferential statistic is Little's MCAR test (naniar::mcar_test).
dataquality.gain: None. Little's MCAR test alone could be ported as an EM-based numpy routine of about 80 lines.

outlierdetection.name: outlierdetection
outlierdetection.core_method: Outlier screening via performance::check_outliers. The default composite combines robust z (MAD), IQR (x1.7) and classical Mahalanobis (chi-square cut-off) with a vote threshold. Optional methods: ETI/HDI, robust Mahalanobis, MCD, OPTICS, LOF. Data above 10,000 rows is subsampled.
needs: scikit-learn (MinCovDet, OPTICS, LocalOutlierFactor), only for the optional multivariate methods
outlierdetection.oracle: performance::check_outliers(method=c('zscore_robust','iqr','mahalanobis'), threshold=...) per-method flags and composite score
outlierdetection.gain: The default composite is a few vectorised lines and can score every row instead of a 5,000-row subsample. That path no longer needs the performance/bayestestR chain.

reportcat.name: reportcat
reportcat.core_method: Report formatting: categorical frequency summaries rendered as gt/gtExtras HTML, with report sentences.

summarydata.name: summarydata
summarydata.core_method: Report formatting: continuous descriptives (mean, SD, median, IQR, skewness/kurtosis, Shapiro) rendered as gt/gtExtras HTML. pydescriptives already covers the numbers.

tableone.name: tableone
tableone.core_method: Table formatting: a Table 1 via tableone, gtsummary, arsenal or janitor.

vartree.name: vartree
vartree.core_method: Plot only: vtree variable-tree diagram (DiagrammeR, exported as SVG).

venn.name: venn
venn.core_method: Plot-first: Venn and UpSet diagrams (ggvenn, ggVennDiagram, UpSetR, ComplexUpset) with set-intersection counts and a membership table.

advancedanova.name: advancedanova
advancedanova.core_method: One-way ANOVA on the first factor only, with Shapiro/Levene/Bartlett checks, eta2/omega2/Cohen's f, a Tukey, Games-Howell, Dunnett or Bonferroni post-hoc, and power. The factorial/ANCOVA/repeated-measures model types, covariates, weights, and the Welch and robust options are ignored.
advancedanova.oracle: stats::aov; stats::TukeyHSD; PMCMRplus::gamesHowellTest; multcomp::glht(mcp(g='Dunnett')); stats::pairwise.t.test(p.adjust='bonferroni', pooled SD); car::leveneTest; stats::bartlett.test; pwr::pwr.anova.test
advancedanova.gain: Drops PMCMRplus, multcomp, car and pwr. The ignored Welch option is one argument (f_oneway(equal_var=False)), and Games-Howell is tukey_hsd(equal_var=False).

advancedimputation.name: advancedimputation
advancedimputation.core_method: Stub/placeholder: the whole MICE pipeline is commented out, and the summary and pooled tables only show placeholder structure.
advancedimputation.gain: None. mice is the reference implementation, and nothing is computed today.

autoeda.name: autoeda
autoeda.core_method: Report generation: DataExplorer introduce/profile_missing summaries plus correlation and PCA overviews, rendered as HTML.

batcheffect.name: batcheffect
batcheffect.core_method: Batch-effect screen: PCA coloured by batch, per-feature ANOVA on batch, flags for variance, missingness, redundancy (|r| above threshold) and MAD outliers, and ComBat empirical-Bayes correction (sva, parametric or non-parametric).
batcheffect.oracle: sva::ComBat(dat, batch, mod, par.prior=TRUE/FALSE); stats::prcomp; stats::aov
batcheffect.gain: Removes sva (Bioconductor) with about 100 lines of parametric ComBat. The non-parametric prior is heavier but still numpy.

bayesianclinical.name: bayesianclinical
bayesianclinical.core_method: Only the continuous-outcome path works: a JZS Bayes-factor two-sample t-test (BayesFactor::ttestBF, medium Cauchy prior) with MCMC posterior summaries. The binary/count/ordinal, hierarchical and decision-analysis paths, and most declared tables, are stubs.
bayesianclinical.oracle: BayesFactor::ttestBF(rscale='medium') (BF to about 1e-6); BayesFactor::posterior (only within MCMC error)
bayesianclinical.gain: A deterministic quadrature posterior for the effect size, instead of MCMC noise. Drops BayesFactor and its dependency chain.

biomarkerdiscovery.name: biomarkerdiscovery
biomarkerdiscovery.core_method: Biomarker selection by elastic net (cv.glmnet) or random forest after optional ComBat, univariate t/Kruskal/correlation filters with FDR, k-fold CV and ROC AUC. The cutpoint, risk-stratification and several plot outputs are placeholders.
biomarkerdiscovery.gain: None in the bundled interpreter, which has no scikit-learn.

ciSingle.name: ciSingle
ciSingle.core_method: Confidence interval for a mean, per variable and group: t, normal (z) or unseeded percentile bootstrap (boot.ci type='perc'), with Shapiro-Wilk diagnostics.
ciSingle.oracle: stats::t.test()$conf.int; boot::boot.ci(type='perc') (only within Monte Carlo error); stats::shapiro.test
ciSingle.gain: A seeded, reproducible bootstrap (R's is unseeded), and BCa at no extra code.

clinicalprediction.name: clinicalprediction
clinicalprediction.core_method: Random train/test split (R sample()), then random forest, xgboost, SVM or logistic regression for a binary outcome; test-set AUC (pROC) and confusion-matrix metrics, RF/xgboost importance; 26 of 46 options (SHAP, calibration, DCA, nomogram, bootstrap, etc.) are unwired
clinicalprediction.oracle: randomForest::randomForest, xgboost::xgboost, e1071::svm, glm(family = binomial), pROC::roc/auc. Only the logistic branch can match R, and only given the same split
clinicalprediction.gain: none: the bundled Python has no scikit-learn or xgboost, and an RNG-dependent split cannot be validated against R

clinicaltrialdesign.name: clinicaltrialdesign
clinicaltrialdesign.core_method: pwr power, sample size or detectable effect for two-sample/paired t (noncentral t), two proportions (Cohen's h), one-way ANOVA (noncentral F) and correlation; dropout inflation; a flat 2%-per-interim inflation instead of alpha spending; NI/equivalence margin unused. The sample-size total = 2n(1+1/r) gives 4n at 1:1, twice the pwr requirement
clinicaltrialdesign.oracle: pwr::pwr.t.test, pwr::pwr.2p.test, pwr::pwr.anova.test, pwr::pwr.r.test (copy pwr.r.test's Fisher-z approximation rather than an exact method)
clinicaltrialdesign.gain: small: drops pwr. A port could add real Lan-DeMets/O'Brien-Fleming boundaries (scipy.stats.multivariate_normal.cdf) in place of the 2% heuristic, but R could do the same. It must not copy the allocation doubling

coefplot.name: coefplot
coefplot.core_method: plot only: fits lm, logistic/Poisson glm or coxph and draws a coefficient (forest-style) plot via coefplot/jtools, plus a Wald coefficient table; robust_se, standardize and compare_models are not wired
needs: matplotlib (or R/ggplot2 drawing from Python-computed estimates)
coefplot.oracle: lm, glm(binomial/poisson), survival::coxph + confint(); coefplot::coefplot / jtools::plot_coefs for the figure
coefplot.gain: none: the figure is the product, and the models duplicate the regression analyses

contTables.name: contTables
contTables.core_method: jmv-style r x c contingency analysis with layers: Pearson chi-square with/without Yates, likelihood-ratio G, Fisher exact (2x2), phi, contingency coefficient, Cramér's V, log OR, OR, RR (Katz), risk difference and NNT with Wald CIs, Goodman-Kruskal gamma, Kendall tau-b, Cochran-Armitage trend
contTables.oracle: chisq.test (correct = FALSE/TRUE), fisher.test (conditional MLE OR and CI = odds_ratio(kind='conditional')), vcd::assocstats, vcd::loddsratio (adds 0.5 when a cell is 0), vcdExtra::GKgamma, cor.test(method = 'kendall') (tie-corrected asymptotic), DescTools::CochranArmitageTest
contTables.gain: none: jamovi's built-in Contingency Tables covers all of it except RD, NNT and trend. The increasing/decreasing trend options pass 'greater'/'less', which DescTools' alternative = c('two.sided','one.sided') does not accept

contTablesPaired.name: contTablesPaired
contTablesPaired.core_method: McNemar chi-square with/without continuity correction (Bowker symmetry for r x r), exact McNemar (binomial test on discordant pairs) with conditional OR CI, row/column percentages
contTablesPaired.oracle: stats::mcnemar.test (correct = FALSE/TRUE), exact2x2::exact2x2(paired = TRUE) (binom.test p and Clopper-Pearson CI mapped to OR = p/(1-p))
contTablesPaired.gain: none: duplicates jamovi's built-in Paired Samples Contingency Tables

continuousrelationship.name: continuousrelationship
continuousrelationship.core_method: lm or logistic glm of the outcome on one continuous predictor as a natural cubic spline (splines::ns), a quadratic labelled 'fractional polynomial', linear, or tertiles; LR test linear vs ns(df = 3), AIC. The covariates option is unread and all four plots are stubs
continuousrelationship.oracle: splines::ns (reproduce R's QR-projected natural-spline basis), lm, glm(family = binomial), anova(test = 'Chisq'), AIC
continuousrelationship.gain: none: the value would be the dose-response plot, which is unimplemented in R too

crosstable2.name: crosstable2
crosstable2.core_method: Table One-style cross tables rendered by arsenal, finalfit, gtsummary or tangram with their default tests, output as HTML
crosstable2.gain: none: formatting from an R-only table ecosystem

crosstablepivot.name: crosstablepivot
crosstablepivot.core_method: stub/placeholder: the pivottabler integration is unfinished; it shows a basic HTML count table, and show_totals/format_style are unused

deeplearningprediction.name: deeplearningprediction
deeplearningprediction.core_method: stub/placeholder: no network is trained. Training curves, predictions, confusion matrix, AUC and attention maps are generated with runif/rnorm
deeplearningprediction.gain: none: the bundled Python has no deep-learning stack, and the R output is fabricated

desctools.name: desctools
desctools.core_method: DescTools wrappers: Cohen's d/Hedges' g with CI, Hosmer-Lemeshow on user-supplied fitted probabilities, Anderson-Darling + Jarque-Bera, Cochran-Armitage. Verified defects: AndersonDarlingTest(x) defaults to null = 'punif' (tests Uniform(0,1), not normality); JarqueBeraTest defaults to robust = TRUE; the trend call passes g =, an argument CochranArmitageTest(x, alternative) does not have, so it always errors
desctools.oracle: DescTools::CohenD (pooled, correct, conf.level), DescTools::HosmerLemeshowTest (ngr), nortest::ad.test for a real normality AD test, DescTools::JarqueBeraTest (robust = TRUE needs own RJB code; scipy.stats.jarque_bera matches only robust = FALSE), DescTools::CochranArmitageTest on a 2 x k table
desctools.gain: drops DescTools. A port must not copy the uniform-null AD or the broken trend call

enhancedcrosstable.name: enhancedcrosstable
enhancedcrosstable.core_method: HTML cross tables (danchaltiel/crosstable style) with Pearson chi-square, phi, Cramér's V, contingency coefficient and a Wald OR with a fixed 1.96
enhancedcrosstable.oracle: chisq.test (default correction in the test line, correct = FALSE for the effect sizes)
enhancedcrosstable.gain: none: formatting, and the statistics duplicate contTables

enhancedfactorvariable.name: enhancedfactorvariable
enhancedfactorvariable.core_method: factor frequency tables (counts, valid/cumulative %, rare-level pooling) with Shannon entropy, Simpson and Berger-Parker diversity, a heuristic complexity score, and bar plots
enhancedfactorvariable.gain: none: descriptive formatting; jamovi's Frequencies covers the counts

enhancedfrequency.name: enhancedfrequency
enhancedfrequency.core_method: frequency tables (counts, %, valid %, cumulative) with rare-category pooling and entropy / Gini-impurity data-quality diagnostics

enhancedtables.name: enhancedtables
enhancedtables.core_method: gt-rendered Table One (mean/SD, median/IQR, n/%) by group, with t-test/ANOVA, Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis and chi-square/Fisher p-values
enhancedtables.oracle: t.test, aov, wilcox.test, kruskal.test, chisq.test, fisher.test; gt::gt for the rendering
enhancedtables.gain: none: the product is the gt styling

eurostatmap.name: eurostatmap
eurostatmap.core_method: plot only: downloads a Eurostat dataset and NUTS geometries and draws a tmap choropleth
eurostatmap.gain: none: network data plus mapping, an R-ecosystem task

featurequality.name: featurequality
featurequality.core_method: per-feature data-quality screen: missing %, IQR/z/modified-z outliers (isolation_forest is selectable but has no branch), Shapiro-Wilk (on a random 5000-subsample above n = 5000), a hand-coded Anderson-Darling statistic with a 3-step p lookup (0.001/0.05/0.25), adjusted skewness/kurtosis, low variance, Pearson pairs, importance by |r|, chi-square on 4 bins or between-group variance (random_forest/mutual_info fall back to variance), heuristic quality score
featurequality.oracle: shapiro.test, nortest::ad.test (for a genuine AD p-value), cor.test, chisq.test, quantile(type = 7), mad(); n > 5000 cannot match R because of the random subsample
featurequality.gain: a real Anderson-Darling p-value in place of the fabricated 3-step lookup; otherwise none

groupsummary.name: groupsummary
groupsummary.core_method: dplyr group_by/summarise (sum, mean, median, n), with optional date flooring to hour/day/week/month/year

gtsummary.name: gtsummary
gtsummary.core_method: gtsummary tbl_summary/tbl_cross/tbl_regression with add_p/add_q/add_overall, rendered as kable HTML

jcorrelation.name: jcorrelation
jcorrelation.core_method: pairwise Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation matrix with cor.test p-values and Pearson CIs, significance flags, ggpairs/corrplot/qgraph network plots and an easystats report text
jcorrelation.oracle: cor.test(method = 'pearson'|'spearman'|'kendall'). R's exact Spearman p (AS 89, n < 1290, no ties) differs from spearmanr's t approximation and needs own code; Kendall needs method = 'exact' for n < 50 without ties, as R does
jcorrelation.gain: none: jamovi's built-in Correlation Matrix covers it, and the plots stay in R

jrecode.name: jrecode
jrecode.core_method: recodes one variable from user rules (dplyr::recode; questionr::irec) into a new column; data wrangling

jsummarytools.name: jsummarytools
jsummarytools.core_method: summarytools dfSummary/freq/descr/ctable HTML reports, optionally weighted or by group

mantelhaenszel.name: mantelhaenszel
mantelhaenszel.core_method: stratified 2x2 analysis: stratum ORs (Woolf CI), MH OR with Robins-Breslow-Greenland CI, MH chi-square, crude OR, 10% confounding rule, Woolf and Breslow-Day homogeneity. Defects: the measure option (RR/RD) is unwired; Breslow-Day uses a wrong quadratic and its fourth variance term is 1/0, so BD is always 0 (p = 1); the stratum chi-square is too small by a factor n^2
mantelhaenszel.oracle: stats::mantelhaen.test (MH OR, RGB CI, correct = TRUE/FALSE), DescTools::BreslowDayTest (correct = FALSE/TRUE Tarone), DescTools::WoolfTest, chisq.test(correct = FALSE) per stratum, epiR::epi.2by2 for MH RR/RD
mantelhaenszel.gain: none beyond a correct Breslow-Day and the promised RR/RD; R needs the same fixes, and there is no dependency to remove

measurementuncertainty.name: measurementuncertainty
measurementuncertainty.core_method: GUM root-sum-of-squares budget: Type A = SD/sqrt(n); three Type B components entered as % of the mean (one labelled 'Rectangular' without the sqrt(3) divisor); U = k x u_c. Monte Carlo, operator/instrument/replicate and the other Type B inputs are unwired
measurementuncertainty.oracle: sd(x)/sqrt(n) and the root-sum-of-squares by hand (metRology::uncert / uncertMC for GUM and GUM-S1; not installed here)
measurementuncertainty.gain: a GUM Supplement 1 Monte Carlo propagation in numpy for the declared but unwired monte_carlo_simulations option, and a Welch-Satterthwaite coverage factor

missingdata.name: missingdata
missingdata.core_method: multiple imputation by chained equations (mice: pmm, norm, logreg, polyreg) with ggmice diagnostic plots (pattern, correlation, flux, trace, density, strip, xy) and an md.pattern table; no pooled analysis
missingdata.oracle: mice::mice (imputed draws agree only in distribution, because the RNG differs), mice::md.pattern
missingdata.gain: none: mice is the reference implementation, and the output is mainly plots

missingdataexplorer.name: missingdataexplorer
missingdataexplorer.core_method: per-variable missingness counts, Little's MCAR test, md.pattern pattern table, Pearson correlations of missingness indicators, vis_miss/upset plots; most temporal, group and dropout options are unwired
missingdataexplorer.oracle: naniar::mcar_test (EM via norm::prelim.norm/em.norm; copy its convergence criterion to match), mice::md.pattern, cor() on is.na() indicators
missingdataexplorer.gain: drops the naniar/norm/mice chain for the tables; the plots stay in R

mixedmodelanova.name: mixedmodelanova
mixedmodelanova.core_method: linear mixed model (lmerTest::lmer, REML/ML) with sum-coded fixed factors and random intercepts, Satterthwaite F-tests, variance components and ICC, emmeans post hoc, Shapiro-Wilk on residuals
needs: statsmodels (MixedLM; still lacks Satterthwaite df and emmeans)

nonparametric.name: nonparametric
nonparametric.core_method: Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman, median and Mood median, van der Waerden, Cochran Q, Page, McNemar, sign and Jonckheere-Terpstra tests; eta^2/epsilon^2/rank-biserial/Cliff's delta/CLES; Dunn or pairwise-Wilcoxon post hoc; Shapiro/AD/KS; Levene/Fligner/Bartlett; trimmed/winsorized/Hodges-Lehmann; bootstrap Cliff CI; normal-approximation 'power'. Dunn p-values come from dunn.test with altp = FALSE, i.e. one-sided
nonparametric.oracle: wilcox.test (exact when n < 50 without ties, correct = TRUE; set scipy's method explicitly), kruskal.test, friedman.test, mcnemar.test, DescTools::SignTest/PageTest/CochranQTest/JonckheereTerpstraTest, dunn.test::dunn.test (altp = TRUE for two-sided), car::leveneTest (center = median), fligner.test, bartlett.test, nortest::ad.test, ks.test, p.adjust
nonparametric.gain: exact permutation p-values and fast bootstrap CIs (scipy.stats.permutation_test / bootstrap). jamovi's built-in tests already cover Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis, Wilcoxon and Friedman

outbreakanalysis.name: outbreakanalysis
outbreakanalysis.core_method: outbreak epidemiology: attack rates with Wald CIs, exposure RR/OR with Wald CIs (1.96 fixed regardless of confidence_level), chi-square/Fisher per exposure, Welch t for continuous exposures, Bonferroni/Holm/FDR adjustment, logistic dose-response trend over exposure quartiles, epidemic-curve and attack-rate plots
outbreakanalysis.oracle: chisq.test, fisher.test, t.test (Welch), p.adjust (bonferroni/holm/fdr), glm(case ~ dose, family = binomial), epiR::epi.2by2 for RR/OR CIs
outbreakanalysis.gain: none: the epidemic curve is the main product and stays in R

patientreported.name: patientreported
patientreported.core_method: PRO scale scoring (reverse coding, sum/mean scores), Cronbach's alpha via psych::alpha (standardised alpha, Feldt CI, r.cor item-total), inter-item correlations, ceiling/floor effects, group comparisons (Welch t, ANOVA, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis); factor, IRT and invariance options are unwired
patientreported.oracle: psych::alpha (use = 'pairwise': std.alpha, feldt, item.stats$r.cor), t.test, aov, wilcox.test, kruskal.test
patientreported.gain: drops psych and reshape2; otherwise none

pcacomponenttest.name: pcacomponenttest
pcacomponenttest.core_method: permutation test of PCA components: prcomp variance-accounted-for against columns permuted independently, p = (#perm >= obs + 1)/(P + 1), permutation CIs, sequential stop rule, p.adjust; scree and loadings plots
pcacomponenttest.oracle: prcomp (observed eigenvalues/VAF match exactly); permutation p-values match only within Monte Carlo error (R's sample() stream); p.adjust
pcacomponenttest.gain: speed: thousands of permutations vectorised in numpy

pcaloadingtest.name: pcaloadingtest
pcaloadingtest.core_method: permutation test of PCA loadings: per-variable permutation, PCA of the permuted data, Procrustes rotation to the observed loadings (pracma::procrustes), p = (#|perm| > |obs| + 1)/(P + 1), CIs, p.adjust; loading heatmap
pcaloadingtest.oracle: prcomp (observed loadings, up to sign), pracma::procrustes; p-values only within Monte Carlo error; p.adjust
pcaloadingtest.gain: speed for large permutation counts; drops pracma

qualityoflife.name: qualityoflife
qualityoflife.core_method: partly stub/placeholder: domain scores by a linear 0-100 transform (assumes a 1-5 scale), ceiling/floor effects, domain correlations, Welch t/Wilcoxon/ANOVA are real; norm-based scores and population norms are placeholders, and the SF-6D/EQ-5D utilities are invented linear maps (0.3 + 0.7(PCS+MCS)/200, 0.2 + 0.8 x score/100)
qualityoflife.oracle: t.test, wilcox.test, aov, cor for the real parts. No oracle exists for the invented utilities: they need licensed SF-6D/EQ-5D algorithms and items the analysis does not collect
qualityoflife.gain: none: a port would carry the fabricated utilities, and the real parts are trivial in R

reportcat2.name: reportcat2
reportcat2.core_method: frequency summaries of categorical variables (counts, %, cumulative) rendered with gt

retracted.name: retracted
retracted.core_method: looks up each DOI (PMIDs via rcrossref::id_converter) against the OpenRetractions API over HTTP; no statistics
retracted.gain: none: the bundled stdlib has urllib.request and ssl, but Python adds nothing

riverplot.name: riverplot
riverplot.core_method: plot only: alluvial, sankey and stream diagrams (ggalluvial, ggstream) of category transitions over time
riverplot.gain: none from Python; an interactive D3 sankey would be a front-end feature, not a port

samplingerror.name: samplingerror
samplingerror.core_method: closed-form root-sum-of-squares sampling-error budget: detection error (1 - sensitivity), biological CV/sqrt(n), binomial sampling error with finite-population correction; n for a target error and an error-vs-n curve
samplingerror.oracle: the backend's own formulas (no package), checked by hand

screeningevaluation.name: screeningevaluation
screeningevaluation.core_method: screening programme 2x2 accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, LRs) with Wald CIs labelled 'exact', coverage/detection/recall rates per 1000 with qpois-based CIs, age-stratified rates, quality-indicator targets. The lead-time and overdiagnosis blocks are heuristics in which 'x / 1e5 || 0.005' collapses to TRUE
screeningevaluation.oracle: the backend's Wald formula (binom.test for genuinely exact CIs), qpois for rate limits, epiR::epi.tests for the accuracy table
screeningevaluation.gain: none beyond what fixing the R code gives (exact Clopper-Pearson via binomtest)

summarydata2.name: summarydata2
summarydata2.core_method: descriptives via summarytools descr/freq/dfSummary and gtExtras gt_plt_summary, plus mean/SD/median/MAD, moments skewness/kurtosis, Shapiro-Wilk and date parsing

tidydensity.name: tidydensity
tidydensity.core_method: plot only: draws random samples from 14 distributions (TidyDensity tidy_*), plots density/QQ/quantile panels, and tabulates sample mean/SD/quantiles
tidydensity.oracle: TidyDensity::tidy_* only in distribution (different RNG); theoretical moments against the stats d/p/q functions

tinytable.name: tinytable
tinytable.core_method: tinytable-rendered summary tables (n, mean, SD, median by group)

toolssummary.name: toolssummary
toolssummary.core_method: summarytools dfSummary/descr/freq/ctable reports with a base-R fallback (mean, SD, median, counts)

toxicityprofile.name: toxicityprofile
toxicityprofile.core_method: adverse-event incidence by AE, grade and organ class with Clopper-Pearson CIs (binom.test), grade-distribution chi-square, arm comparison by Fisher exact, naive cumulative incidence (count/N, no competing risks), and several AE plots. The dot-plot path calls binom::binom.test, which binom does not export
toxicityprofile.gain: none for the tables (drops binom); the plot types are the main product and stay in R

treatmenteffects.name: treatmenteffects
treatmenteffects.core_method: partly stub/placeholder: propensity scores (logit/probit glm), PS stratification, IPTW means, greedy 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching, doubly robust (AIPW with lm outcome models) and SMD balance are real; the SE is hard-coded at 0.1 (so CI and p are fabricated), the 'adjusted' SMD is 0.3 x unadjusted, Rosenbaum bounds are invented, and the IV branch is empty
treatmenteffects.oracle: glm(binomial/probit) for the PS; MatchIt::matchit(method = 'nearest', caliper, replace); WeightIt::weightit with sandwich/survey SEs for IPTW; rbounds::psens/binarysens for Rosenbaum bounds
treatmenteffects.gain: genuine bootstrap SEs/CIs of the whole PS-to-effect pipeline, fast in numpy, in place of the fixed SE = 0.1

treatmentmeta.name: treatmentmeta
treatmentmeta.core_method: pairwise meta-analysis via meta/metafor: metacont, metabin, metagen, metacor and HR inputs; FE/RE (tau^2), Q, I^2, prediction interval, subgroups, meta-regression, leave-one-out/influence, cumulative, Egger, trim-and-fill, metaBMA Bayesian averaging; forest/funnel/Baujat/radial plots
treatmentmeta.oracle: meta::metacont/metabin/metagen/metacor (metabin's fixed effect is Mantel-Haenszel; pin method.tau, whose default changed across meta versions), metafor::rma, meta::metabias (Egger), meta::trimfill, metafor::influence.rma.uni, meta::metacum, meta::metareg
treatmentmeta.gain: none: meta and metafor are the reference implementations, and the plots are the product

assayoptimization.name: assayoptimization
assayoptimization.core_method: DOE-style lm/aov of a response on factors (main effects + 2-way interactions, Type I ANOVA), quadratic response-surface lm, pwr.f2.test power and required n, Shewhart mean +/- 3 SD limits, linearity/robustness lm checks; contour and optimisation plots
assayoptimization.oracle: lm, aov/anova (sequential SS with treatment contrasts), pwr::pwr.f2.test

bayesianci.name: bayesianci
bayesianci.core_method: conjugate credible intervals: Beta-binomial (beta, Jeffreys or uniform prior), normal mean with the known variance set to the sample variance (the non-informative case uses a normal posterior, not t_{n-1}), Gamma-Poisson; equal-tailed intervals. The 'HPD' rows repeat the equal-tailed intervals, and the MCMC options are unused
bayesianci.oracle: qbeta, qgamma(shape, rate), qnorm; binom::binom.bayes(type = 'highest') for true beta HPD intervals
bayesianci.gain: true HPD intervals (shortest interval found by minimize_scalar over the ppf), which the R code only labels

bayesianma.name: bayesianma
bayesianma.core_method: stub/placeholder: an MC3-style search over predictor subsets whose 'marginal likelihood' is sum(log|cor(X, time x event)|) minus a BIC penalty (no survival likelihood); coefficients are rnorm draws, and the CV/sensitivity metrics are runif/rnorm placeholders
bayesianma.oracle: BMA::bic.surv (BIC-approximated Cox models over the model space; not installed here) for a real implementation; nothing in the current R output is a valid oracle
bayesianma.gain: none until a real Cox-likelihood BMA exists; a Python one would need its own Cox partial-likelihood fitter (Efron ties) for every model visited

bayesianmetaanalysis.name: bayesianmetaanalysis
bayesianmetaanalysis.core_method: Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of supplied effect sizes and SEs via brms (Stan), with a metafor rma comparison and an inverse-variance fixed-effect fallback. The random-effects brms formula is 'yi | se(sei) ~ 1' without (1 | study), so it fits a common-effect model and reports tau^2 = 0; only 'hierarchical with covariates' adds (1 | study)
bayesianmetaanalysis.oracle: bayesmeta::bayesmeta (exact semi-analytic normal-normal posterior; not installed here), brms::brm only within MCMC error, metafor::rma for the frequentist columns
bayesianmetaanalysis.gain: large: an exact posterior by 1-D integration over tau in milliseconds, with no MCMC noise and no Stan/C++ toolchain (brms needs rstan plus a compiler, which jamovi users rarely have)

betabinomialdiagnostic.name: betabinomialdiagnostic
betabinomialdiagnostic.core_method: mostly stub/placeholder: per-study sensitivity/specificity pooled by method-of-moments beta fits or a plain mean/var on the logit scale, simplified DerSimonian-Laird Q/I^2; the Egger/Begg statistics are rnorm draws, influence Cook's D/DFFITS are runif, and the subgroup and Dirichlet branches are placeholders
betabinomialdiagnostic.oracle: VGAM::vglm(cbind(tp, fn) ~ 1, betabinomial) for beta-binomial ML; metafor::rma (DL) on logit sensitivity/specificity; mada::reitsma for the bivariate model; metafor::regtest for Egger
betabinomialdiagnostic.gain: a real ML beta-binomial fit (and a bivariate Reitsma model via scipy.optimize) in place of moment estimators and random-number placeholders

categoricaladvanced.name: categoricaladvanced
categoricaladvanced.core_method: Pearson chi-square (Yates on 2x2), Fisher exact (2x2 conditional-MLE OR with CI; r x c by Monte Carlo), Mantel-Haenszel/CMH across a stratifier, phi/Cramer's V, standardized and adjusted residuals, pairwise row chi-square post hoc with p-adjustment, Goodman-Kruskal lambda/tau/gamma
categoricaladvanced.oracle: stats::chisq.test, stats::fisher.test, stats::mantelhaen.test, stats::p.adjust, DescTools::Lambda, DescTools::GoodmanKruskalTau, DescTools::GoodmanKruskalGamma
categoricaladvanced.gain: Exact r x c Fisher p (scipy 1.17 fisher_exact enumerates r x c; R code falls back to Monte Carlo) and the heavy DescTools import dropped; CMH and Goodman-Kruskal need ~60 lines of own code. Otherwise overlaps jamovi's Contingency Tables.

clinicalalerts.name: clinicalalerts
