clinicalalerts.core_method: Rule-based flags only: each value is compared with hard-coded critical/high/medium cut-offs chosen by regex on the variable name (potassium, sodium, glucose, creatinine, haemoglobin, age), then counts and canned action text; custom thresholds, the confidence level, trend analysis and two plots are stubs
clinicalalerts.oracle: none (no statistical method; check against hand-computed flags)

clinicaldashboard.name: clinicaldashboard
clinicaldashboard.core_method: Report formatting: counts, mean/SD/median/quartiles, a completeness score, IQR outlier counts and rule-based alerts, plus trend and distribution plots; realTimeUpdate and export options are stubs

clinicaldataintegration.name: clinicaldataintegration
clinicaldataintegration.core_method: stub/placeholder: only a data-quality overview (completeness, IQR outliers, date and patient-ID consistency, range checks); the FHIR/HL7/CDISC import, ICD-10/SNOMED/LOINC mapping and export it promises are not implemented

clinicalnomograms.name: clinicalnomograms
clinicalnomograms.core_method: rms nomograms for Cox (cph + survest), logistic (lrm) and linear (ols) models, with backward-AIC or cv.glmnet LASSO selection, bootstrap calibration and optimism validation (rms::calibrate/validate), timeROC/pROC discrimination and dcurves decision curves
clinicalnomograms.oracle: rms::cph, rms::lrm, rms::ols, rms::nomogram, rms::calibrate, rms::validate, glmnet::cv.glmnet, stats::step, timeROC::timeROC, pROC::roc, dcurves::dca
clinicalnomograms.gain: none (the value is the rms nomogram drawing and rms validation machinery; R is its natural home)

clinmon.name: clinmon
clinmon.core_method: Haemodynamic indices from continuous waveforms (PRx, Mx, Sx, Dx, PI, RI, CVRi, COest, PWA; CPPopt = 5 mmHg CPP bin with the lowest mean PRx) by block averaging and epoch-wise Pearson correlations (clintools::clinmon)
clinmon.gain: Drops clintools, which imports lme4, parameters, signal, xml2, pROC and irr for this one function; vectorised block/epoch maths handles long 1 kHz recordings without clintools' lossy 'fast' aggregation.

cochranq.name: cochranq
cochranq.core_method: Cochran's Q for k paired binary outcomes (chi-square p), a Monte Carlo within-subject permutation p, an 'exact' option that is only a column-permutation approximation, Kendall's W = Q/(n(k-1)) with an ad hoc CI, Clopper-Pearson marginal proportions; pairwise McNemar, response patterns and plots are empty placeholders
cochranq.gain: A true exact conditional p (permutation_test with permutation_type='samples' enumerates all within-subject permutations when small) and fast vectorised Monte Carlo instead of the mislabelled 'exact'; the empty pairwise McNemar post hoc becomes a few lines with binomtest.

coxphw.name: coxphw
coxphw.core_method: Weighted Cox regression for non-proportional hazards (coxphw::coxphw average-hazard-ratio weighting, robust variance) beside a standard coxph; the weight-method choice is passed as an argument coxphw 4.x does not have (it uses template = AHR/ARE/PH), and the fallback refits coxph with per-subject weights, which is not the time-dependent weighting the method needs
coxphw.gain: none (needs a Cox partial-likelihood engine with risk-set-specific weights and sandwich variance; no Python library provides it)

coxrobust.name: coxrobust
coxrobust.core_method: Bednarski robust Cox regression (coxrobust::coxr) beside coxph; the UI passes huber/tukey/hampel/bounded/weighted as f.weight although coxr accepts only linear/quadratic/exponential, so the call errors, and the fallback (deviance-residual-weighted coxph) is ad hoc

directregression.name: directregression
directregression.core_method: Jackknife pseudo-observations of the KM survival probability at chosen times (pseudo::pseudosurv), then a separate lm/glm per time point with naive model SEs; the cloglog type falls back to linear and the 'bootstrap'/'analytical' pseudo methods run the same leave-one-out loop
directregression.gain: GEE sandwich SEs and one joint model across time points (Andersen-Klein) where R reports naive per-time SEs; drops pseudo/KMsurv/geepack. One pseudo-value engine would also serve generalpseudo, pseudosurvival and rmstregression.

distributionfit.name: distributionfit
distributionfit.core_method: Censored ML fits of Weibull, exponential, log-normal, log-logistic, gamma, generalized gamma and generalized F (flexsurv::flexsurvreg, optional covariates) ranked by AIC/BIC/AICc with Akaike weights; the goodness-of-fit table is fabricated (KS of observed times against an evenly spaced grid, AD = 1.5 x KS and CvM = 0.8 x KS, all reusing the KS p)
distributionfit.gain: Real GOF: parametric-bootstrap AD/CvM/KS (scipy.stats.goodness_of_fit for uncensored data, Monte Carlo for censored) replaces fabricated statistics; scipy's censored .fit covers the five common families without flexsurv's large import tree (generalized gamma/F and covariates need own likelihoods).

dynamiccoeff.name: dynamiccoeff
dynamiccoeff.core_method: stub/placeholder: a 'Kalman filter' whose observations are the static Cox linear predictor and whose single state is copied to every coefficient; the particle, Bayesian and recursive variants and the AIC/BIC comparison are equally ad hoc, so no valid time-varying coefficient is estimated
dynamiccoeff.gain: none for a port; only a rewrite to a published dynamic model (e.g. extended-Kalman discrete-time hazard, Fahrmeir 1994) would add value

dynamicprediction.name: dynamicprediction
dynamicprediction.core_method: Landmark Cox PH per landmark time (survivors at t_LM, last biomarker value carried forward) giving S(t_LM + horizon | alive at t_LM); joint-model and super-learner options fall back to landmarking, and the dynamic-Cox predictions (0.5/1.0/0.3/0.7), C-index (0.7) and fallback AUC (0.75) are hard-coded placeholders
dynamicprediction.oracle: survival::coxph, survival::survfit.coxph, dynpred::cutLM, timeROC::timeROC, JMbayes2::jm (joint models)
dynamicprediction.gain: Real C-index and time-dependent AUC in place of hard-coded numbers; the landmark part becomes implementable once a shared numpy Cox (Efron) engine exists. Joint models stay out of reach.

effectsize.name: effectsize
effectsize.core_method: Cohen's d, Hedges' g and Glass's delta (one- and two-sample) with Wald-type CIs (large-sample SE x t quantile; the one-sample CI omits the 1/sqrt(n) scaling, so it is about sqrt(n) times too wide); 13 further advertised measures plus bootstrap, paired and power options are not implemented
effectsize.oracle: effectsize::cohens_d, effectsize::hedges_g, effectsize::glass_delta, MBESS::conf.limits.nct, effectsize::rank_biserial, effectsize::cliffs_delta
effectsize.gain: Exact noncentral-t CIs and BCa bootstrap CIs instead of wrong or approximate ones; the missing rank-based measures (rank-biserial, Cliff's delta, Vargha-Delaney A, CLES) follow from mannwhitneyu's U in a few lines.

enhancedcorrelation.name: enhancedcorrelation
enhancedcorrelation.core_method: Pairwise Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation matrix via psych::corr.test or cor.test (Fisher-z CIs, t-based p) with heat-map and pairs plots; the p-adjustment the code reads is not an option in the .a.yaml, so no adjustment is ever applied
enhancedcorrelation.gain: none beyond optional bootstrap CIs for Spearman/Kendall; jamovi's Correlation Matrix covers it and the GGally pairs plot stays in R

enhancedtwowayfrequency.name: enhancedtwowayfrequency
enhancedtwowayfrequency.core_method: Two-way crosstab with row/column/total percentages, Pearson chi-square (optional Yates), Fisher exact, standardized residuals, phi and Cramer's V (V is computed from the Yates-corrected chi-square on 2x2 tables, so understated), heat-map and mosaic plots
enhancedtwowayfrequency.gain: none (duplicates jamovi's Contingency Tables; plots stay in R)

exacttests.name: exacttests
exacttests.core_method: Fisher exact (conditional-MLE OR with exact CI), exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson), McNemar (asymptotic chi-square despite the 'exact' title) and a 'Barnard' option that silently runs Fisher; the Wilson and Agresti-Coull CI choices are labels only
exacttests.oracle: stats::fisher.test, stats::binom.test, stats::mcnemar.test, exact2x2::mcnemar.exact, Exact::exact.test (Z-pooled Barnard, Boschloo), DescTools::BinomCI (wilson, agresti-coull)
exacttests.gain: Real Barnard and Boschloo unconditional exact tests (scipy has both), exact McNemar (binomtest on discordant pairs) and Wilson/Agresti-Coull CIs: all advertised in R but not computed.

excessmortality.name: excessmortality
excessmortality.core_method: stub/placeholder: a Poisson GLM of all deaths with offset log(follow-up) and a cubic time polynomial; the 'expected rates' are synthetic (1% x exp(0.08(age-50)) x sex factor) and never enter the model, so no excess hazard over population mortality is estimated
excessmortality.gain: A genuine additive excess-hazard model (population hazard per subject supplied as a column or a bundled life table) where R has none; life-table input is required either way.

factoranalysis.name: factoranalysis
factoranalysis.core_method: Exploratory factor analysis by ML or principal-axis (psych::fa) or principal components (psych::principal), varimax/quartimax/oblimin/promax rotation, Kaiser or parallel-analysis factor count, KMO, Bartlett sphericity and factor scores
factoranalysis.oracle: psych::fa (fm = 'ml', 'pa'), psych::principal, psych::fa.parallel, psych::KMO, psych::cortest.bartlett, GPArotation::oblimin, GPArotation::quartimax, stats::varimax, psych::factor.scores
factoranalysis.gain: none (jamovi's built-in EFA and PCA already wrap psych)

flexiblerelativesurvival.name: flexiblerelativesurvival
flexiblerelativesurvival.core_method: stub/placeholder: Poisson GLM with offsets log(follow-up) + log(expected hazard) where the expected hazard is synthetic (no life table), the 'splines' are polynomials, and relative-survival CIs use a fixed SE of 0.05; no real flexible relative-survival model
flexiblerelativesurvival.gain: Honest net survival (Pohar Perme) and a spline excess-hazard model from a user-supplied population hazard, replacing fixed-SE CIs.

frailtysurvival.name: frailtysurvival
frailtysurvival.core_method: Shared gamma-frailty Cox by penalized likelihood (coxph + frailty(cluster)) or Gaussian random-effect Cox (coxme); the frailty-distribution, baseline-hazard, nested/correlated and MCMC options are read but not used

friedmantest.name: friedmantest
friedmantest.core_method: Friedman rank test (hand formula without tie correction; 'exact' returns friedman.test's chi-square p; Monte Carlo by 10,000 R-loop simulations), Kendall's W with an ad hoc CI, post hoc Nemenyi (PMCMRplus), pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank (normal approximation) or sign tests with p-adjustment
friedmantest.gain: Drops PMCMRplus (needs the GMP/MPFR system libraries through gmp/Rmpfr) for a few lines with studentized_range; a genuine tie-corrected exact or vectorised Monte Carlo permutation p (permutation_test, permutation_type='samples').

generalpseudo.name: generalpseudo
generalpseudo.core_method: Jackknife pseudo-observations for S(t), cumulative incidence (Aalen-Johansen), RMST and KM quantiles, regressed by lm, logit/cloglog GLM or betareg with naive SEs; the 'bootstrap' and 'analytical' pseudo-values are the point estimate plus rnorm() noise (fabricated)
generalpseudo.oracle: survival::pseudo, pseudo::pseudosurv, pseudo::pseudoci, pseudo::pseudomean, geepack::geese, betareg::betareg
generalpseudo.gain: Exact (or infinitesimal-jackknife) pseudo-values instead of rnorm-generated ones, GEE sandwich SEs and a vectorised leave-one-out (R refits survfit n times per time point); one engine shared with pseudosurvival, directregression and rmstregression.

hierarchicalbayes.name: hierarchicalbayes
hierarchicalbayes.core_method: stub/placeholder: unweighted means/SDs of study logit sensitivity and specificity labelled as posterior estimates of a Bayesian bivariate/HSROC model; 'prediction intervals' are CI +/- 0.1, posterior SDs are constants, and R-hat, ESS, MCMC SE, Mahalanobis distances and influence come from runif()/sample()
hierarchicalbayes.oracle: bamdit::metadiag or a JAGS/Stan bivariate binomial-normal model; frequentist check mada::reitsma
hierarchicalbayes.gain: none until rewritten; an honest numpy/scipy alternative is the frequentist bivariate random-effects model (Reitsma REML or binomial GLMM, oracle mada::reitsma)

imagingcorrelation.name: imagingcorrelation
imagingcorrelation.core_method: Mostly stub/placeholder: pairwise Pearson/Spearman/Kendall tests (polychoric falls back to Spearman), unweighted Cohen's kappa without SE, 2x2 sensitivity/specificity with 'AUC' = (sens + spec)/2; heat-map, network and ROC plots are drawn from runif()/rnorm() data and the radiomics/texture/AI sections are text
imagingcorrelation.gain: none (the genuine pieces duplicate the agreement, diagnostic-test and correlation analyses)

interruptedtimeseries.name: interruptedtimeseries
interruptedtimeseries.core_method: Segmented OLS (pre-trend, level change, slope change) with Newey-West HAC SEs (fixed or automatic lag, no prewhitening, small-sample adjustment), coeftest t-tests, Durbin-Watson test and counterfactual predictions
interruptedtimeseries.gain: none beyond dropping sandwich/lmtest; a block-bootstrap or permutation p for the level/slope change would be a new option

intervalsurvival.name: intervalsurvival
intervalsurvival.core_method: Interval-censored survival via icenReg: Turnbull NPMLE (ic_np), semiparametric PH (ic_sp), parametric AFT (Weibull, log-normal, log-logistic, exponential, gamma; ic_par), covariate-averaged S(t) and seeded bootstrap percentile CIs
intervalsurvival.gain: scipy.stats.CensoredData takes interval censoring natively for any scipy distribution, so extra families come cheaply; the NPMLE and semiparametric PH fit are the costly part. Otherwise none.

labcontrolcharts.name: labcontrolcharts
labcontrolcharts.core_method: Levey-Jennings limits (mean +/- k SD), Westgard multi-rule violations, linear-trend (lm) and Wald-Wolfowitz runs tests, a max-t shift search with an unadjusted t-test p, Shewhart-only ARL constants; CUSUM and EWMA are never computed and all three control-chart renderers are 'implementation in progress' placeholders
labcontrolcharts.oracle: qcc::qcc, qcc::cusum, qcc::ewma, spc::xcusum.arl, spc::xewma.arl, randtests::runs.test
labcontrolcharts.gain: Computes the tabular CUSUM, EWMA (exact time-varying limits) and their ARLs (Markov-chain approximation) that R only advertises; the charts would still need an R/ggplot2 or HTML renderer fed by Python data.

labinterpret.name: labinterpret
labinterpret.core_method: Rule-based lab interpretation against hard-coded, name-matched reference ranges (generic 0-100 fallback), critical-value flags, per-test lm trend slope, percent-change delta checks, pairwise Pearson correlations and canned medication-effect text

mediansurvival.name: mediansurvival
mediansurvival.core_method: Kaplan-Meier median survival with CIs per group, log-rank and G-rho tests (the 'Wilcoxon' and 'Peto-Peto' choices both run rho = 1), pairwise log-rank with p-adjustment; log-log/plain CIs come from a survfit refit on the collapsed unique times (wrong whenever times are tied), 'Brookmeyer-Crowley' is the default log CI and ignores the chosen confidence level
mediansurvival.gain: Correct median CIs with ties, distinct Gehan-Breslow vs Peto-Peto weights and the confidence level honoured; scipy.stats.logrank is two-sample only, so k-group and G-rho tests need ~40 lines.

ordinalmixedmodel.name: ordinalmixedmodel
ordinalmixedmodel.core_method: Cumulative link mixed model (ordinal::clmm; random intercepts, Laplace/adaptive Gauss-Hermite) with ordinal::nominal_test for proportional odds

pagetrendtest.name: pagetrendtest
pagetrendtest.core_method: Page's L test for an ordered trend across repeated conditions (normal approximation); the 'exact' option silently returns the normal approximation and 'permutation' is an unseeded 1000-draw loop; descriptive, assumption and plot helpers are empty placeholders
pagetrendtest.gain: A genuine exact null distribution (page_trend_test method='exact', valid without ties) and a seeded, vectorised permutation p; custom/decreasing orders map to predicted_ranks.

partialcorrelation.name: partialcorrelation
partialcorrelation.core_method: Partial Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation by correlating OLS residuals after regressing out the controls; p and CI come from cor.test on the residuals (df n-2 instead of n-2-k) and Spearman/Kendall residualise raw values rather than ranks; semi-partial, bootstrap and other advertised features are no-op stubs
partialcorrelation.gain: Correct df for p and CI, rank-based partial Spearman/Kendall as in ppcor, and the stubbed semi-partial and bootstrap CIs; otherwise overlaps jamovi's Partial Correlation.

patientdashboard.name: patientdashboard
patientdashboard.core_method: stub/placeholder: a patient-monitoring dashboard whose risk levels, alert and dosing times, compliance, outcome and quality metrics are generated with runif()/sample() rather than computed from the data, around rule-based vital/lab range flags

permutationsurvival.name: permutationsurvival
permutationsurvival.core_method: Permutation (optionally within-stratum) test of survival differences using the survdiff chi-square with rho = 0 (log-rank), 1 (labelled Gehan-Breslow, actually Peto-Peto) or 0.5 (labelled Tarone-Ware, actually Fleming-Harrington), p = (b + 1)/(B + 1), plus per-group KM medians
permutationsurvival.gain: Vectorised permutations (R refits survdiff once per permutation), exact enumeration for small samples, and correctly weighted Gehan and Tarone-Ware statistics; the permutation histogram can be drawn from Python-computed data.

pheval.name: pheval
pheval.core_method: Proportional-hazards checks after coxph: cox.zph score tests with identity/log/rank/KM time transforms, correlation and lm slope of Schoenfeld residuals against time; the 'log-rank trend' and 'supremum' tests are placeholders (the coefficient's Wald z, and |beta| treated as a z)
pheval.gain: A genuine Lin-Wei-Ying supremum test by simulated score processes could replace the placeholder, but only on top of a numpy Cox engine; otherwise none.

polychoriccorr.name: polychoriccorr
polychoriccorr.core_method: stub/approximation: tetrachoric r from cos(pi/(1 + sqrt(OR))) with an extra sign flip (wrong sign when OR > 1 but the diagonal sum is smaller) and an ad hoc SE; polychoric, polyserial and biserial all fall back to Spearman; the ML/two-step choice is ignored; chi-square independence test
polychoriccorr.oracle: polycor::polychor (ML = TRUE/FALSE, std.err = TRUE), polycor::polyserial, psych::tetrachoric, psych::biserial
polychoriccorr.gain: True ML or two-step polychoric/tetrachoric/polyserial estimates with SEs and a bivariate-normality test, where R shows a rough formula or Spearman.

populationhealth.name: populationhealth
populationhealth.core_method: stub/placeholder: most helpers return literals or runif()/rnorm() values (regional health score, disparity index, quality metrics, predictive model, trends) and several sections never read the data

pseudosurvival.name: pseudosurvival
pseudosurvival.core_method: Jackknife KM pseudo-values at chosen times (clipped to [0,1], which biases them) regressed by lm or geeglm (identity link, independence, sandwich SE); 'RMST regression' uses each subject's observed (even censored) time as their RMST in OLS; cumulative-incidence, life-years-lost and quantile analyses are placeholders
pseudosurvival.gain: Unclipped pseudo-values, real RMST/CIF/life-years-lost pseudo regressions with sandwich SEs and a vectorised jackknife; same engine as generalpseudo.

raftgee.name: raftgee
raftgee.core_method: Semiparametric rank-based AFT (aftgee::aftgee: Gehan or log-rank rank-estimating-equation start, then GEE least-squares iterations with a working correlation for clusters, resampling variance) with a coxph comparison

referenceintervals.name: referenceintervals
referenceintervals.core_method: Reference interval as nonparametric percentiles (quantile type 7) or mean +/- 1.96 SD with a Shapiro-Wilk/KS normality check; the robust, bootstrap, Box-Cox and log-normal methods, outlier tests (Dixon, Grubbs, Tukey, Horn), Harris-Boyd partitioning and CIs of the limits are advertised but fall back to percentiles or do nothing
referenceintervals.gain: The CLSI EP28-A3c pieces R only advertises: 90% CIs of the limits (order-statistic ranks or bootstrap), robust Horn-Pesce biweight limits, Box-Cox/log-normal limits, Horn/Dixon/Tukey outlier screening and Harris-Boyd partitioning.

rmst.name: rmst
rmst.core_method: RMST per group as the area under the KM curve up to tau (fixed, percentile or min-of-max), Greenwood-type variance, between-group difference and ratio (delta method) with Wald tests; the bootstrap-CI option is never used
rmst.gain: The advertised bootstrap CI (paired resampling with scipy.stats.bootstrap) and a fast tau sweep of the RMST difference; otherwise none.

rmstregression.name: rmstregression
rmstregression.core_method: RMST regression by jackknife pseudo-observations and OLS (naive SEs); 'direct modelling' reports Weibull AFT coefficients from survreg on tau-truncated times as if they were RMST effects; the Wei-Lin-Ying (Tian IPCW) option is a placeholder that falls back to pseudo-values; unadjusted group RMST via survRM2::rmst2
rmstregression.oracle: survRM2::rmst2 (covariates = Tian et al. IPCW regression), pseudo::pseudomean + geepack::geese, survival::survreg
rmstregression.gain: Real Tian-Zhao-Wei IPCW RMST regression and GEE sandwich SEs where R has a placeholder and naive OLS SEs; shares the pseudo-value engine.

robustaft.name: robustaft
robustaft.core_method: Ad hoc iteratively reweighted parametric AFT (survival::survreg) with Huber/Tukey/Hampel/Andrews weights on standardized log-time residuals (censored residuals treated as complete; 'median'/'LAD' are plain survreg), naive weighted-fit SEs; not a published robust AFT estimator
robustaft.oracle: survival::survreg (with weights), RobustAFT::TML.censored (a genuine robust estimator)
robustaft.gain: none for a port (it would reproduce an unvalidated procedure); a truncated-ML robust AFT like RobustAFT::TML.censored would be new work

robustcorrelation.name: robustcorrelation
robustcorrelation.core_method: Pairwise robust correlations: Spearman/Kendall (cor.test), percentage bend (WRS2::pbcor), biweight midcorrelation (WGCNA::bicor, Fisher-z p), MCD/MVE robust covariance (robustbase, Fisher-z p); Mahalanobis/MCD/z/IQR outlier flags; percentile bootstrap CIs (boot)
robustcorrelation.gain: Drops WGCNA (Bioconductor impute/preprocessCore), WRS2, robustbase and boot; vectorised bootstrap CIs. MCD/MVE use random subsets, so they match robustbase only to a tolerance.

sigmametrics.name: sigmametrics
sigmametrics.core_method: Per-analyte Sigma = (TEa - |bias|)/CV, DPMO and yield from the normal tail with a 1.5-sigma shift, quality goal index = bias/(1.5 CV), normalized method-decision chart; about 16 declared options are unused and the cost estimate uses a hard-coded monthly volume

smoothtimevary.name: smoothtimevary
smoothtimevary.core_method: Aalen additive hazards model (timereg::aalen) cumulative regression functions B(t) interpolated at chosen times; the SEs/CIs are one constant from the SD of successive differences and the 'constancy test' statistic is identically n-1 (fabricated); the smoothing method, df and bandwidth options are ignored
smoothtimevary.oracle: timereg::aalen (cum, var.cum, robvar.cum, constancy tests), survival::aareg
smoothtimevary.gain: Genuine pointwise Aalen/robust SEs, a real resampling (supremum) constancy test and actual spline/kernel smoothing of dB(t) in place of fabricated values; drops timereg.

spatialautocorrelation.name: spatialautocorrelation
spatialautocorrelation.core_method: Global Moran's I and Geary's C (normality or randomisation moments) and local Moran's I (LISA) on point coordinates with Delaunay, k-nearest, distance-band, inverse-distance or Gaussian weights via spdep; the 'permutation test' choice actually selects the analytical randomisation moments, and queen/rook both fall back to Delaunay
spatialautocorrelation.oracle: spdep::moran.test, spdep::geary.test, spdep::localmoran, spdep::moran.mc, spdep::geary.mc, spdep::localmoran_perm, spdep::knn2nb, spdep::dnearneigh, spdep::tri2nb
spatialautocorrelation.gain: Drops spdep's sf/s2/units (GDAL/GEOS) stack; genuine vectorised permutation tests for global and local statistics where R relabels analytical moments; useful for cell-coordinate data from digital pathology.

splinehazard.name: splinehazard
splinehazard.core_method: Royston-Parmar flexible parametric survival (flexsurv::flexsurvspline): natural cubic spline in log time on the log cumulative hazard/odds/normal scale, knots at event-time quantiles, equally spaced or chosen by AIC, optional covariates
splinehazard.gain: Drops flexsurv's large import tree (tidyverse, rstpm2, mstate, deSolve); otherwise none.

stratifiedparametric.name: stratifiedparametric
stratifiedparametric.core_method: flexsurv::flexsurvreg MLE per stratum (Weibull, exponential, lognormal, log-logistic, gamma, gen. gamma, gen. F; covariates on the location parameter) compared with one pooled fit: LR test of stratification, AIC, and survival/hazard at hard-coded t = 1,2,3,5,10 with simulation CIs. The shared-shape and proportional options use survreg + strata() instead. Partly placeholder: the residual table is fabricated (mean 0, SD 1, KS p 0.5, 'Adequate') and the spline df/knot options are never used. 'loglogistic' is not a flexsurv dist name (flexsurv uses 'llogis'), so that choice probably fails silently.
needs: plot renderer for its 4 survival/hazard plots (excluded from effort)
stratifiedparametric.oracle: flexsurv::flexsurvreg (dist = 'weibull', 'exp', 'lnorm', 'llogis', 'gamma', 'gengamma', 'genf'): loglik, AIC and the res table; survival::survreg(Surv ~ x + strata(s)); summary.flexsurvreg only within a tolerance, because its CIs are simulated (B = 1000)
stratifiedparametric.gain: Small. Deterministic delta-method CIs and a cheap parametric bootstrap in numpy. flexsurv stays a dependency anyway, because the shipped survival analysis uses it. The real work is replacing the fabricated residual table, the fixed time points and the dead spline options, which R can do equally well.

transformationmodels.name: transformationmodels
transformationmodels.core_method: stub/placeholder: no tram/mlt model is ever fitted (there is no tram:: call). It transforms the time variable (Box-Cox, log-log, probit, logit, cloglog) and fits a survival::survreg AFT on the result. The Box-Cox lambda grid search omits the Jacobian, Shapiro-Wilk runs on residuals that include censored rows, and the method, support, bootstrap and weights options do nothing.
needs: plot renderer for its 4 plots (excluded from effort)
transformationmodels.oracle: tram::Coxph, tram::Colr, tram::BoxCox, tram::Survreg (mlt::mlt); for the current code, survival::survreg and MASS::boxcox
transformationmodels.gain: None over wiring up tram in R. A faithful Python version means rewriting mlt: Bernstein bases with monotone constraints, censored likelihoods, and score/Hessian SEs. Porting today's code would only port its defects.

treatmentoptim.name: treatmentoptim
treatmentoptim.core_method: stub/placeholder: the treatments, drug interactions, doses, safety rows and comparison results ('65% vs 72%, p = 0.032') are hard-coded and ignore the patient data. The prediction model returns nothing and there are no plot renderers (the code carries a RELEASE-BLOCKING TODO).
treatmentoptim.gain: None. It needs a real design first (a validated response model such as logistic regression, plus a curated interaction source), whatever the language.

treatmentswitching.name: treatmentswitching
treatmentswitching.core_method: partly stub: Cox HRs for ITT and per-protocol. 'IPCW' is a baseline logistic propensity weight (stabilised, trimmed to [0.1, 10]) in a weighted Cox. 'RPSFT' shrinks post-switch time by a user-fixed acceleration factor, with no g-estimation. 'TVC' is a Cox on the received treatment, with no counting process. 'Two-stage' divides the ITT HR by a hard-coded 0.7. There is a percentile bootstrap CI for the HR, and the generic sensitivity branch returns hard-coded HRs.
needs: plot renderer for its 3 plots (excluded from effort)
treatmentswitching.oracle: survival::coxph (ties = 'efron', with weights), stats::glm(family = binomial), and rpsftm::rpsftm for a genuine RPSFTM
treatmentswitching.gain: Moderate, but only as a rewrite. A real RPSFTM (log-rank g-estimation with brentq, plus recensoring) and a vectorised bootstrap suit numpy. A true time-varying IPCW (counting-process weighted Cox) would be hard. Porting the placeholders adds nothing.

advancedraincloud.name: advancedraincloud
advancedraincloud.core_method: plot first: ggrain raincloud with longitudinal ID lines, covariate colouring and Likert jitter. Html panels give group descriptives, a Wilcoxon (2 groups) or Kruskal-Wallis p, d-type effect sizes, change scores and responder rates, MCID/reference/CV bands and outlier filtering.
needs: plot renderer (matplotlib not bundled; R/ggplot2 or HTML/D3 from Python data; excluded from effort)
advancedraincloud.gain: None from Python itself; the figure is the value. Dynamic idea: an HTML/D3 raincloud with hover (subject ID, value) and click to highlight one patient's trajectory across time points.

hullplot.name: hullplot
hullplot.core_method: plot only: ggforce concave hulls (geom_mark_hull, concavity/expand) around groups on an x-y scatter. Optional 95% data ellipses (stat_ellipse, multivariate t), per-group quartiles, and the smallest centroid distance in within-group SD units.
needs: concave-hull algorithm (ggforce uses concaveman; scipy has only ConvexHull)
hullplot.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover a hull to list its patients, and toggle groups from the legend.

jjarcdiagram.name: jjarcdiagram
jjarcdiagram.core_method: plot first: arc diagram of an edge list (igraph), with nodes sized by degree or strength and sorted by name, degree or group. Network summary: density, connectedness, degree/strength, betweenness (weighted via inverse weights) and the most central node.
needs: networkx optional (Brandes betweenness is about 40 lines of own code)
jjarcdiagram.gain: None numerically. It is the strongest interactivity candidate in this batch: hover a node to highlight its arcs and neighbours, filter arcs by weight, and re-sort without re-running. This needs an Html result type in ClinicoPathPj, which today has only Table and Preformatted.

jjbarstats.name: jjbarstats
jjbarstats.core_method: plot first: ggstatsplot::ggbarstats stacked bars with a statsExpressions subtitle: Pearson chi-square of independence with a Cramer's V CI, McNemar for paired data (no correction), a contingencyTableBF Bayes factor, and per-bar proportion (goodness-of-fit) tests. Its own Fisher exact fallback runs when expected counts are below 5; an optional ggpubr balloon plot is also offered.
jjbarstats.oracle: statsExpressions::contingency_table, stats::chisq.test, stats::mcnemar.test(correct = FALSE), stats::fisher.test, BayesFactor::contingencyTableBF
jjbarstats.gain: None; the subtitle duplicates jmv contingency tables. Caveat for any stats-only port: scipy.stats.fisher_exact is exact only for 2x2. For RxC it uses Monte Carlo: measured p = 0.0668 against an exact 0.0659, and the value changes on every call. RxC therefore needs own exact enumeration. Dynamic idea: hover a segment for n, % and the cell residual.

jjbetweenstats.name: jjbetweenstats
jjbetweenstats.core_method: plot first: ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats box-violin plot. Subtitle: Welch or Fisher one-way ANOVA (omega^2/eta^2 CI), Kruskal-Wallis (epsilon^2), trimmed-means ANOVA (WRS2::t1way) or anovaBF; with 2 groups: Welch t, Mann-Whitney, Yuen or ttestBF. Pairwise Games-Howell, Student, Dunn or Yuen with p-adjustment; Levene check; ggpubr variants.
jjbetweenstats.oracle: statsExpressions::oneway_anova, statsExpressions::two_sample_test, statsExpressions::pairwise_comparisons (PMCMRplus::gamesHowellTest, PMCMRplus::kwAllPairsDunnTest, WRS2::lincon), stats::oneway.test, WRS2::t1way, BayesFactor::anovaBF
jjbetweenstats.gain: None; jmv's one-way ANOVA already does Welch with Games-Howell. Verified in the bundled scipy 1.17.1: f_oneway(equal_var=False) equals Welch's oneway.test and tukey_hsd(equal_var=False) equals Games-Howell, both matching hand formulas exactly. Dunn, t1way and the Bayes factors would be own code, so a statsExpressions equivalent is large. Effort is for a stats-only companion. Dynamic idea: hover points for case ID or outlier label.

jjcorrmat.name: jjcorrmat
jjcorrmat.core_method: plot first: ggcorrmat heatmap plus a correlation table from correlation::correlation: Pearson, Spearman, 20% winsorized ('robust'), or Bayesian (BF10 with an MCMC posterior-median rho). Optional partial correlations, p-adjustment (Holm by default) and CIs.
jjcorrmat.gain: None; jmv corrMatrix already covers Pearson and Spearman. The table alone would be implementable: partial r from the inverse correlation matrix, and Holm in 3 lines (false_discovery_control does only BH/BY). The Bayesian posterior medians come from MCMC, so they would match only approximately. Dynamic idea: hover cells for r, CI, p and n, and click a cell to open that pair's scatter.

jjdotchart.name: jjdotchart
jjdotchart.core_method: plot first: ggdotplotstats dot chart of one centrality per group (mean, median, trimmed mean or MAP), with a group summaries table. The k group summaries are tested against a reference value with a one-sample t, a Wilcoxon signed-rank (normal approximation, continuity-corrected), a trimmed-mean bootstrap-t, or a Bayes factor.
jjdotchart.oracle: statsExpressions::one_sample_test, statsExpressions::centrality_description, WRS2::trimcibt; the signed-rank test matches scipy wilcoxon(method='asymptotic', correction=True)
jjdotchart.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover a dot for the group's n and CI.

jjdotplotstats.name: jjdotplotstats
jjdotplotstats.core_method: plot first: 'Horizontal Box-Violin Comparison' is ggbetweenstats with coord_flip(), plus an optional reference line. Its subtitle tests are those of jjbetweenstats: Welch/Fisher ANOVA or t, Kruskal-Wallis or Mann-Whitney, Yuen/t1way, BF, and pairwise comparisons.
jjdotplotstats.gain: None; it duplicates jjbetweenstats and would share its engine, at almost no marginal effort once that exists.

jjhistostats.name: jjhistostats
jjhistostats.core_method: plot first: gghistostats histogram with a centrality line. Optional one-sample test against test.value: t (Hedges' g), Wilcoxon signed-rank, trimmed-mean bootstrap-t, or ttestBF with a chosen prior. Shapiro-Wilk and a skewness interpretation; ggpubr histogram, density, QQ and ECDF panels.
jjhistostats.gain: None. Dynamic idea: a live bin-width slider and hover counts per bin, all client-side.

jjpiestats.name: jjpiestats
jjpiestats.core_method: plot first: ggpiestats pie, or a ggpubr donut. With one variable: chi-square goodness of fit (equal proportions or a user ratio). With two: chi-square of independence with a Cramer's V CI, McNemar for paired data, or a BF. Per-slice proportion tests, and its own Fisher fallback when expected counts are below 5.
jjpiestats.oracle: statsExpressions::contingency_table, stats::chisq.test, stats::mcnemar.test(correct = FALSE), stats::fisher.test, BayesFactor::contingencyTableBF
jjpiestats.gain: None. It shares jjbarstats' engine, and the same RxC Fisher caveat applies: scipy's RxC test is Monte Carlo. Dynamic idea: hover a slice for its count and %.

jjridges.name: jjridges
jjridges.core_method: plot first: ggridges ridgeline densities (nrd0/nrd/SJ bandwidths, gradient fill). Two tables. 'Statistical Summary': n, mean, SD, median, IQR, skewness. 'Statistical Tests': pairwise Welch t, Wilcoxon with a Hodges-Lehmann CI, Yuen or ttestBF; Levene and Shapiro checks; Cohen's d, Hedges' g, eta^2 and omega^2 with CIs; percentile bootstrap CI.
jjridges.oracle: stats::t.test, stats::wilcox.test(conf.int = TRUE), WRS2::yuen, BayesFactor::ttestBF, effectsize::cohens_d/hedges_g/eta_squared/omega_squared, car::leveneTest(center = median), boot::boot.ci(type = 'perc')
jjridges.gain: None for the figure. Both tables are implementable in scipy (ttest_ind(trim=0.2) is Yuen's t) but only duplicate standard tests. Dynamic idea: toggle groups from the legend, and hover a ridge for its n and median.

jjscatterstats.name: jjscatterstats
jjscatterstats.core_method: plot first: ggscatterstats scatter with an lm/loess/gam smooth and ggExtra marginals. Subtitle: Pearson r (Fisher-z CI), Spearman rho, 20% winsorized r, or Bayesian BF10 with a posterior rho. Also a ggpubr scatter with stat_cor, and grouped panels.
jjscatterstats.gain: None numerically. Dynamic idea: hover points for the case label instead of ggrepel clutter, brush to select points, and toggle the smoother.

jjsegmentedtotalbar.name: jjsegmentedtotalbar
jjsegmentedtotalbar.core_method: plot first: ggsegmentedtotalbar 100% (segmented-total) bars with composition and summary tables. A Pearson chi-square of independence without correction runs on the summed values, reporting the largest adjusted standardized residual; a note says it is valid only when the value variable is a count.
jjsegmentedtotalbar.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover a segment for its count, % of the bar and residual.

jjwithinstats.name: jjwithinstats
jjwithinstats.core_method: plot first: ggwithinstats paired box-violin with connecting paths. Subtitle: repeated-measures ANOVA (afex), Friedman, WRS2 rmanova or anovaBF; with 2 levels: paired t, signed-rank, Yuen or BF. Pairwise Student, Durbin-Conover or Yuen with p-adjustment. Its own 'Paired Changes' table gives mean/median/Hodges-Lehmann changes with a t, signed-rank (normal approximation) or seeded whole-case bootstrap CI, plus geometric-mean time ratios.
jjwithinstats.oracle: statsExpressions::oneway_anova(paired = TRUE), statsExpressions::two_sample_test(paired = TRUE), statsExpressions::pairwise_comparisons (PMCMRplus::durbinAllPairsTest, WRS2::rmmcp), WRS2::rmanova, stats::wilcox.test(paired, conf.int = TRUE, exact = FALSE, correct = TRUE), DescTools::HodgesLehmann
jjwithinstats.gain: None for the figure. The Paired Changes table alone is implementable (Walsh-average median, a brentq-inverted signed-rank CI, scipy bootstrap) but adds nothing over R. Dynamic idea: hover a path to highlight one case across time points.

jwaffle.name: jwaffle
jwaffle.core_method: plot only: waffle chart of category proportions (waffle::geom_waffle), with optional facets and count or percent labels.
jwaffle.oracle: none (figure only); the square allocation in waffle::geom_waffle layer data
jwaffle.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover a category to highlight its squares and show n and %.

linechart.name: linechart
linechart.core_method: plot first: line chart by group with CI ribbons, an lm/polynomial trend line and a reference line. A summary table, plus a 'naive' correlation table: Pearson r with CI, Spearman rho (asymptotic when tied), and OLS slope, intercept, R^2 and p, with a caveat that repeated measures are ignored.
linechart.gain: None; the table is direct in scipy but duplicates jmv. Dynamic idea: hover points for the value and CI, toggle groups, and zoom the time axis.

lollipop.name: lollipop
lollipop.core_method: plot only: lollipop chart of a value per category, with optional mean/median aggregation, sorting, highlighting and a reference line. A data summary table gives n, mean, median, SD and quartiles.
lollipop.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover for values and sort interactively.

raincloud.name: raincloud
raincloud.core_method: plot first: ggdist raincloud (half-eye + dots + box). Html panels give per-group n, mean, median, SD, IQR, skewness and kurtosis, then Shapiro-Wilk and Bartlett checks. These choose a t, Welch t or Wilcoxon test, or an ANOVA, Welch ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis, followed by pairwise t or Wilcoxon tests with p-adjustment.
raincloud.oracle: stats::oneway.test, stats::t.test, stats::wilcox.test, stats::kruskal.test, stats::pairwise.t.test, stats::pairwise.wilcox.test, stats::bartlett.test, moments::skewness, moments::kurtosis (= scipy kurtosis(fisher=False))
raincloud.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover dots for case IDs and outliers.

statsplot2.name: statsplot2
statsplot2.core_method: plot only: chooses a ggstatsplot plot from the variable types. Continuous by factor gives ggbetweenstats or ggwithinstats; continuous by continuous gives ggscatterstats; factor by factor gives ggbarstats or an alluvial plot (ggalluvial/easyalluvial). Grouped variants exist, and the statistics come from those engines.
statsplot2.gain: None. Python could only choose the test from the variable types, which R already does.

advancedbarplot.name: advancedbarplot
advancedbarplot.core_method: plot first: bar charts in several styles (ggprism, BBC, ggpattern, patchwork) of mean, median or sum, with SE, SD, CI, MAD or IQR error bars. Optional t, Wilcoxon, ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis p, and an optional plotly widget.
advancedbarplot.oracle: stats::aov, stats::t.test, stats::wilcox.test, stats::kruskal.test, stats::mad (= median_abs_deviation(scale='normal'))
advancedbarplot.gain: None. It already tries interactivity: plotly::ggplotly is pasted into an Html result through htmltools::HTML(as_widget()), without plotly.js. Whether that renders in jamovi is unverified. Test it before investing in any HTML/D3 interactivity.

basegraphics.name: basegraphics
basegraphics.core_method: plot only: base R graphics (histogram, boxplot, scatter, bar, density, pairs and so on), with janitor/labelled name cleaning.
basegraphics.gain: None; base graphics is an R idiom.

bbcplots.name: bbcplots
bbcplots.core_method: plot first: BBC-style ggplots (bbplot::bbc_style, finalise_plot) of bar, line, scatter and box charts, with an optional ANOVA, t, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis or chi-square p in Html. bbplot is GitHub-only; installation appears only as instructions.
bbcplots.gain: None; it is a styling theme. Re-creating the theme in plain ggplot2 would remove a GitHub-only dependency, and that needs no Python.

economistplots.name: economistplots
economistplots.core_method: plot first: ggeconodist Economist-style distribution plots (10th/50th/90th percentile bars), with skewness and outlier notes and an optional t, Wilcoxon, ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis p. ggeconodist is GitHub-only.

esquisseauto.name: esquisseauto
esquisseauto.core_method: plot only: esquisse::potential_geoms and ggcall build an automatic ggplot from the selected variables' types.
esquisseauto.gain: None; this is R-only ggplot code generation.

ggprism.name: ggprism
ggprism.core_method: plot first: GraphPad Prism-style ggplots (theme_prism, prism palettes, guides, brackets) with mean CIs from t.test and an optional t, Wilcoxon, ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis p.

grafify.name: grafify
grafify.core_method: plot first: grafify plots (scatter or dot with bar, box or violin; before-after; 3d/4d scatterbar; density; histogram; xy) plus a one- or two-way ANOVA (aov) with grafify post-hoc comparisons (emmeans: pairwise, levelwise, vs reference, trends).
needs: emmeans-style contrasts and grafify's default p-adjustment as own code (statsmodels optional)
grafify.gain: None; jmv ANOVA covers this. scipy's tukey_hsd and dunnett cover only the classic adjustments, not emmeans contrasts with grafify's defaults.

groupedbar.name: groupedbar
groupedbar.core_method: plot first: grouped bar chart of mean, median, sum or count with SD, SE or t-CI error bars, and a descriptives table. Each item gets a one-way ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Welch t or Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Partial stub: the 'chisq' and 'fisher' choices (and 'auto' for factor items) have no branch, so they produce nothing, and the post-hoc table is never filled.
groupedbar.gain: None; fix the dead options in R instead.

jcomplexupset.name: jcomplexupset
jcomplexupset.core_method: plot only: UpSet plot of set intersections from binary membership columns (ComplexUpset: intersection sizes, ratios and percentages; set sizes; sorting and filtering).
needs: plot renderer (excluded from effort; Python upsetplot also needs matplotlib)
jcomplexupset.gain: None numerically. A strong dynamic candidate: click an intersection bar to list or highlight its cases, and hover for size and %. This needs an Html result type in ClinicoPathPj.

jextractggstats.name: jextractggstats
jextractggstats.core_method: Runs a ggstatsplot function (between, within, correlation, histogram, scatter, bar, contingency, one-sample) and prints ggstatsplot::extract_stats (subtitle, caption, pairwise and descriptive data frames) as Html. It is a ggstatsplot introspection tool.
jextractggstats.gain: None. Its purpose is to show ggstatsplot's own numbers, so a Python reimplementation would no longer be an extraction. It is, however, the natural oracle harness if the ggstatsplot tests are ever ported.

jforester.name: jforester
jforester.core_method: plot first: forest plot of user-supplied study estimates and CIs (log scale, weights proportional to n, stripes, arrows). The user types in the summary diamond. The 'heterogeneity' Q and I^2 use sample-size-proportion weights instead of inverse-variance weights, so the Q, p and I^2 it shows are not valid meta-analytic statistics.
jforester.oracle: metafor::rma(yi, sei, method = 'FE', 'DL' or 'REML') for a correct Q, I^2 and tau^2
jforester.gain: None for the figure. The fix (SE from the CI, inverse-variance FE or DerSimonian-Laird pooling, Q, I^2, tau^2) is short in either language. ClinicoPath already ships metafor-based analyses (metaanalysis, treatmentmeta).

jforestmodel.name: jforestmodel
jforestmodel.core_method: plot first: fits lm, glm (chosen family) or survival::coxph and draws forestmodel::forest_model. Tables: model summary (R^2 or deviance), coefficients (exponentiated for glm and Cox, with confint CIs), and diagnostics (AIC etc.).
jforestmodel.oracle: stats::lm, stats::glm + confint (profile likelihood), survival::coxph, forestmodel::forest_model
jforestmodel.gain: None; regression already exists in jmv and ClinicoPath. Matching confint.glm's profile-likelihood CIs and coxph's Efron ties would be own code.

jggheatmap.name: jggheatmap
jggheatmap.core_method: plot first: ggplot heatmap of a matrix (wide variables, or long row/col/value) with optional row or column z-scaling. Hierarchical clustering uses hclust with the chosen linkage on dist or 1 - Pearson/Spearman distances, and drives the dendrogram ordering. The cluster table is cut at a hard-coded k = min(3, n).
jggheatmap.gain: None numerically. The clustering is direct in scipy, but leaf order differs from hclust, and R's 'ward.D' has no scipy equivalent (scipy 'ward' = R 'ward.D2'). Dynamic idea: hover cells for values, click a dendrogram branch to select a cluster, and choose k interactively instead of the fixed 3.

jggstats.name: jggstats
jggstats.core_method: plot first: the ggstats suite. ggcoef_model and ggcoef_compare on lm, glm, coxph, lmer or glmer (with broom tidy/glance tables), plus gglikert, stat_prop, stat_cross (chi-square residuals), stat_weighted_mean and cascade plots.
needs: mixed models: statsmodels MixedLM for lmer; no exact Python equivalent of glmer (Laplace)
jggstats.oracle: ggstats::ggcoef_model, broom::tidy, broom::glance, stats::glm, survival::coxph, lme4::lmer, lme4::glmer
jggstats.gain: None. It is an R-only visual grammar, and the mixed-model paths would be hard to port.

jjcoefstats.name: jjcoefstats
jjcoefstats.core_method: plot first: ggcoefstats coefficient forest plot, either from pre-computed estimates, SEs, CIs and p, or from a fitted lm, binomial glm, coxph or lmer/glmer (broom or broom.mixed tidy). Coefficient and model-fit tables.
needs: statsmodels MixedLM for lmer; no exact Python equivalent of glmer
jjcoefstats.oracle: ggstatsplot::ggcoefstats, broom::tidy, broom.mixed::tidy, stats::lm, stats::glm, survival::coxph, lme4::lmer, lme4::glmer
jjcoefstats.gain: None. The pre-computed mode is pure plotting, and the model paths duplicate the regression analyses.

jjpubr.name: jjpubr
jjpubr.core_method: plot first: ggpubr publication plots (box, violin, scatter with stat_cor and marginals, histogram, density, bar, dot, line, error plot) with stat_compare_means (t, Wilcoxon, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis). Tables of descriptives, test statistics and Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation; Levene check.

jjradarplot.name: jjradarplot
jjradarplot.core_method: plot only: radar (spider) chart of the per-group mean or median of several variables, optionally min-max scaled to [0, 1].
jjradarplot.gain: None. Dynamic idea: hover a vertex for the raw value, and toggle groups.

jjsyndromicplot.name: jjsyndromicplot
jjsyndromicplot.core_method: plot first: PCA (stats::prcomp, centred and/or scaled) with component loadings and VAF. A syndromic plot (syndRomics style) shows one PC's loadings above a cutoff; there is a loadings table.
jjsyndromicplot.gain: None numerically. PCA is direct via SVD, but loading signs are arbitrary and must be aligned to prcomp. Dynamic idea: hover arrows for exact loadings, and a live cutoff slider.

jjtreemap.name: jjtreemap
jjtreemap.core_method: plot only: treemap of category sizes (treemap::treemap pivotSize layout with ggfittext labels), with optional subgroup nesting and colour by value.
needs: own pivot-by-size layout (Python squarify implements only the squarified algorithm)
jjtreemap.oracle: treemap::treemap (rectangle coordinates in its returned tm data frame)
jjtreemap.gain: None numerically. Dynamic idea: zoomable drill-down into subgroups, and hover for n and %.

jscattermore.name: jscattermore
jscattermore.core_method: plot only: rasterised scatter for very large n (scattermore::geom_scattermore, geom_scattermost, scattermoreplot) with colour and size mapping.
jscattermore.gain: None from Python; this is a rendering problem. A canvas or WebGL HTML scatter would add pan, zoom and hover on 10^5 to 10^6 points.

jsjplot.name: jsjplot
jsjplot.core_method: R-ecosystem wrapper: sjPlot tab_model regression tables and plot_model coefficient, interaction and marginal-effects plots (lm/glm), plus frequency tables, a correlation matrix and a PCA plot.
needs: no Python equivalent of sjPlot/ggeffects marginal effects (statsmodels only partly)

jviolin.name: jviolin
jviolin.core_method: plot only: violin plot (geom_violin with an hrbrthemes theme) with optional boxplot, points and quantile lines. Known bug: the quantile_lines string option is never parsed (in-code TODO).

parallelplot.name: parallelplot
parallelplot.core_method: plot only: parallel-coordinates plot of several numeric variables (z-score, min-max or [-1, 1] scaling) coloured by group, plus a variable summary table.
parallelplot.gain: None numerically, but this is the textbook case for interactivity: brush on axes to filter cases, re-order axes, and highlight one patient's line (HTML/D3; needs an Html result type in ClinicoPathPj).

pcaloadingheatmap.name: pcaloadingheatmap
pcaloadingheatmap.core_method: plot first: PCA (stats::prcomp) loadings, computed as rotation x sdev, shown as a heatmap and a bar map, plus a variance-explained table.
pcaloadingheatmap.gain: None numerically (PCA via SVD, sign-aligned to prcomp). Dynamic idea: hover cells for loadings, and a slider for the number of components.

tidyplots.name: tidyplots
tidyplots.core_method: plot only: tidyplots pipeline (points, jitter or beeswarm; bars, box, violin; lines, areas, curve fit; pie or donut) with mean/median and SEM, SD or CI95 error bars, plus optional add_test_pvalue or asterisks.

facts: Method: client bundles in /Applications/jamovi.app/Contents/Resources/jamovi/client/dist/assets (resultsview-CDm5kSBa.js, analysisui-DyZ6n9l6.js, main-RVur5Zlb.js, highcontrast-DQVdg4nC.js); server in .../Resources/jamovi/server/jamovi/server; jamovi's bundled jmvcore 28.3 (.../Resources/modules/base/R/jmvcore, built 2026-10-15) was read by decoding its lazy-load DB with /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-serdarbalci-Documents-GitHub-ClinicoPathJamoviModule/4bfabdde-8e9b-4965-bbff-ea5258db43d7/scratchpad/rprobe/rdb.py. One R process was used (it printed versions, then stopped on a helper bug). Nothing in any repo was modified.

Q1, scripts: inline <script> in Html results DOES execute in 28.13. The Html view's render() parses content with htmlTrusted() (highcontrast: `document.createElement(`template`);t.innerHTML=e.trim()`, which is inert), inserts it, then re-creates each script: `for(let e of n){let t=document.createElement(`script`);t.textContent=e.textContent,document.head.appendChild(t),t.parentNode.removeChild(t),e.parentNode.removeChild(e)}`. Only textContent is copied: src= and type= are dropped, so <script src=...> loads nothing and a <script type='application/json'> block is run as JavaScript. The Svg view's _runScripts() does the same.

Module JS/CSS assets: the Html and Svg views load element.scripts as `<script src=module/${e} class=module-asset>` in <head> and await them before inserting content. Server server.py module_asset serves `os.path.join(module_path, 'R', analysis.ns, path)`, which is the package's inst/ (installed ClinicoPathPj: modules/ClinicoPathPj/R/ClinicoPathPj/python/...). jmvcore 28.3 Html has setScripts(), setStylesheets() and knit(). The r.yaml Html/Svg schemas have no scripts key, so assets are attached from R.

Q1, arbitraryCode: script execution is not tied to it. resultsview-CDm5kSBa.js contains 0 occurrences of arbitraryCode. The flag only (a) makes the server refuse the run when config allow_arbitrary_code is false (engine.py: 'Analyses which execute arbitrary code are not permitted in this session.') and (b) makes such analyses load from a file disabled (analyses.py `enabled = not arbitrary_code`), behind the banner 'One or more analyses in this data set have been disabled because they allow the execution of arbitrary code'. ClinicoPathPj runs only module-shipped Python, so it should not set arbitraryCode.

Q1, sandbox and CSP: each analysis's results are a separate iframe, `sandbox:`allow-scripts allow-same-origin`` (main-RVur5Zlb.js), served from a different origin (server.py runs main, analysisui and resultsview on three ports for an IP host). resultsview.html is served with CSP `default-src 'self'; font-src 'self' data:; img-src 'self' data:; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' data:`. Inline scripts and eval are allowed; CDN scripts, external fetch/XHR and remote images are blocked. D3 must therefore ship inside the module; Pj inlines d3 v7.9.0 (279,706 bytes) into every chart.

The results iframe exposes window.setOption(name,value), window.setParam(address,options), window.getParam(address,name) and window.openUrl(url), all by postMessage to the main window. main-RVur5Zlb.js _messageEvent matches e.source to the sending iframe and runs `case`setOption`:l[a.name]=a.value,c.setOptions(l)` on that analysis. There is no option allow-list. Tables use the same call for rowSelect and sortSelect.

Export behaviour: the export hydrator maps an Svg element to `{type:`image`,...}` with `resource=e.svg.path`. An Html element becomes text paragraphs parsed from its source string (Oe), or the raw source when copying. The docx and odt writers emit only group, image, table, preformatted and text items. Script-drawn Html charts are therefore lost in Word/ODT export, while Svg charts export as images. On .omv save the client calls getSvgs() and posts each rendered SVG as form field svg:<part>; analysis.py set_svg stores it ('an Svg element is drawn by the client, so the client is the only place its svg can come from'). The Svg view falls back to that stored file (fetch(res/path)) when content is empty or module scripts fail to load.

Svg status: it is in the jmvtools 28.4 schemas (resultsschema.yaml enum; resultelementschemas.yaml Svg {content}), in jmvcore 28.3 (Svg inherits Html; saveAs rejects 'svg elements cannot be saved by the engine') and in the 28.13 server and client. There is no dev.jamovi.org page for it. The umbrella guide vignettes/jamovi_module_patterns_guide.md lists it under 'Exists Upstream, Not Yet Documented ... Do not use them'. The earliest jamovi version that supports it was not verified.
Size cap: engine.py sets `nanomsg.RCVMAXSIZE, 4 * 1024 * 1024` on the engine socket, so a whole results tree, Html/Svg content included, must stay well under 4 MB.

Q3, checkpoint (jmvcore 28.3, decoded): `.checkpoint=function(flush=TRUE){ if (is.null(private$.checkpointCB)) return(); if (flush) results <- RProtoBuf_serialize(self$asProtoBuf(includeState=FALSE), NULL); cmd <- private$.checkpointCB(results); if (is.character(cmd) && cmd == 'restart') { self$setStatus('restarting'); stop(jmvcore::createError('restarting', 'restart')) } }`. Analysis$run() returns FALSE when status is 'restarting'. Outside the engine the callback is NULL, so checkpoint is a no-op.

Q3, option change during a run: engine.py run() calls `self._current_analysis.cancel()` (the server-side wait task) and sends the new request on the same socket; responses with a stale revision are ignored. The R process is never interrupted. ClinicoPathPj's bridge blocks in `system2(..., timeout = .cpjTimeout)` with `.cpjTimeout <- 60` (R/utils-python.R), so the new run waits until Python returns. Only a .checkpoint() call can abort a run early.

Q3, packages: jamovi's base R library (modules/base/R, on R_LIBS in Contents/Resources/env.conf) contains processx 3.9.0, callr 3.7.6, ps 1.9.3, digest 0.6.39, jsonlite 2.0.0, ggplot2, ragg, openxlsx and jmvReadWrite. modules/jmv/R adds later 1.4.8, promises 1.5.0, websocket, V8, htmlwidgets and reactable. jamovi-compiler/snapshots.js (jmvtools 28.4) lists these in R460base/R460jmv and filters them out of installation, so declaring processx in Imports does not bundle it into the .jmo.

Engine lockdown: the jamovi-engine binary embeds R code that always replaces install.packages, update.packages, download.packages and remove.packages with stop('<fn>() is not permitted in jamovi R'). Next to the string JAMOVI_EXTRA_LOCKDOWN it does the same for base source, library, system, system2, shell, shell.exec, download.file and url; that this is conditional is inferred from the string order. The desktop env.conf does not set JAMOVI_EXTRA_LOCKDOWN, which is why system2 works there. Where it is set (likely jamovi cloud), a Python bridge should refuse rather than route around it with processx.

Engines: session.py `Scheduler(1, 3, ...)` gives 4 engine processes (1 init slot, 3 run slots). A request goes to whichever slot is free, so any in-R cache or warm worker exists per engine. jmvcore Analysis$.getSessionTemp() returns a session temp directory shared by all engines.

Measured with the bundled Python 3.11.9 (3 runs): interpreter start 0.02 s, import numpy 0.06-0.12 s, import scipy.stats 0.70-0.96 s. That is about 0.8-1.1 s per ClinicoPathPj run before any statistics. The trimmed stdlib has json, select, selectors, socket, threading, hashlib, signal, subprocess and multiprocessing; sqlite3 is missing. All scipy subpackages import.

Q3, state: analyses.py create_from_serial says 'the state can't come from a file: a crafted .omv could otherwise run arbitrary R code when the state is restored ... the analysis has to run from scratch before anything which needs the state'. Saved results (tables, image paths, Html/Svg content) are still shown on open. Within a session, ResultsElement$fromProtoBuf restores an element's state unless one of its clearWith options changed. jmvcore warns when the compressed state exceeds 500000 bytes. A hidden `type: State` results element (jmvcore State) can hold a cache.

Q2, actions: the option schema allows only `action: open | openExternal`. jmvcore 28.3 OptionAction$perform() creates a hidden Array of Action results. open writes the data frame with jmvReadWrite::write_omv and the client calls requestOpen (new window). openExternal and export move the file into <sessionTemp>/external/; the client then calls P.openFile (OS application; download in a browser) or P.exportFile (save dialog, then 'Exported to {filename}'). The client reads Action elements only inside top-level Arrays. The server resets Action options after every run ('set action options back to false') and on .omv load. Pj builds export at run time with `jmvcore::OptionAction$new(name='saveEditorScript', value=TRUE, action='export')`. Docs: open needs 2.7.12 and openExternal 28.4; export arrived in 28.7 per the release note. openExternal opens only listed extensions (pdf, docx, csv, xlsx, json, svg, png, zip, ...), not html.

Q2, dependent controls (analysisui-DyZ6n9l6.js): a value is a binding only when `t.startsWith(`(`)&&t.endsWith(`)`)`. Operands are name, name:value (compared with loose ==), !, nested parentheses, and {js} code compiled with Function(`ui`, code). && and || are folded strictly left to right. Option controls register enable but have no visible property, so controls can be greyed out but not hidden. List controls ignore enable (`else if(e!==`enable`&&e===`infoText`...)`).

Q2, events.js (jus 3.0): the compiler loads jamovi/js/<analysis>.js as `this.handlers = require('./<basename>')`. The client auto-binds handler keys <control>_<event> and view_<event> (`mt={OptionControl:[`changed`,`changing`],...,root:[`loaded`,`updated`,`remoteDataChanged`,`creating`]}`). From the options panel, code can call requestData('columns'), requestData('column', {columnName, properties:[...]}) and requestAction('createColumn' | 'selectFiles').

Q2, dropdowns from data: LevelSelector fills from `requestData(`column`,{columnName:n,properties:[`measureType`,`levels`]})`. allowNone adds '- None -', which maps to null; without it the control auto-selects levels[defaultLevelIndex] (default 0). jmvcore OptionList rejects any value outside its declared list ('Argument {a} must be one of {options}'), so List dropdowns cannot be filled from data. OptionLevel has no check, so the backend must validate the level.

ClinicoPathPj's generated .u.yaml files say compilerMode: aggressive, and jamovi-compiler uicompiler.js then discards the existing UI (`if (uiData === null || uiData.compilerMode === 'aggressive') uiData = {..., children: []}`). enable bindings, CollapseBox, ModeSelector (form: listbox | radio | tabs), defaultLevelIndex and events.js therefore require the generator to write .u.yaml itself in tame mode. The schema and client support for CollapseBox (collapsed, label) and ModeSelector is present.

Not usable as hoped: the analysis key `pause:` is accepted by the compiler but nothing in the 28.13 client or server reads it. `passive: true` (server options.py: a change to a passive option triggers no run) compiles only on Group and Sort options, because all other option schemas set additionalProperties: false. There is no analysis progress API: jmvcore 28.3 has no progress function, and ComsMessage progress/progressTotal feed only client requests such as open and save. An element with status 'running' shows a spinner (jmv-results-status-running).

Q2, other features: Image `mode: vector` is handled in jmvcore .createImage: `if (vector) grDevices::svg(filename=fullPath, width=width / ppi, height=height / ppi, bg='transparent') else ragg::agg_png(...)`, and renderers receive image, theme and ggtheme. Text results are rendered by marked (`gfm:!0,breaks:!1`) and then an element allow-list, so they cannot run scripts. The File option resolves to <sessionTemp>/<id> in jmvcore OptionFile and rejects 'The file {filename} needs to be re-selected' when the file is missing; the dev docs say it needs jamovi 28.4 and that the file is written into the .omv.

Table rowSelect and sortSelect are implemented but undocumented. jmvcore 28.3 has `Table$new(..., rowSelect='', sortSelect='')`, and rowSelected is the bound option's value + 1. The client's onRowSelect calls window.setOption(rowSelect, index), and clicking the already-selected row sends -1. A sortable column header calls window.setOption(sortSelect, {sortBy, sortDesc}).

features.name: Narrative interpretation paragraph (Text / Markdown result)
features.user_gets: A plain-language sentence or short paragraph under the tables, e.g. 'Mean Ki-67 was 4.1 points higher in grade 3 than in grade 2 tumours; Welch t = 2.8, df = 41.3, p = .008'. It wraps, supports bold, italic and lists, and exports to Word and PDF as text.
features.evidence: jmvcore 28.3 exports Text. resultelementschemas.yaml defines `Text: name, title, content, visible, clearWith, refs`. highcontrast-DQVdg4nC.js Dt() runs `q.parse(String(e),{gfm:!0,breaks:!1,async:!1})` and then an element allow-list. dev.jamovi.org reference/api/text.md: 'Available in jamovi 28.3 and newer'. The docx and odt writers handle type==='text'.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC result {'type': 'Text', 'name': 'interpretation', 'title': 'Interpretation'} becomes r.yaml type: Text. Runtime API out.markdown('interpretation', text), plus a cpj_runtime md_escape() helper for column names and level labels. Bridge: self$results$get(name)$setContent(text). minApp is already 28.3.0.
features.risks: Unescaped *, _ or [..](..) in user strings get formatted. HTML entities are not decoded. The wording must be built from the computed numbers only. Messages stay English-only, like the rest of the Python output.

features.name: Explicit event/positive level choice (LevelSelector allowNone + pending state)
features.user_gets: For an event, positive class or 'abnormal' level, the dropdown starts at '- None -'. The analysis then lists the levels with their counts and asks for a choice, instead of silently using the first level.
features.evidence: analysisui-DyZ6n9l6.js LevelSelector: `this.getPropertyValue(`allowNone`)&&this.input.append(t(`option`,{},this.none))`, and choosing '- None -' calls setValue(null). Without allowNone it sets `this.levels[e].label`, where e is defaultLevelIndex (default 0). jmvcore 28.3 OptionLevel has no .check. Project memory feedback_event_value_never_inferred: the levels[0] auto-fill is a GUI-only defect that R tests cannot see.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: The generator already passes allowNone through. Add a SPEC key role: 'event' | 'positive' that forces allowNone: true. The bridge treats None as pending: an INFO notice plus a small level/count table, and the test itself is not run. The runtime checks that the chosen label exists in Factor.levels.
features.risks: A Level is always a required argument of the generated R wrapper. R tests always pass a level, so a GUI check is still needed. A reference-group Level (as in pywelch) may keep a default, but a note should say which level was used.

features.name: Cancellable Python runs (processx polling + private$.checkpoint)
features.user_gets: Changing an option while Python is still working stops the stale run within about 0.1 s and starts the new one. Today the engine can stay busy for up to the 60 s timeout. This matters most for slow methods such as bootstrap, permutation or exact tests.
features.evidence: engine.py run() calls `self._current_analysis.cancel()` and sends the new request on the same socket, so the R process keeps running. jmvcore 28.3 .checkpoint(): `cmd <- private$.checkpointCB(results); if (is.character(cmd) && cmd == 'restart') { self$setStatus('restarting'); stop(jmvcore::createError('restarting', 'restart')) }`. processx 3.9.0 is in modules/base/R and in jamovi-compiler snapshots.js R460base, so it is not bundled. ClinicoPathPj R/utils-python.R blocks in system2(..., timeout = .cpjTimeout).
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: Bridge change. Start Python with p <- processx::process$new(python$path, args, env = ..., stdout = '|', stderr = '|', cleanup_tree = TRUE), and kill it on exit with p$kill_tree(). Loop while (p$is_alive()) { p$poll_io(100); checkpoint(); check the timeout }. The generated .b.R passes checkpoint = function() private$.checkpoint(flush = FALSE) into .cpjRun(). The restart condition must escape every tryCatch (re-raise when identical(e$code, 'restart')). Add processx to DESCRIPTION Imports.
features.risks: A tryCatch that catches the restart turns an option change into an error or keeps a stale loop alive (umbrella review guide §15-18). processx inside the jamovi engine (empty PATH, PYTHONHOME set) is unverified, so probe it first. flush = TRUE re-serialises the whole results tree on every call. Where JAMOVI_EXTRA_LOCKDOWN disables system/system2, refuse rather than bypass it.

features.name: Warm Python worker per engine
features.user_gets: Option clicks return in tens of milliseconds instead of about 1 s, because numpy and scipy.stats are imported once per engine rather than on every run.
features.evidence: Measured with jamovi's Python 3.11.9: interpreter start 0.02 s, import numpy 0.06-0.12 s, import scipy.stats 0.70-0.96 s. Engines are long-lived R processes that keep module namespaces loaded, and session.py `Scheduler(1, 3, ...)` gives 4 of them. The bundled stdlib has json, select, selectors, threading, hashlib and signal; sqlite3 is missing.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: Bridge keeps one processx process per engine in a package-level environment, started as 'cpj_runtime.py --serve' with stdin/stdout pipes and supervise = TRUE. Protocol: one line per request naming the request/response JSON files, and one DONE line back. The runtime re-loads the analysis file for each request (no cross-request globals), exits on stdin EOF or after an idle limit, and answers a version handshake so that a module update restarts it. On restart or timeout the bridge kills the worker, and the next run starts a new one. This depends on cancellable runs.
features.risks: Data or results can leak between analyses if analysis code keeps module-level state. Up to four resident Python processes hold numpy and scipy in memory. A hard-killed engine can orphan the worker (mitigated by stdin-EOF exit and supervise). A broken worker must be replaced, not reused. It is harder to test than one process per run.

features.name: Native plots drawn by R/ggplot2 from Python-computed data (Image, optional mode: vector)
features.user_gets: Forest plots, Kaplan-Meier-style step curves, ROC curves, box/violin plots, waterfall and bar charts. They resize, follow the jamovi theme and palette, and copy or export to Word and PDF like any jamovi plot.
features.evidence: jmvcore 28.3 Analysis$.createImage: `if (vector) grDevices::svg(filename=fullPath, width=width / ppi, height=height / ppi, bg='transparent') else if (requireNamespace('ragg', quietly=TRUE)) ragg::agg_png(...)`, and it calls `render(image, theme=t$theme, ggtheme=t$ggtheme, ...)`. ggplot2 and ragg are in modules/base/R. The compiler Image schema has mode: raster|vector, renderFun and requiresData. The docx and odt writers export type==='image'.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC result {'type': 'Image', 'name': 'forest', 'plot': 'forest', 'width': 600, 'height': 400} becomes an r.yaml Image with a renderFun and requiresData: false. Runtime API out.plot('forest', rows=[...]), checked against the columns each plot kind needs. The bridge calls image$setState() with a small base data.frame. One shared R renderer file (R/utils-plots.R) holds a ggplot builder per plot kind and applies ggtheme last.
features.risks: State is dropped when an .omv is reopened, so a resize or export after reopening re-runs Python. Keep state small (jmvcore warns above 500000 bytes). Use mode: vector only for plots with a bounded number of marks. The drawing code is R, not Python.

features.name: Computed columns written back to the spreadsheet (Output)
features.user_gets: A tick box such as 'Save risk group' adds a column (H-score, Ki-67 category, predicted probability, outlier flag) to the data. Users can analyse it with other ClinicoPath or jamovi analyses, and it is saved in the .omv.
features.evidence: dev.jamovi.org reference/api/option-output.md and learn/tutorial/tuts0202a-output-variables.md: 'setRowNums() uses these row names to map each computed value back to the correct row'. The compiler Output schema has measureType: nominal|ordinal|continuous. The protobuf has ResultsOutputs {outputs, rowNums}. Pj fills Output columns from Python results (R/mzPj_results_service.R: output$set(...), output$setRowNums(rowNums), output$setValues()).
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC result {'type': 'Output', 'name': 'riskGroup', 'title': 'Risk group', 'measureType': 'ordinal'}; the generator writes the paired .a.yaml Output option and .r.yaml Output result. Runtime API out.column('riskGroup', values), which checks that the length equals the number of rows sent. Bridge: if (self$options$riskGroup && el$isNotFilled()) { el$setRowNums(rownames(self$data)); el$setValues(values) }.
features.risks: Misaligned row numbers fail silently (filters, excluded rows). Categorical outputs need an explicit level order. A derived clinical variable tends to be reused without its provenance, so fill varDescription with the method and module version.

features.name: Generator-owned options panel: dependent controls, collapsible sections, tabs, default level
features.user_gets: Controls are greyed out until they apply (e.g. the CI level until 'Show CI' is ticked). Advanced settings sit in collapsible sections and alternative methods appear as tabs. pywelch can default the reference to the second level, so its sign matches jamovi's own t-test.
features.evidence: ClinicoPathPj jamovi/pywelch.u.yaml has compilerMode: aggressive, and uicompiler.js then discards the UI: `if (uiData === null || uiData.compilerMode === 'aggressive') uiData = {..., children: []}`. uictrlschemas.yaml has OptionControl.enable, CollapseBox {collapsed, label}, ModeSelector {options, form: listbox|radio|tabs} and LevelSelector {defaultLevelIndex}. In analysisui-DyZ6n9l6.js, isValueDataBound requires outer parentheses, and {js} operands are compiled with Function(`ui`, code).
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC keys per option: enable: '(showCI)', section: 'Advanced', collapsed: true, defaultLevelIndex: 1. The generator writes jamovi/<name>.u.yaml with jus: '3.0' and compilerMode: tame. It rejects bindings without outer parentheses, with unknown names, with == or !=, mixing && and || at one level, or placed on a list box. The bridge ignores the values of disabled options.
features.risks: A disabled control keeps its value and still reaches Python. Binding mistakes are silent: the control stays enabled, or a CheckBox freezes at its default. The options panel has enable only, no visible: binding. In tame mode jmvtools may still add or remove controls, so generate.py --check must run after prepare.

features.name: Input-hash result cache (hidden State element)
features.user_gets: Display-only toggles (console, which tables or plots to show, plot styling) redraw immediately. Slow computations such as bootstrap or permutation tests are not repeated for unchanged inputs within a session.
features.evidence: jmvcore 28.3 State is a hidden ResultsElement. ResultsElement$fromProtoBuf skips restoring when `base::any(oChanges %in% private$.clearWith)`, otherwise it restores the state with readRDS(memDecompress(...)). asProtoBuf warns `if (length(state) > 500000)`. Server analyses.py drops all state when an .omv is opened. rlang (a jmvcore import) and digest are in modules/base/R.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: The generator adds a hidden r.yaml item {'name': 'cpjCache', 'type': 'State', 'clearWith': [every option not marked display: true]}. The bridge hashes the full request JSON (data, options and runtime version) with rlang::hash(). When the key matches it reuses state$response; otherwise it runs Python and calls setState(list(key = key, response = json)). A SPEC option flag display: true keeps that option out of both the request and clearWith.
features.risks: Numbers go stale if the key misses anything Python reads, so hash everything that is sent. The first run after reopening an .omv always recomputes. Skip caching responses close to 500 KB. An option marked display-only must really change no statistic.

features.name: Click-a-row drill-down tables (Table rowSelect)
features.user_gets: In a screening table (one row per marker, cut-off or subgroup), clicking a row selects it and fills a detail table or plot for that row below. Clicking it again clears the selection.
features.evidence: The compiler Table schema has rowSelect (a '(optionName)' pattern) and sortSelect. jmvcore 28.3 has `Table$new(..., rowSelect='', sortSelect='')`, and rowSelected is `private$.options$eval(private$.rowSelect, silent=TRUE) + 1`. resultsview-CDm5kSBa.js onRowSelect: `r===t.rowSelected?window.setOption(t.rowSelect,-1):window.setOption(t.rowSelect,r)`. dev.jamovi.org does not document it.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: The generator gains an Integer option type (hidden, default -1) and a Table key rowSelect: 'selectedRow', emitted as rowSelect: (selectedRow). Python reads options['selectedRow'] (0-based, -1 = none) and fills the detail results.
features.risks: Undocumented, so it may change. Every click is a full re-run, so it needs the warm worker or the cache to feel responsive. The index refers to row order: validate it in Python and do not combine it naively with sorting.

features.name: Action buttons: open a derived data set, open or save files
features.user_gets: Buttons such as 'Open matched cohort as a new data set' (new jamovi window), 'Open table in Excel', or 'Save case classifications...' (save dialog).
features.evidence: The option schema allows `action: enum [open, openExternal]`. In jmvcore 28.3 OptionAction$perform, open calls jmvReadWrite::write_omv(...), and `if (private$.action %in% c('openExternal', 'export'))` moves the file to <sessionTemp>/external/. main-RVur5Zlb.js resultsAction handler: open calls a.requestOpen(...), openExternal calls P.openFile(...), export calls P.exportFile(...) and shows 'Exported to {filename}'. The server clears Action options after every run. Pj creates export at run time with jmvcore::OptionAction$new(name='saveEditorScript', value=TRUE, action='export').
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC option {'type': 'Action', 'name': 'saveGroups', 'title': 'Save...', 'action': 'open' | 'openExternal' | 'export'}. For export the generator writes openExternal in the YAML, and the .b.R swaps in OptionAction$new(..., action = 'export') at run time, as Pj does. Runtime APIs: out.dataset(columns) for open, out.file(filename, text) for CSV; XLSX would go through R's openxlsx. The bridge calls option$perform(function(action) { write to action$params$fullPath; list(filename = ...) }). minApp 28.4.0, or 28.7 for export.
features.risks: A click is an option change, so the whole analysis, Python included, re-runs. html is not on openExternal's allowed extension list. The export workaround relies on undocumented jmvcore behaviour. Patient-level files leave jamovi.

features.name: Reference files next to the data (File option)
features.user_gets: Load a CSV or JSON alongside the data: published model coefficients for externally validating a nomogram, a standard population for age-standardised rates, lab reference intervals, or a morphology recode map. The file is saved inside the .omv.
