features.evidence: dev.jamovi.org reference/api/option-file.md: 'Available in jamovi 28.4 and newer' and 'The file is written into the .omv when the analysis is saved'. jmvcore 28.3 OptionFile resolves to file.path(analysis$.getSessionTemp(), file$id) and rejects 'The file {filename} needs to be re-selected'. The client File control calls requestAction('selectFiles', {multiple, extensions}). Server analyses.py keep_file_ids drops files that are not in the session.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC option {'type': 'File', 'name': 'coefs', 'title': 'Model coefficients', 'extensions': ['json', 'csv']} becomes an .a.yaml File option. The bridge sends {path, filename} or None. Runtime helpers read_table(path) and read_json(path) check size and structure. Raise minApp to 28.4.0.
features.risks: minApp applies to the whole module. extensions only filter the file browser, so the content must be validated. A file containing patient data gets embedded in the .omv. Never unpickle, eval or exec a user file; that would also require arbitraryCode.

features.name: Progress and progressive results for long runs
features.user_gets: A status line such as 'Bootstrap 400/2000...', and tables that appear as soon as each part is ready, instead of a long spinner.
features.evidence: jmvcore 28.3 has no progress API. ComsMessage progress/progressTotal only feed request promises in main-RVur5Zlb.js (`r.onprogress([t.progress,t.progressTotal])`), which are used for open and save. .checkpoint(flush=TRUE) serialises and sends partial results. The results view marks running elements (jmv-results-status-running, data-status=running).
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: Runtime APIs out.progress(fraction, message) and out.flush(table) write JSON lines to stdout. The bridge's polling loop (from the cancellable-runs feature) reads them, updates a hidden Text 'status' item and fills finished tables, then calls private$.checkpoint(flush = TRUE) at most once per second.
features.risks: flush = TRUE re-serialises all results. Partial tables can be mistaken for final ones, so mark them as running and clear the status at the end. It needs streamed output, i.e. processx.

features.name: Interactive D3 charts as Svg results (hover, zoom) that still export as figures
features.user_gets: Hover a point or bar to see the case ID and values (useful for checking outliers in waterfall, swimmer or scatter plots), and zoom. The chart is saved in the .omv as an SVG and copies or exports like an image.
features.evidence: The compiler results enum includes Svg. jmvcore 28.3 Svg inherits Html (setScripts, setStylesheets), and its saveAs rejects 'svg elements cannot be saved by the engine'. The resultsview Svg view awaits module scripts, sets the content, runs inline scripts, and falls back to fetch(res/path). Export (hn) serialises svg.jmv-results-svg-content. main getSvgs() posts svg:<part> on save, and server analysis.py set_svg stores it. There is no dev.jamovi.org page, and the umbrella jamovi_module_patterns_guide.md says 'Exists Upstream, Not Yet Documented ... Do not use them'.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC result {'type': 'Svg', 'chart': 'waterfall'}. Ship inst/js/d3.min.js, inst/js/cpj-charts.js and inst/css/cpj-charts.css once, and attach them with element$setScripts(c('js/d3.min.js', 'js/cpj-charts.js')) and setStylesheets('css/cpj-charts.css'). The content is a <div id='cpj-<uuid>' data-payload='<attribute-escaped JSON>'> followed by <script>cpjCharts.render('cpj-<uuid>')</script>. Do not use a script type=application/json block: the client drops the type and runs it. The chart code draws svg.jmv-results-svg-content and sets labels with .text(). Use minApp 28.13.0 until an older version is checked.
features.risks: Undocumented, and against the current project policy. The SVG is harvested only on .omv save. The JS chart code is outside testthat. Labels from the data must never be inserted as HTML. Inlining D3 (280 KB) per chart instead of loading it as an asset runs into the 4 MB message cap. Colours should match the ggplot plots.

features.name: Charts that set analysis options (window.setOption linkage)
features.user_gets: Clicking a subgroup in a forest plot, or a bar in a chart, selects it and re-runs the analysis to show details for that subgroup.
features.evidence: resultsview-CDm5kSBa.js: `window.setOption=(e,t)=>{this.mainWindow.postMessage({type:`setOption`,data:{name:e,value:t}},`*`)}`. main-RVur5Zlb.js _messageEvent matches e.source to the analysis iframe and runs `case`setOption`:l[a.name]=a.value,c.setOptions(l)` with no allow-list. Inline scripts in Html/Svg results run in that same window.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: Chart JS calls window.setOption('selectedSubgroup', label). The SPEC marks the target as a hidden String or Level option that results may set. Python validates the value against the data before using it. This builds on the D3 chart feature.
features.risks: Internal, undocumented API. Any option of the analysis can be set, so validate on the R/Python side. Each click is a full re-run. Saved Html/Svg scripts also run when an .omv is opened, so keep scripts static and the payload data-only.

features.name: Sortable long result tables (sortSelect)
features.user_gets: Click a column header to sort a long table (e.g. markers by p-value or AUC); the sort order is saved in the .omv.
features.evidence: The compiler Table schema has sortSelect, and columns have sortable: boolean. jmvcore 28.3 Table sortSelected evaluates the bound Sort option. resultsview sort() calls `window.setOption(n.sortSelect,{sortBy:e,sortDesc:t===`desc`})`. The Sort option schema lacks additionalProperties: false, so passive: true compiles.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC table key sortable: true. The generator adds a hidden passive Sort option, sortSelect: (<table>Sort), and sortable: true on the columns. No Python change.
features.risks: Undocumented. Without passive: true every sort would re-run Python. Sorting is presentation only.

features.name: Chart view state kept without re-running (passive options, setParam)
features.user_gets: Zoom level, expanded panels or a chart's selected tab survive saving and reopening without triggering a recomputation.
features.evidence: server options.py: `elif name not in self._options or not self._options[name].passive: changes = True`, and 'results/' options trigger no run except widthScale/heightScale. The results view's window.setParam and window.getParam read and write results/<address>/<name>. The compiler accepts passive only on Group and Sort options. Pj keeps its editor draft in a hidden passive Group (editorState).
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: The generator adds a hidden passive Group option cpjViewState. Chart JS reads it from the payload and writes it with window.setOption, or uses setParam/getParam.
features.risks: Undocumented. The values are stored in the .omv. The benefit is cosmetic.

features.name: Custom option logic in events.js
features.user_gets: Smarter panels: e.g. choosing a method fills in its recommended settings, or a custom list refreshes when the data change.
features.evidence: uicompiler.js createConstructorCode emits `this.handlers = require('./<basename>')` for jamovi/js/<name>.js when jus is 3 or higher. The analysisui mt map binds <control>_changed, <control>_changing, view_loaded, view_updated, view_remoteDataChanged and view_creating. requestData('column', {columnName, properties}) returns any column property. Pj batches option writes with ui.view.model.options.beginEdit()/endEdit().
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: An optional hand-written jamovi/js/<name>.js per analysis that the generator references. Limit it to explicit user actions. Add no SPEC key until a concrete need appears.
features.risks: testthat cannot reach it. A handler that rewrites values (clamping, auto-fill) silently changes the statistics; the cotest analysis did exactly this until it was removed. Handlers do not run when an .omv is reopened, but they do run on undo.

features.name: Free-form interactive Html widgets (Pj style)
features.user_gets: Interactive explorers inside the results (linked D3 views, collapsible panels), meant for exploration rather than reporting.
features.evidence: The resultsview Html render() re-creates each inline script and appends it to document.head. Pj mzPj_plots.py builds `'<script>' + D3_INLINE + '</script>'` for every chart. Export turns Html into text paragraphs (Oe), and the docx/odt writers have no html item type.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: SPEC result {'type': 'Html'}. Load JS through element$setScripts() rather than inlining it. Use it only for views that need not appear in Word or PDF.
features.risks: Flattened or lost in Word/ODT export and copy. Pj-style inlining adds 280 KB per element toward the 4 MB cap. Html render() removes one .module-asset node from <head> on every render, so prefer inline styles and check that module stylesheets survive re-renders. The same escaping discipline as Svg applies.

features.name: Dropdowns filled from the data beyond the levels of one variable
features.user_gets: Choose several 'positive' levels, or a subset of categories, from a list built from the data.
features.evidence: jmvcore 28.3 OptionList .check rejects values with 'Argument {a} must be one of {options}', so List values are fixed in .a.yaml. Only LevelSelector reads levels, via requestData('column', {properties: ['measureType', 'levels']}). A Supplier with populate: manual can list arbitrary items from an events.js handler.
features.how_in_clinicopathpj: A custom Supplier plus a hidden Array-of-String option, filled by events.js from requestData levels. Python validates the labels.
features.risks: Complex hand-written JS. jmvcore does not validate an Array of String. Hard to test.
